# [New Model][Nvidia] Add SM12x support for DeepSeek V4 Flash with essential fixes

[Upstream PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834) · state: closed · merged: False

## Original PR description

## Summary

This PR enables DeepSeek V4 Flash on SM120/SM121 Blackwell client hardware by carrying the SM12x fallback and tuning stack needed for the current vLLM V1 path. It targets RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, RTX 5090-class SM120, and GB10 / DGX Spark SM121 users who cannot use SM100-only TMEM / `tcgen05` kernels.

The branch is **reconciled on top of the merged #43477** and provides the **stock-deps path**: DeepSeek V4 on SM120/121 that builds and serves on *released* FlashInfer / DeepGEMM wheels, complementing #43477's route that needs the unreleased FlashInfer #3395 + DeepGEMM #324 dependency branches. It is kept **synced onto current `upstream/main`**.

**Latest validated head: tag `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260809` (`aa0d513027`), synced onto `upstream/main` as of 2026-08-09 (`f18e10a7e1`)** — see [Update 2026-08-09](#update-2026-08-09) below. **The default model runner is now V2**; `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` still selects V1, which stays supported.

**Model / speculative-decode status.** `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` is the checkpoint this branch is validated on. It **removed the MTP heads** and folded the DSpark draft into the main checkpoint, so **DSpark (`method: "dspark"`, `num_speculative_tokens: 5`) is the speculative path**; MTP is supported only for older checkpoints that still carry those weights. Running without speculation is also fully supported and validated.

## Change footprint — model kernels vs. core-vLLM touch points

187 files, ~+29.1k / −1.3k against `upstream/main`, of which ~10.7k added lines are tests. The branch splits cleanly into model/kernel code and a small set of core-vLLM integration points:

- **DeepSeek-V4 model + SM12x kernels — the enablement itself.** Everything under `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/**` plus the SM12x sparse-MLA decode / indexer / DeepGEMM kernels that live in shared dirs (`v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_mla_kernels.py`, `model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py`, `v1/attention/backends/mla/{indexer,sparse_swa}.py`, `utils/deep_gemm.py`, `kernels/mhc/tilelang.py`), the new DSv4 reasoning parser / tokenizer, and device tuning JSONs.
- **C128A metadata device→host sync removed** (`models/deepseek_v4/sparse_mla.py`, perf) — `_c128a_effective_topk_width` takes the max position from the CPU-side `CommonAttentionMetadata.max_seq_len` instead of a per-step `int(positions.max().item())` device sync, dropping a launch-stream stall on every C128A metadata step. Decode is identical (`max_seq_len-1 == positions.max()`); only chunked prefill sees a safe, slightly-wider 128-aligned top-k.
- **Core-vLLM integration — the hooks below.** Almost all are gated by model architecture / quant config / an env flag and are inert for other models.

| Subsystem | Files | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| KV-cache core | `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, `kv_cache_coordinator.py`, `kv_cache_manager.py`, `sched/scheduler.py` (+1) | prefix-cache correctness for DSv4 sparse-MLA + speculative decode: an MLA cache-manager with prompt-block protection, a hybrid-coordinator `cache_blocks` tail-block-reuse rewrite |
| Speculative decode | `v1/spec_decode/{dspark,dspark_sampling,llm_base_proposer,dflash}.py`, `config/speculative.py` | DSpark self-drafting proposer + sampling; DSv4 probabilistic draft sampling and per-step draft-layer routing in the shared proposer base; DSpark/MTP method detection and validation |
| MoE quantization | `fused_moe.py`, `oracle/mxfp4.py`, `routed_experts.py`, `experts/flashinfer_cutlass_moe.py`, `quantization/mxfp4.py`, `oracle/nvfp4.py` | MXFP4 / NVFP4 backend selection; the one-line NVFP4 fix (FLASHINFER_CUTLASS into the SwiGLU-clamp allow-list) lets DSv4-Flash-NVFP4 serve |
| FP8 / Marlin GEMM | `quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py`, `linear/scaled_mm/{cutlass,marlin}.py`, `csrc/.../marlin_moe_wna16/ops.cu` (the only C++) | SM12x e8m0→fp32 upcast + Marlin MoE SM12.0a cudagraph hardening |
| cudagraph / compile / config | `config/vllm.py`, `compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py`, `passes/utility/fix_functionalization.py`, `config/compilation.py` | breakable-cudagraph auto-enable gate (MiniMax-only; DSv4 deliberately excluded), DSv4 custom-op defunctionalization + splitting-op registration |
| OpenAI entrypoints / parsers | `chat_completion/protocol.py`, `serve/render/serving.py`, `tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py`, `chat_utils.py`, `engine/protocol.py`, `chat_completion/{serving,batch_serving}.py`, `reasoning/__init__.py` | expose DSv4 API semantics — `reasoning_content` / `thinking` param / tool-call streaming (jasl/vllm#19 instruction-following) |
| Kernel warmup | `model_executor/warmup/deepseek_v4_sm12x_warmup.py` (new), `kernel_warmup.py` (+11) | DSv4 warmup passes (D512-split prefill precompile, paged-MQA rowwise, draft path) that avoid JIT-during-inference wedges. Kept in a separate module so `kernel_warmup.py` stays a two-line hook on upstream's file |
| Weight loading | `weight_utils.py`, `default_loader.py` | fast-safetensors weight filter + EP-skip (lowers DSv4 load overhead on GB10) |
| env / utils | `envs.py`, `utils/flashinfer.py`, `utils/import_utils.py`, `v1/worker/{gpu_model_runner,ubatch_utils}.py` | `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_*` flags + `has_cutedsl` / `has_flashinfer_trtllm_sparse_mla` probes |

Two notes for review:
- The most invasive generic edits were **removed** in the 2026-06-21 audit cleanup: the scheduler carries a single +1-line change (the prefill-fairness heuristics were dropped) and the prefix-cache write-fence is gone.
- A few hooks touch code paths shared with non-DSv4 models and are worth a closer look: the `kv_cache_coordinator` `cache_blocks` rewrite (affects hybrid-KV models; validated ≥ prior behavior), the proposer base-class change, and the OpenAI-entrypoint plumbing. Everything else (MoE oracle, fp8_utils, cudagraph gate, warmup, envs) is arch / quant / env-gated and inert for other models.

## Update 2026-08-02 — `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, 234 upstream commits, two DSpark fixes

Validated head **`9a94c54292`** (tag `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260802`), 234 upstream commits absorbed, level with `upstream/main` as of 2026-08-02.

**What's in it**

- **`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` support.** The new checkpoint ships **no MTP heads** — `enorm`, `hnorm`, `e_proj`, `h_proj` and `shared_head` are absent from the weight index, and `mtp.{0,1,2}.*` now carries the DSpark-style `main_norm` / `main_proj` structure (matching `dspark_target_layer_ids: [40, 41, 42]`). DSpark is the speculative path going forward; the MTP code is retained for older checkpoints.
- **`num_speculative_tokens` vs `dspark_block_size`** — *this rule was relaxed on
  2026-08-04; see Update 2026-08-04. It now errors only BELOW the block size and warns
  above it.* The original reasoning and measurements follow.
- The validator was tightened to require equality. The validator previously accepted `>=` and its error message recommended exceeding it. The drafter emits exactly one block per pass, so the extra slots are structurally unreachable — measured on a prose workload, the **7th draft position accepted 0.000 in every sample** (the 6th in all but one, 0.004 there), and `nst=7` drafts 40% more tokens per step for strictly worse acceptance:

| configuration | mean acceptance length (3 samples) | avg draft acceptance rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nst=5 probabilistic | 2.15 / 2.16 / **2.19** | 22.9 / 23.2 / **23.8%** |
| nst=7 probabilistic | 1.61 / 1.75 / 1.95 | 8.7 / 10.7 / 13.6% |
| nst=5 greedy | 1.82 / 2.06 / **2.23** | 16.4 / 21.2 / **24.5%** |
| nst=7 greedy | 1.57 / 1.66 / 1.75 | 8.2 / 9.5 / 10.8% |

All samples are shown rather than a single figure: the probe reads whatever `SpecDecoding metrics` lines vLLM flushed inside its window, so a low sample means "not much steady traffic in that slice", not a worse drafter. Both `nst=7` runs also hit connection errors partway through, so their spread is noisier.
- **`method: "mtp"` is no longer silently rewritten to `"dspark"`.** Auto-detection preserved an explicitly requested method only for `eagle`/`eagle3`/`dflash`/`dspark`. Since 0731 puts `dspark_block_size` in every DSv4 config, `method: "mtp"` fell through to the dspark branch, was rewritten, and then failed validation with a DSpark message the user never asked for.
- **Absorbed** #49335 (mxfp8 activation-scale swizzle after DP/EP dispatch, verified non-vacuous) and #50686 (consecutive assistant messages merged in prompt encoding — it also removes a spurious mid-turn `<|end_of_sentence|>` on the default `drop_thinking=True` path). #50693's regression test is carried; its code fix is not reachable here.
- **Three community reports re-tested and not reproduced** on this head: nst=7 draft-position collapse, TP=4 + expert-parallel `Check failed: num_tokens > 64`, and `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` missing `tile_sched`. Details in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5152562124).

**Validation (GB10 SM121, 2-node TP=2, `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, torch 2.13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1, nccl 2.30.7)**

| | DSpark nst=5 | no speculation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K 8-shot (flexible) | 0.9394 | 0.9500 |
| GSM8K 8-shot (strict) | 0.9363 | 0.9484 |
| instruction-following (jasl/vllm#19, JSON-only) | PASS | PASS |
| long-context recall (arthur needle, c=1) | 2/2 | 2/2 |
| illegal-access / assertion in serve log | 0 | 0 |
| draft acceptance (prose) | mean 2.08, 21.7% | — |

The GSM8K difference (1.06 pp flexible / 1.21 pp strict) is within this gate's measured single-run spread (~1.1 pp). **Resolved:** three runs per cell were collected and the arms interleave, so it was noise. `0731` is the first checkpoint where the strict and flexible extractors disagree at all; on every prior baseline they were identical.

Perf — pinned llama-benchy standard (fp8 KV, prefix-cache on, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, mml 49152, util 0.85; C=1, 3 runs), against the **full** recorded range of the prior MTP2 baselines. This crosses a checkpoint boundary, so read it as a sanity band rather than a controlled A/B:

| metric | prior MTP2 range (n=10) | 0731 + DSpark | vs band |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pp2048 @ d8192 | 1339.11 – 1400.81 | **1432.23** ± 11.74 | **above** |
| pp2048 @ d16384 | 1308.77 – 1344.68 | **1356.56** ± 11.78 | **above** |
| pp2048 @ d32768 | 1089.05 – 1226.63 | **1250.75** ± 2.18 | **above** |
| ctx_pp @ d8192 | 1757.16 – 1876.01 | 1816.97 ± 5.89 | inside |
| ctx_pp @ d16384 | 1769.85 – 1842.16 | 1817.43 ± 1.43 | inside |
| ctx_pp @ d32768 | 1595.87 – 1756.01 | 1740.22 ± 2.87 | inside |
| tg128 @ d8192 | 36.27 – 43.08 | 41.72 ± 5.09 | inside |
| tg128 @ d16384 | 34.59 – 43.14 | 37.92 ± 9.92 | inside |
| tg128 @ d32768 | 32.77 – 42.91 | 34.88 ± 5.78 | inside |
| ctx_tg @ d8192 | 38.52 – 43.01 | 39.37 ± 2.34 | inside |
| ctx_tg @ d16384 | 39.29 – 43.07 | **35.07** ± 0.67 | **below, −10.7%** |
| ctx_tg @ d32768 | 38.02 – 42.73 | 40.70 ± 6.85 | inside |

**Batched prefill (pp2048) is above the historical band at all three depths** (+2.2% / +0.9% /
+2.0%) — the only consistent directional move here. Clearing the max of ten prior runs at all
three depths says more than any single one of those margins would: +0.9% is inside this metric's
own resolution, so read the consistency rather than the magnitudes. No sign of DSpark being
slower than MTP2 was.

One caveat reported rather than buried: **`ctx_tg @ d16384` sits 10.7% below its historical
minimum**, the only metric outside its band. It is non-monotonic against our own neighbouring
depths (39.37 at d8192, 40.70 at d32768, where history has d16384 ≈ d8192), which points at a
single-run artifact rather than a depth-specific regression. **Resolved:** repeated on later
heads and it did not recur.

A measurement caveat for anyone benchmarking this branch: the `±` in a benchy row is the spread of the three runs *inside one invocation*, and it runs 5–30× smaller than the build-to-build spread. This branch's own history spans 31% on tg128 @ d32768 and ~1.3% on ctx_pp, so anything under ~15% on tg or ~2% on ctx_pp is not resolvable this way.

<a name="update-2026-08-04"></a>
## Update 2026-08-04 — four fixes from community reports, 35 upstream commits, and first SM120 validation

Validated head **`0f59188db1`** (tag `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260804`).

**This is the first head validated on both SM121 and SM120.** Every SM120 discrete-GPU
result on this PR up to now was a contributor's measurement we could not reproduce. We have
since rebuilt a 2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell box as a first-party SM120 target.

### Fixes

- **DSpark's fused Markov sampler could emit an out-of-vocab token id** (`e171c51036`).
  `_dspark_markov_probs_blocks_kernel` stores `vocab_size` as the filler for a block with no
  active lane. On a fully-masked row — every candidate `-inf`, which structured-output
  constraints can produce — *no* block has an active lane, so every block stores the filler and
  the reduce kernel returns it verbatim as the sampled token. Nothing downstream bounded it: the
  runner clamped `input_ids` with `min=0` only, and the DSv4 hash-MoE router indexes
  `tid2eid[token_id * 6 + lane]` on a `[vocab_size, 6]` table. Result is an illegal memory access
  on every TP rank.

  This is the producer on the **V1** path, which is this branch's default. @alexbi29's report
  traced the same class of defect to the V2 samplers (#50843) — a real defect, but a different
  tree. Fixed by folding out-of-range to `0` (matching `torch.argmax` on such a row, so the fused
  kernel stays bit-identical to the eager reference) and making the runner clamp two-sided.

  Worth stating plainly for anyone with similar gates: **our own gates could not have caught
  this**. The fused path is skipped when `all_greedy`, and both our long-context recall gate and
  GSM8K are greedy, so they are structurally incapable of executing that kernel. The new
  regression test is explicitly non-greedy.

- **Adopted #50844** (`3df857ba50`) — bound `token_id` before the `tid2eid` gather. Defence in
  depth; `prompt_token_ids` reach that gather directly when `--skip-tokenizer-init` disables the
  engine's vocab check. **Not** taking #50843 (V2-tree only, inert on our default) or #50845,
  which has a defect reported on its own thread.

- **Eager scratch pool is now OFF by default** (`d42b8d9f55`, `b1ef3033f4`), opt-in via
  `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_EAGER_SCRATCH_POOL=1`. @tobymao bisected output corruption under concurrent
  mixed prefill+decode to it: pool active 7/7 rounds corrupt, disabled 0/2. We first removed the
  cross-template aliasing (`max()` → `sum()` sizing with per-family offsets); **they tested that
  commit directly and it was still corrupt in round 1**. Their diagnosis is the useful part: the
  pre-pool code was race-free *for free* because per-call transients go through the caching
  allocator, whose cross-stream reuse is event-guarded — the pool reuses memory without that
  machinery, so no static partitioning fixes it. Making the cross-layer reuse safe needs
  producer-waits-on-consumer events against the real stream graph; until then, off by default.

- **Two contributor PRs merged** — jasl/vllm#37 (tuned FP8 W8A8 config for `N=4096,K=12288` on
  RTX PRO 6000) and jasl/vllm#38 (hoist the E8M0 block-scale upcast out of the FP8 GEMM hot path,
  13,561 kernel launches removed per 25 decode steps), both from @alexbi29.

- **`num_speculative_tokens` rule relaxed.** Upstream removed its own assertion in #50869 as
  "invalid". They were right that erroring *above* `dspark_block_size` is wrong — two users on
  this thread run `nst=7` against `block_size=5` and it demonstrably works. The two directions are
  not symmetric, so this branch now **errors below** the block size (that genuinely garbles
  output) and **warns above** it, quoting the acceptance cost. Strictly more permissive than what
  shipped before.

### Validation

Full gate battery on **both** architectures, same branch:

| gate | SM121 (2× GB10, 2-node TP=2) | SM120 (2× RTX PRO 6000, TP=2) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| serve, DSpark nst=5, `--block-size 256` | ✅ | ✅ |
| instruction-following (jasl/vllm#19) | PASS | PASS |
| long-context recall, arthur c=1 | 2/2 | 2/2 |
| long-context recall, arthur c=12 | 22, 23, 22 / 24 | 22, 23 / 24 |
| GSM8K 8-shot flexible | 0.9484 / 0.9507 / 0.9492 | 0.9371 |
| GSM8K 8-shot strict | 0.9462 / 0.9477 / 0.9462 | 0.9303 |
| tool-calling, 135 cases | 256/270 (94.8%) | — |
| illegal-access / assertion lines | 0 | 0 |

The ~1.1 pp GSM8K difference between architectures sits inside this gate's measured single-run
spread and spans different silicon, different memory architecture and a 3× smaller KV cache
(6.25 GiB vs ~18.5 GiB). We are not claiming a difference from it.

**`Check failed: num_tokens > 64` does not reproduce on this branch.** @fuzzifikation reported
stock 0.26.0 dying there on SM120 at `--block-size 256`, correctly tracing it to the DSv4 decode
dispatch requiring `page_block_size == 64`. On our SM120 box, at the same `--block-size 256`, the
serve comes up and the assertion never appears — the DSv4 packed KV cache is laid out in 64-token
pages independent of vLLM's logical block size, and FlashInfer derives `page_block_size` from
tensor geometry rather than the engine config. The SM120 packed decode path is confirmed engaged
in the same run. Note the same assertion has **two** distinct gates (`page_block_size` and
`(num_heads, topk)`, the latter being #50720 / flashinfer#3989), so patching one and still seeing
it means checking the other.

### Prefill: V1 vs V2 model runner

The 2026-08-02 V1-vs-V2 comparison never measured throughput. It has now been measured, blocked
and pre-registered — 10 blocks, both arms inside each node pair, exact sign-flip permutation test,
Holm-corrected across the six prefill cells, with the decision rule committed before any data was
collected:

| metric | V2 / V1 | 95% CI | exact p |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ctx_pp @ d8192 | **+1.18%** | [+0.82, +1.53] | 0.0020 |
| ctx_pp @ d16384 | **+1.11%** | [+0.35, +1.87] | 0.0137 |
| ctx_pp @ d32768 | **+1.61%** | [+1.17, +2.04] | 0.0020 |
| pp2048 @ d8192 | **+4.18%** | [+3.28, +5.09] | 0.0020 |
| pp2048 @ d16384 | **+4.18%** | [+3.36, +5.00] | 0.0020 |
| pp2048 @ d32768 | **+4.33%** | [+3.56, +5.11] | 0.0020 |

All six survive Holm; both node pairs agree in direction on every cell. **Decode is not resolved
in either direction** — `tg128` was declared unresolvable before the run (its within-build spread
equals its entire historical range) and is reported for the record only.

**V1 was the default when this was written; that was reversed on 2026-08-09 — see Update 2026-08-09.** The reasoning below was correct on the evidence available at the time, and the collapse it describes was real; it turned out not to be a property of the runner. Kept unedited because how the conclusion failed is the useful part. V2 is ahead on prefill, KV headroom (+4.70 GiB) and draft acceptance
(+6.6%), but its long-context recall under concurrency is unreliable in a way that is worse than a
consistent deficit: across 14 independent serves on the same build and configuration, roughly two
thirds land in a state that loses most of the needles (arthur c=12 as low as 3/24), while the rest
match V1 at 22–24/24. The mode is fixed at startup and stable within a serve, and nothing we have
found predicts or detects it. A deployment could run clean for days and restart into the bad mode.

The cause is **not identified**. Eliminated so far: the eager-scratch cross-template aliasing, the
upstream merges, and the eager scratch pool as a whole (pool on 2 good / 6 bad vs pool off 3 good /
3 bad over 14 serves — no effect). The startup logs of a good and a bad serve are structurally
identical, which rules out "a different code path was taken". Anyone opting into V2 with
`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` should know this.

### Measurement note

Two errors from our own process, since they affect how the numbers above should be read.

The n=8 sampling that originally established V2's recall deficit took eight gate runs from **one
serve** — it measured within-serve variance while the quantity that actually varies is
across-serve. Raising n on the wrong axis. The 14-serve figures above use the inverted design:
many serves, few gates each.

And the `±` in a benchy row is the spread *within one invocation*; it runs 5–30× smaller than the
build-to-build spread. The blocked design above exists because of that: a coarse range screen over
the same 10 blocks returns "no measurable difference" on all six prefill cells, while the paired
test finds all six. Had the screen been the decisive statistic, this section would have concluded
the opposite and been wrong.

## Update 2026-08-09 — the V2 recall collapse was a prefix-cache race, not the runner; V2 becomes the default

70 upstream commits (to `643c125fab`), and the long-standing reason this branch
pinned V1 is gone: it was **an unfixed upstream bug**, not a property of the V2
model runner.

### The defect

`FullAttentionManager.cache_blocks()` commits prefix block hashes to the shared
`BlockPool` **at scheduling time, before the forward pass writes their KV**. A
request admitted later in the same step can match those hashes and read unwritten
values. `MambaManager` has guarded this since #29387; no other manager does.

This is **vllm-project/vllm#42359**, open and unmerged. Two more reports look
like the same triple on different models — **#50188** (prefix caching + MTP spec
decode + fp8 KV, byte-identical repeat requests, RTX 5090 / Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4)
and **#43559** (closed without a merged fix). Anyone on `--enable-prefix-caching`
with speculative decoding is exposed; DeepSeek-V4 is not special here.

What makes it hard to catch: **the damage persists**. A serve that loses the race
keeps serving from the poisoned blocks for its lifetime, so a later *serial*
request fails too — which is why it looked like a per-serve "mode" rather than a
race. It is also stochastic, roughly half of cold serves.

### Evidence

Same binary, `VLLM_ALLOW_SPEC_DEC_SAME_STEP_PREFIX_HIT` the only variable, cache
populated by the real gate, **4 fresh serves per arm** (a single clean serve
proves nothing at ~50% incidence), 3 arthur c=12 runs each:

| | serve 1 | serve 2 | serve 3 | serve 4 | mean | min |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| guard **off** | 22/23/24 | **6/5/3** | **14/9/10** | **7/8/7** | 11.5 | 3 |
| guard **on** | 23/22/21 | 20/22/20 | 22/23/23 | 23/22/23 | 22.0 | 20 |

Mann-Whitney U, p = 0.0043. Every serve's runner and guard state was read back
from the serve log rather than assumed.

**It also fixes V1**, which was not expected: V1's arthur c=12 goes 20.7 → 23.0
with the guard on (24.0 with prefix caching disabled entirely). V1's own 2–4
needle shortfall was the same defect, not an inherent concurrency margin.

### Runner arbitration, re-run on the fixed tree

Same tree, same guard mode, **runner the only variable**:

| | V1 | V2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| arthur c=12, 4 serves × 3 | 22.3 / 21.7 / 21.7 / 21.0 → **21.67** | 22.0 / 20.7 / 22.7 / 22.7 → **22.00** |
| pp2048 d8192 / 16384 / 32768 | 1427 / 1363 / 1216 | **1472 / 1421 / 1303** (+3.1% / +4.2% / +7.1%) |
| tg128 mean | 39.95 / 41.16 / 35.25 | **41.56 / 49.61 / 45.18** |
| e2e TTFT | 1437 / 1506 / 1689 ms | **1393 / 1444 / 1576 ms** |
| GPU KV cache | 339,194 tok | **423,752 tok** (+24.9%) |
| GSM8K strict / flexible | 0.9378 / 0.9401 | 0.9401 / 0.9439 |
| issue19 · multi-needle · c=1 | PASS · 48/48, 0 leaks · 2/2 | PASS · 48/48, 0 leaks · 2/2 |

Recall: p = 0.697, neither side with a single-digit serve. GSM8K differs by
<0.4 pp against ~1.1 pp single-run noise. **V2 is not behind anywhere and leads
on throughput, latency and KV headroom, so it becomes the default.**
`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` still selects V1, which stays supported.

**Correction:** the *"V2 +6.6% draft acceptance"* figure in Update 2026-08-04
does **not** survive re-measurement — 2.772 (V1) vs 2.710 (V2) on the same
formula and sample size, i.e. a tie. It was measured while V2 was poisoned.

### If you are running this branch

**Nothing to set — the guard is on by default where it matters.**
`KVCacheCoordinator` enables it whenever prefix caching and speculative decoding
are both active, which is the only configuration in which a block hash can be
published before its KV is written *and* a second request admitted in the same
step to match it.

This correction matters: an earlier revision of this update shipped V2 as the
default while leaving the guard off by default, which would have handed a plain
serve the exact combination measured at mean 11.5 with a 3/24 floor. Both
changes looked like improvements in isolation. If you pulled `c054feedac`,
take `aa0d513027` instead, or set the variable yourself.

To turn it **off** (it is a real escape hatch, pinned by a test):

```bash
VLLM_ALLOW_SPEC_DEC_SAME_STEP_PREFIX_HIT=0
```

`1` is upstream's semantics, gated on `use_eagle`; on DeepSeek-V4 that covers
only **2 of 5** managers and leaves the main MLA path unguarded — measured, not
assumed, via a startup log line this branch adds that reports how many managers
are actually guarded. `2` covers every group and is what the engine selects.

Regression sweep on the merged tree: 261 passed, 1 failed, that one failing
identically on the pre-merge tree `4ebd1fb698`.

### The two endpoints disagreed about the same model, twice

`ResponsesRequest.reasoning` took its type from the OpenAI SDK, whose
`ReasoningEffort` stops at `xhigh`, so DeepSeek's documented top tier `max` was
rejected by schema validation on `/v1/responses` while `/v1/chat/completions`
accepted it.

Worse, and on the default path: with no thinking kwarg,
`DeepSeekV4Tokenizer.apply_chat_template` defaults thinking **on** while
`DeepSeekV4ReasoningParser` defaults it **off** and selects
`IdentityReasoningParser`. The model reasoned and its reasoning, with a bare
`</think>`, came back inside `output_text` as though it were the answer —
whenever a request omitted `reasoning`, which is exactly what a stock OpenAI
SDK sends. Chat was immune only because it normalises thinking state at the
protocol boundary, and its own docstring says why: *"so the tokenizer and
reasoning parser see the same effective state"*. Responses never called that
hook. The derivation now lives in `deepseek_v4_chat_kwargs` and both request
types call it, so a third endpoint cannot repeat it.

Measured on both checkpoints with no workaround flag set, 21/21 each:

| | `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` | `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| silence: reasoning in its own field | PASS | PASS |
| silence: no `</think>` in the answer | PASS | PASS |
| `effort: none` disables thinking | PASS | PASS |
| six spellings × two endpoints | PASS | PASS |
| `high` reasons deeper than `low` | +85% / +110% | +19% / +35% |

26 unit cases accompany it, 11 of which fail on the unpatched tree.
`tests/reasoning` 440 passed, `tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py` 45 passed.

### Acceptance on the exact published SHA

Everything above was re-measured on `d44e224ab9` — the commit this tag points at,
after a second upstream sync (17 further commits, FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3) — not
on an ancestor assumed to be equivalent. 17 of 18 checks pass:

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| four nodes clean at the SHA, FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3 | PASS |
| `tests/v1/core` | 509 passed, 1 pre-existing failure |
| default serve with **nothing set**: boots, runner V2, guard 5/5, no NameError | PASS |
| arthur c=12 ×3 / c=1 | 22 / 20 / 23 · 2/2 |
| GSM8K strict · issue19 · multi-needle | 0.9363 · PASS · 48/48, 0 leaks |
| pp2048 d8192 | 1480.77 (arbitration V2 arm 1471.8) |
| `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` → V1, guard still 5/5, c=1 2/2 | PASS |
| `VLLM_ALLOW_SPEC_DEC_SAME_STEP_PREFIX_HIT=0` → guard 0/5, c=1 2/2 | PASS |

**The one non-pass, and what it turned out to be.** `tests/v1/spec_decode` does
not complete on this hardware — it wedges under a 30-minute bound on this head
and on `4ebd1fb698` alike. Narrowed to `test_max_len.py` and measured both ways:

| how it is run | result |
| --- | --- |
| whole file, one pytest process | wedges after ~7 min, 5 of 11 done |
| each case in its own process | **11 of 11 pass**, free memory steady at 117 GiB |

No individual case is broken. Each stands up a full engine, and repeated
create/tear-down inside one process does not release resources fast enough on a
**single-GPU** unified-memory node. That also explains why both trees wedge and
why they stop at different points. It remains **unverified coverage rather than a
pass**; running one process per case produces a verdict instead of a hang.

`test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders` is the
same class: it builds `pipeline_parallel_size=2`, and a GB10 node has one GPU, so
it fails at config construction. It is the only case in `tests/v1/core` that needs
more than one GPU; the other 509 pass.

### What this arbitration does and does not cover

Everything above was measured on **one configuration**: 2-node TP=2,
`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, DSpark `num_speculative_tokens: 5`, fp8 KV,
`max_model_len` 131072, prefix caching on, GB10 (SM121). The default now applies
to **every** DSpark config, including shapes not measured here — TP=4, other
context lengths, the NVFP4 checkpoint, single-node setups.

The reasoning generalises better than the numbers do: the race is in block
publication and is not specific to a model shape, and V2's advantage comes from
KV headroom and scheduling rather than anything config-specific. But if you run
a materially different shape and see something worse, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`
returns you to V1 and a report would be welcome — that is a gap in our coverage,
not a claim we have ruled out.

## Running DSpark

DSpark is DeepSeek's self-drafting speculative-decode variant; on `0731` the draft weights are carried in the main checkpoint, so no separate `--speculative-model` is needed.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --max-model-len 49152 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
```

- `num_speculative_tokens` **must equal** the checkpoint's `dspark_block_size` (5). Larger values are rejected: they are never accepted and only waste draft compute.
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` is mandatory — DSv4's `fp8_ds_mla` attention asserts an fp8 KV layout, so the default `auto` fails at model construction. Not DSpark-specific.
- Runs on the **V1 runner by default** (correct long-context recall). `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` opts into the V2 DSpark speculator; V2's long-context recall is correct after the jasl/vllm#26 padded-Q fix.
- If you measure draft acceptance yourself, **use prose**. On counting or repeated text the Markov head alone reaches 68–100% acceptance even with the neural draft path degraded, which hides real regressions entirely.

## Dependencies (stock-deps path)

Pins on the current head: torch 2.13.0 (triton 3.7.1) · `flashinfer-python` / `flashinfer-cubin` 0.6.15.post1 · tilelang 0.1.12 · `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]` 4.6.0 · `quack-kernels>=0.6.1` · nvidia-nccl-cu13 2.30.7 (multi-node, see below).

- **FlashInfer** is pinned in `requirements/cuda.txt` (`flashinfer-python` **and** the GitHub-release `flashinfer-cubin`, which must be the same version); it ships the SM120 packed sparse-MLA kernels, so a stock build picks them up with no manual install dance.
- **GB10 / multi-node**: pin `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7` on every node. A rebuild silently reverts it to torch's bundled version, and a per-node mismatch hangs the NCCL handshake.
- The SM120 **decode** (`VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE`) and **prefill** (`VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL`) FlashInfer sparse-MLA paths **default on**; set either `=0` to fall back to the FlashMLA / Triton path. Both are availability-gated, so stock installs without the kernel degrade gracefully rather than raising.

## Running the NVFP4 checkpoint

This branch also serves `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4` on SM12x (RTX PRO 6000 / GB10). The NVFP4 MoE auto-selects the FlashInfer CUTLASS backend (the SwiGLU-clamp model gate accepts it), so no `--moe-backend` flag and no special FlashInfer build are required:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4
```

Expert-parallel off (plain TP) is the supported path. Accuracy matches MXFP4 (GSM8K 8-shot ~0.96 on both SM120 and SM121). On SM12x NVFP4 is **not** a memory or throughput win versus MXFP4: NVFP4 weights are ~4 GiB/GPU larger, leaving less KV-cache room; single-stream prefill is marginally faster and aggregate decode marginally slower. Its value here is checkpoint availability / parity with the SM100 datacenter path — MXFP4 remains the better practical choice on consumer Blackwell.

The branch was validated through human review plus the commands and harness artifacts listed above; every performance and accuracy number quoted was measured on real SM120/SM121 hardware.

- zorrofox · comment · 2026-05-13T07:23:58Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4438388452)

Tested on **GCP G4 `g4-standard-96`** (2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell **Server Edition**, SM120, driver 580.126.20, compute_cap 12.0).

**Non-MTP works** (TP=2, eager=off, cc=1 → 76.6 tok/s). With `--speculative-config '{"method":"deepseek_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'` (or N=1), serve crashes during MTP warmup with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`.

`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` traceback (commit `dda4668b`, py3.12, cutlass-dsl 4.5.0):
```
kernel_warmup.py:411 _deepseek_v4_sparse_mla_attention_warmup
→ gpu_model_runner.py:5720 _dummy_run
→ deepseek_v4_attention.py:1557 _forward_prefill
→ cache_utils.py:371 dequantize_and_gather_k_cache
→ dequant_gather_k_cutedsl.py:29 DequantGatherKCacheKernel.compile
→ tvm_ffi → cudaErrorIllegalAddress
```
Forcing the Triton fallback (`dequantize_and_gather_k_cache_triton`) crashes at the same callsite:
```
cache_utils.py:330 _dequantize_and_gather_k_kernel[(num_reqs, NUM_WORKERS)]
→ Triton Error [CUDA]: illegal memory access
```
So both kernel impls fail under the MTP warmup prefill shape — looks like the dummy `block_table`/`seq_lens` indexes out of bounds rather than a kernel codegen issue.

Environment aligned per `vllm-ds4-sm120-harness/HANDOFF.md`:
- `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0a` (runtime; build-time `12.0a` fails nvcc on CUDA 12.8 → using `12.0` for build)
- `CUDA_ARCH_LIST=120a`, `TRITON_PTXAS_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas`, `unset PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF`
- `use_fp4_indexer_cache=False` (default)
- Base: `nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu24.04`, torch 2.11.0+cu128

Serve flags: `--tp 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.96 --max-model-len 4096 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4` + `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`.

Since the PR body shows MTP=2 working on Workstation Edition (148.9 tok/s), could you share the exact `vllm serve` command + any additional env (e.g. `--max-num-seqs`, `--cuda-graph-max-bs`, CUDA toolkit version) used for the RTX PRO 6000 numbers? Happy to retest with full alignment.

- jasl · comment · 2026-05-13T22:47:21Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4445778499)

Hi @arthur-drozdov — this looks different from the SIGKILL-induced stuck-RPC I documented earlier. Two things would narrow it down a lot:

**1. `py-spy` dump on each rank while stuck:**
```bash
for pid in $(pgrep -f "vllm.*EngineCore|Worker_TP"); do
  echo "=== $pid ==="; py-spy dump --pid $pid --nonblocking
done
```
Key question: are both ranks blocked in `ncclAllReduce` / `pynccl_comm.all_reduce`, or is one in scheduler / cudagraph replay while the other is in NCCL? Asymmetric → scheduler bug; symmetric → collective hang.

**2. Quick 4-run bisection** (each run reproduces or doesn't, ~minutes):
- **A.** `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE","custom_ops":["all"]}'` — isolates cudagraph replay
- **B.** `--no-enable-prefix-caching` — isolates prefix-cache / indexer interaction (your 88.7% hit rate at the moment of stall is suspicious)
- **C.** drop `--speculative-config` — isolates MTP draft loop (your `drafts` counter is also frozen, so I doubt it, but cheap to check)
- **D.** `--max-model-len 100000 --max-num-seqs 8` — same total KV budget but flips the lopsided seqs=2 corner

The combo you're using (`max_model_len=200000 + max_num_seqs=2`) is much more KV-lopsided than the deploy recipes I've been validating (`max_model_len=32–65K, max_num_seqs=16–36`, post-`dda4668b5` canon 4-cell is clean on the same hardware). That's the axis I'd suspect first.

Happy to repro on my GB10 cluster with your exact flags tomorrow if it helps confirm it's config-shape rather than image-build specific.

- aabbccddwasd · comment · 2026-05-14T13:04:02Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4450901180)

@jasl I've been running a fork based on this PR on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), TP=4, with several additional performance optimizations. Sharing the ones that had measurable throughput impact — feel free to pick any that are useful.

## Performance-validated optimizations (DSv4-Flash on SM120)

### 1. Triton autotune on sparse MLA prefill accumulate kernels
**File:** `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_mla_kernels.py`

Added `@triton.autotune (num_warps={4,8}, num_stages={2,3}, key=["num_candidates"])` to 5 prefill hot-path kernels:
- `_accumulate_indexed_attention_chunk_kernel`
- `_accumulate_fp8ds_global_slots_attention_chunk_kernel`
- `_accumulate_fp8ds_global_slots_attention_chunk_multihead_kernel`
- `_accumulate_fp8ds_paged_attention_chunk_kernel`
- `_accumulate_fp8ds_paged_attention_chunk_multihead_kernel`

The multihead kernel additionally needs `num_tokens: tl.constexpr` + `reset_to_zero=["num_tokens"]` for autotune correctness. Remove hardcoded `num_warps=8` from all 5 call sites (autotune supplies it).

**Impact:** +39% prefill (2,575 → 3,585 tok/s on the earlier prototype; the PR base already has better baseline so the absolute gain is smaller, but still material).

### 2. C128A metadata loop cap + effective_topk
**File:** `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py`

Two changes in `_build_c128a_topk_metadata_kernel`:
- Change decode/prefill inner-loop range from `max_compressed_tokens` → per-token `num_compressed` (already computed but was unused as loop bound — the mask already guarded correctness, but launching ~97% dead iterations for short contexts is pure waste)
- Expose `c128a_decode_effective_topk` and `c128a_prefill_effective_topk` in `FlashMLASparseMetadata` so `deepseek_v4_attention.py` can truncate `topk_indices` downstream

**Impact:** eliminates the ~23% prefill regression observed with 1M `max_model_len` vs 32K when processing 2K-token inputs. 1M config prefill matches 32K config within noise.

### 3. C128A prefill topk index truncation
**File:** `vllm/model_executor/layers/deepseek_v4_attention.py`

Truncate `attn_metadata.c128a_prefill_topk_indices` via `c128a_prefill_effective_topk` so sparse MLA accumulate kernels never iterate over padding entries (all -1).

```python
if attn_metadata.c128a_prefill_effective_topk is not None:
    topk_indices = topk_indices[:, :attn_metadata.c128a_prefill_effective_topk]
```

### 4. seq_lens contiguity fix
**File:** `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py`

One-liner: `seq_lens = decode_metadata.seq_lens[:batch_size].contiguous()`

Without this, `persistent_topk` crashes during CUDA graph capture under V2 model runner when `max_decode_len < next_n` produces a non-contiguous 2D slice. Contiguous `.contiguous()` is a no-op on already-contiguous tensors.

### 5. Triton autotune on fp8_einsum + fused_indexer_q
**Files:** `vllm/v1/attention/ops/deepseek_v4_ops/fp8_einsum.py`, `fused_indexer_q.py`

Added `@triton.autotune` to `_deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum_kernel` and `_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant_kernel`. The fp8_einsum kernel was hardcoded to `num_warps=4`; autotune selects among `{4,8}` per shape.

### 6. 3 additional FP8 W8A8 Block tuned configs
**Files:** 3 new JSON configs under `configs/` for shapes:
- N=4096,K=2048 (q_b/gate projection)
- N=1024,K=4096 (wq_b projection)  
- N=4096,K=512 (wo_b projection)

These complement the 6 shapes already in this PR. Config lookup is device-name-based so no code changes needed.

### Verified throughput (4× RTX PRO 6000, TP=4, 32K ctx, ~2K input, bench_dsv4)
| Config | Prefill | Decode NT | Decode T |
|--------|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Baseline (no MTP) | 4,565 tok/s | 101 tok/s | 101 tok/s |
| MTP N=3 | 4,485 tok/s | 200 tok/s (mean) | 191 tok/s (mean) |

Baseline matches the reference; MTP=3 delivers ~2× decode uplift. All 9 FP8 config shapes load without warnings.

---
*Posted by deepseek-v4-pro*

 def _deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum_kernel(
```

- aabbccddwasd · comment · 2026-05-16T05:43:39Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4465878266)

**Prefill performance optimization report — SM120 DSv4**

Testing on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), TP=4, 1M max_model_len, chunked prefill 512 tok/step, -O3.

Full implementation and benchmark methodology on:
- Branch: https://github.com/aabbccddwasd/vllm/tree/dsv4-sm120-opt-v2
- Commit: `6ff395e0f` (multi-head kernel + gather overlap, on top of PR's 18 commits)
- Analysis doc: `~/AI-stuffs/dsv4-prefill-l2-cache-optimization.md`

Cherry-pick friendly — both optimizations are cleanly separable. Happy to split into individual PRs if there's interest.

---

## 1. Multi-head prefill accumulate kernel (HEAD_BLOCK=4)

**Observation**: The prefill accumulate kernel (`_accumulate_indexed_attention_chunk_kernel`) uses a single-head grid `(num_tokens, num_heads)` — each thread block handles 1 Q head. Every KV row loaded from L2 is used for only one dot product, then re-loaded independently by every other head. The decode path already has `_multihead_kernel` (HEAD_BLOCK=4) that reuses each KV row across 4 heads.

**Fix**: Added `_accumulate_indexed_attention_chunk_multihead_kernel` in `sparse_mla_kernels.py` (~190 LOC), applying the same multi-head pattern to the prefill indexed variant:

- Grid: `(num_tokens, ceil(num_heads / HEAD_BLOCK))` with HEAD_BLOCK=4
- Each block loads HEAD_BLOCK Q vectors, then for each KV candidate loads the KV row once and dots with all HEAD_BLOCK heads (vectorized online softmax)
- Autotune key=`num_candidates`, configs: num_warps={4,8}, num_stages={2,3}

|  | 64K | 128K |
|---|-----|------|
| Baseline | 2,792 tok/s | 1,466 tok/s |
| Multi-head | 3,099 tok/s (+11.0%) | 1,629 tok/s (+11.1%) |

## 2. Overlap KV gather with indexer on aux stream

**Observation**: After the multi-head fix, accumulate is no longer the dominant bottleneck. KV gather (dequantize_and_gather_k_cache) becomes the largest remaining phase in eager attention (~47% of step time). The gather reads from paged KV cache and writes to workspace — memory-bound, but only 1 thread block per request so its bandwidth footprint is tiny.

**Fix**: Moved the KV gather from eager attention into the Pre-Attention CUDA Graph segment, launching it on `aux_stream_list[1]` to overlap with the indexer on `aux_stream_list[0]`. The gather workspace is pre-allocated during warmup and passed to `_forward_prefill` via the workspace manager. Both aux streams are joined before the graph boundary — CUDA-graph-safe. Cross-boundary event passing follows the offloader pattern (`prefetch.py:243-253`).

|  | 128K |
|---|------|
| Multi-head only | 1,629 tok/s |
| Multi-head + gather overlap | 1,712 tok/s (+5.1%) |
| **Total vs baseline** | **+16.8%** |

**Important**: The gather overlap was attempted standalone first and showed zero gain — because accumulate dominated the critical path. Only makes sense after the multi-head kernel reduces accumulate cost. Optimization order matters.

— deepseek-v4-pro

@aabbccddwasd super cool, thank you for sharing! i quickly implemented #1 (multi-head prefill accumulate) with the help of claude since your branch isn't accessible — here are my results on 2× RTX PRO 6000 WS Edition, TP=2, MTP=2, 524K max_model_len:

| Tokens | Baseline (single-head) | Multi-head (HEAD_BLOCK=8) | Δ |
|--------|------------------------|---------------------------|---|
| 1,036 | 2,746 tok/s (0.377s) | 4,100 tok/s (0.252s) | **+49%** |
| 4,491 | 3,122 tok/s (1.439s) | 4,271 tok/s (1.052s) | **+37%** |
| 17,891 | 2,474 tok/s (7.231s) | 3,360 tok/s (5.324s) | **+36%** |
| 63,543 | 1,679 tok/s (37.8s) | 2,146 tok/s (29.6s) | **+28%** |

bigger gain than your +11% — probably because TP=2 means 64 heads/rank vs your TP=4 with 32, so the L2 KV reuse has more leverage.

tuned HEAD_BLOCK and num_warps:

| Config | 1K | 4.5K | 18K | 64K |
|--------|-----|------|-----|-----|
| HB=4, warps=8 | 3,810 | 4,018 | 3,112 | 2,025 |
| HB=4, warps=4 | 2,862 | 4,013 | 3,317 | 2,139 |
| **HB=8, warps=4** | **4,100** | **4,271** | **3,360** | **2,146** |
| HB=8, warps=8 | 4,097 | 3,657 | 3,269 | 2,104 |

HEAD_BLOCK=8 with num_warps=4 wins at all sizes. implementation is the same pattern as the existing decode `_finish_materialized_scores_with_sink_kernel`: load KV once per candidate, broadcast dot across HEAD_BLOCK heads. ~100 LOC kernel + dispatcher change in `accumulate_indexed_sparse_mla_attention_chunk`.

> 
> Tokens	Baseline (single-head)	Multi-head (HEAD_BLOCK=4)	Δ
> 1,036	2,746 tok/s (0.377s)	3,810 tok/s (0.272s)	**+39%**
> 4,491	3,122 tok/s (1.439s)	4,018 tok/s (1.118s)	**+29%**
> 17,891	2,474 tok/s (7.231s)	3,112 tok/s (5.748s)	**+26%**
> 63,543	1,679 tok/s (37.8s)	2,025 tok/s (31.4s)	**+21%**
> bigger gain than your +11% — probably because TP=2 means 64 heads/rank vs your TP=4 with 32, so the L2 KV reuse has more leverage.
> 
> implementation is straightforward — new `_accumulate_indexed_attention_chunk_multihead_kernel` with the same pattern as the existing decode `_finish_materialized_scores_with_sink_kernel`: load KV once per candidate, broadcast dot across HEAD_BLOCK heads. ~100 LOC kernel + dispatcher change in `accumulate_indexed_sparse_mla_attention_chunk`.

Thanks for testing this out! Really impressive results — +39% at 1K tokens and still +21% at 63K is way better than what I saw on TP=4. Your explanation makes sense: at TP=2 you have 64 heads/rank vs 32 on TP=4, so the HEAD\_BLOCK=4 KV reuse gets roughly 2× more leverage. That's a great insight.

By the way, sorry about the branch — it was never pushed to GitHub (just sitting on my local machine). It's up now at https://github.com/aabbccddwasd/vllm/tree/dsv4-sm120-opt-v2.

- dowhirly · comment · 2026-05-19T01:04:02Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4483558472)

## SM12x CUTLASS DSL ImportError

**Env:** RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM 12.0), CUDA 13.0, Docker build

Container crashes during warmup:
```
ImportError: cannot import name 'normalize_field_to_ir_name' from 'cutlass.cute.nvgpu.common'
```

**Root cause:** `has_cutedsl()` uses `importlib.util.find_spec("cutlass")` which only checks package metadata, not whether it actually imports. On SM12x, `nvidia_cutlass_dsl` is installed but `import cutlass` fails because `tcgen05` (SM10x datacenter-only) is loaded unconditionally.

**Fix:** Make `has_cutedsl()` attempt the real import so it returns `False` on SM12x, falling back to Triton:

```python
@cache
def has_cutedsl() -> bool:
    """Whether the optional `cutlass` package is available and importable."""
    try:
        import cutlass  # noqa: F401
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False
```

**Verified:** Container starts and serves normally on 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q with MTP speculative decoding (acceptance rate ~79%).

- jasl · comment · 2026-05-19T12:31:47Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4487738899)

> ## SM12x CUTLASS DSL ImportError
> **Env:** RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM 12.0), CUDA 13.0, Docker build
> 
> Container crashes during warmup:
> 
> ```
> ImportError: cannot import name 'normalize_field_to_ir_name' from 'cutlass.cute.nvgpu.common'
> ```
> 
> **Root cause:** `has_cutedsl()` uses `importlib.util.find_spec("cutlass")` which only checks package metadata, not whether it actually imports. On SM12x, `nvidia_cutlass_dsl` is installed but `import cutlass` fails because `tcgen05` (SM10x datacenter-only) is loaded unconditionally.
> 
> **Fix:** Make `has_cutedsl()` attempt the real import so it returns `False` on SM12x, falling back to Triton:
> 
> ```python
> @cache
> def has_cutedsl() -> bool:
>     """Whether the optional `cutlass` package is available and importable."""
>     try:
>         import cutlass  # noqa: F401
>         return True
>     except Exception:
>         return False
> ```
> 
> **Verified:** Container starts and serves normally on 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q with MTP speculative decoding (acceptance rate ~79%).

Fixed, please retry

- sonny-vleisides · comment · 2026-05-20T02:10:07Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4493888739)

A few iteration notes from 2× RTX PRO 6000, TP=2 MTP=1...

The MTP small-batch graph hangs fix iteration checks out cleanly. `3424fba5` regressed cold-cache TTFT about 5x vs c37f7357, `95774eab` fixed it, `662b0773` (the simplification) kept the fix. So the gpu_model_runner/worker changes from 95774eab weren't load-bearing for the cold-cache path. Concurrent prefix-cache hit-rate stable around 55.7% multi-trial across all three builds (5 trials each).

`edc82b61` (row-tile widening BLOCK_M 16→64) is the one that broke for me. Multi-session concurrent stress destabilizes V4. Repro: 2 sessions × 3 turns × ~800 filler word concurrent, 5 trials back-to-back. First request returns fine (Canberra smoke OK), then trial 1 shows the prefix-cache counter resetting from 26880 to 0 mid-trial (container restarted mid-test), and trials 2-5 all return `Server disconnected` / `Connection reset by peer`. Container ends up restart-looping. Reverting to `662b0773` and V4 cold-loads clean.

No stack trace, worker died silently from systemd's view. Could be BLOCK_M=64 interacting badly with concurrent KV pressure under MTP=1 but that's a guess. Have the multi-trial JSON if useful.

(APIServer pid=1) INFO 05-21 13:10:54 [loggers.py:271] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 137.9 tokens/s, Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs

**Multi-session long-context throughput collapse (~2-3 tok/s).** This issue has persisted since the early versions of this PR:
```
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 05-21 13:19:34 [loggers.py:271] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 2.0 tokens/s, Running: 4 reqs, Waiting: 3 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 21.7%, Prefix cache hit rate: 78.1%
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 05-21 13:19:34 [metrics.py:101] SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 2.22, Accepted throughput: 1.10 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 1.80 tokens/s
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 05-21 13:19:44 [loggers.py:271] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 5615.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 2.3 tokens/s, Running: 5 reqs, Waiting: 2 reqs
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 05-21 13:20:04 [loggers.py:271] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 2.8 tok/s, Running: 6 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs
```

**Not related to KV cache capacity** — after the collapse, letting all multi-session requests drain and serving a single request again immediately restores normal throughput (~135-140 tok/s), even at 40% KV cache usage:
```
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 05-21 14:27:33 [metrics.py:101] SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 2.44, Accepted throughput: 0.63 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 0.87 tokens/s
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 05-21 14:27:43 [loggers.py:271] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 139.8 tokens/s, Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 40.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 48.8%
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 05-21 14:27:43 [metrics.py:101] SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 2.72, Accepted throughput: 88.39 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 102.78 tokens/s, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.988, 0.732, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 86.0%
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 05-21 14:28:03 [loggers.py:271] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 134.4 tokens/s, Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 40.1%, Prefix cache hit rate: 48.8%
```

**Summary:**
- Prefix cache hit rate is ~76-78% (healthy), prefill is fast at 5615 tok/s (healthy) — the bottleneck is purely in the decode stage
- KV cache is far from full (21-40%), capacity is not the cause
- Does NOT reproduce with `--enforce-eager` but very slow 3~16 tok/s
- Not reported on TP=2 by other testers — this appears to be a TP=4 scaling issue that TP=2 validation cannot cover
- Likely a CUDA graph + NCCL multi-stream synchronization interaction problem specific to TP=4 or above

| exact_match_strict | 0.94 |

### User-reported short-prefill regression

The `BLOCK_M=16 -> 64` regression reported above was real for short prefill. I changed the SM120 FP8 MQA logits tile choice to be length-aware: short prefill uses `BLOCK_M=16`, longer contexts keep the larger tile.

On my 2x RTX PRO 6000 proxy sweep, this recovered the short-prefill case without giving up the long-context path:

| Case | Before adaptive tile | After adaptive tile | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1K input tok/s | 3385 | 5152 | +52.2% |
| 4K input tok/s | 6159 | 6091 | -1.1% |
| 16K input tok/s | 5516 | 5565 | +0.9% |
| 64K input tok/s | 4599 | 4561 | -0.8% |

### Mixed long/short workload status

The current branch includes a conservative scheduler-side best-effort improvement so a large prefill chunk does not monopolize the step when decode work or queued requests are present.

This helps the case where a request is already decoding and another long prefill arrives. In my local mixed-arrival gate, the existing long decode path had much better tail spacing after the scheduler change:

- primary elapsed: `26.55s -> 21.59s`
- primary p99 inter-chunk gap: `1.94s -> 0.63s`
- decode throughput mean: `65.5 -> 74.2 tok/s`

However, this does **not** fully solve all mixed workload shapes. If a short request arrives behind an already-running ~124K prefill, the short request can still wait roughly one long-prefill TTFT window in a single vLLM instance. So for TP=4, 512K/1M, or strict multi-user SLA, I still consider this a remaining area for proper 4-card validation and possibly prefill/decode separation or request-class admission control.

### Remaining caveats

- I can only validate up to ~131K on my current 2-card setup. The 256K / 512K / 1M cases still need a 4-card gate before making customer-facing commitments.
- The TP=4 multi-session decode-collapse report above is not reproducible on my TP=2 machine and should be treated as not covered by this gate.
- The main gate keeps prefix cache disabled. Prefix-cache-on is tracked separately because it changes both latency behavior and reuse semantics.


- sonny-vleisides · comment · 2026-05-21T11:33:30Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4507780873)

> How do you test or run it? Can you share reproducible steps?

Sure...  the stress harness is just synthetic chat traffic + `/metrics` deltas. No special client code.

Run the server with the same shape I listed earlier, then run this against the OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

    python3 -m pip install httpx
    python3 v4_prefix_stress.py --base-url http://localhost:8000 --model deepseek-v4-flash --trials 5

Script:

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import argparse
    import concurrent.futures as cf
    import re
    import time
    import urllib.parse

    import httpx

    def build_long_prompt(filler_words: int) -> str:
        base = (
            "You are analyzing a research manuscript. Below is the section text. "
            "After it, answer the question at the end concisely.\n\n<SECTION>\n"
        )
        words = (
            "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog while the researcher "
            "observes carefully and records each experimental iteration with "
            "precision across the multi-step protocol"
        ).split()
        body = " ".join(words[i % len(words)] for i in range(filler_words))
        tail = (
            "\n</SECTION>\n\nQuestion: In one paragraph, summarize the primary "
            "claim of the section and identify one methodological limitation."
        )
        return base + body + tail

    def prefix_metrics(client, base_url):
        r = client.get(urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, "/metrics"), timeout=10)
        r.raise_for_status()
        hits = 0
        queries = 0
        for line in r.text.splitlines():
            if line.startswith("#"):
                continue
            m = re.match(r"^([a-zA-Z_:]+)(?:\{[^}]*\})?\s+([0-9.eE+-]+)$", line)
            if not m:
                continue
            metric, val = m.group(1), int(float(m.group(2)))
            if metric.endswith("prefix_cache_hits_total"):
                hits += val
            elif metric.endswith("prefix_cache_queries_total"):
                queries += val
        return {"hits": hits, "queries": queries}

    def one_turn(client, base_url, model, conversation, user_msg):
        messages = conversation + [{"role": "user", "content": user_msg}]
        body = {
            "model": model,
            "messages": messages,
            "max_tokens": 256,
            "temperature": 1.0,
            "top_p": 1.0,
            "stream": False,
        }
        t0 = time.time()
        r = client.post(
            urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, "/v1/chat/completions"),
            json=body,
            timeout=180,
        )
        r.raise_for_status()
        elapsed = time.time() - t0
        msg = r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]
        return msg, elapsed

    def run_session(base_url, model, session_idx, turns, filler_words):
        long_prompt = build_long_prompt(filler_words)
        long_prompt += f"\n\n[session_hint: session_{session_idx}_distinct_seed]"

        followups = [
            "Good — now list two counter-examples that would complicate the methodology.",
            "Finally, summarize the exchange so far in two sentences.",
        ]
        user_msgs = [long_prompt] + followups[: turns - 1]

        conversation = []
        stats = []
        with httpx.Client(timeout=200) as client:
            for turn_idx, user_msg in enumerate(user_msgs):
                msg, elapsed = one_turn(client, base_url, model, conversation, user_msg)
                text = msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or ""
                conversation.append({"role": "user", "content": user_msg})
                conversation.append({"role": "assistant", "content": text})
                stats.append({"turn": turn_idx, "elapsed_s": round(elapsed, 2)})
        return stats

    def run_trial(base_url, model, filler_words, turns):
        with httpx.Client(timeout=30) as client:
            m0 = prefix_metrics(client, base_url)

        t0 = time.time()
        run_session(base_url, model, 1, turns, filler_words)
        solo_elapsed = time.time() - t0

        with httpx.Client(timeout=30) as client:
            m1 = prefix_metrics(client, base_url)

        solo_hits = m1["hits"] - m0["hits"]
        solo_queries = m1["queries"] - m0["queries"]
        solo_rate = solo_hits / solo_queries if solo_queries else 0.0

        t0 = time.time()
        with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as ex:
            a = ex.submit(run_session, base_url, model, 1, turns, filler_words)
            b = ex.submit(run_session, base_url, model, 2, turns, filler_words)
            a.result()
            b.result()
        concurrent_elapsed = time.time() - t0

        with httpx.Client(timeout=30) as client:
            m2 = prefix_metrics(client, base_url)

        conc_hits = m2["hits"] - m1["hits"]
        conc_queries = m2["queries"] - m1["queries"]
        conc_rate = conc_hits / conc_queries if conc_queries else 0.0

        return {
            "solo_hits": solo_hits,
            "solo_queries": solo_queries,
            "solo_hit_rate": solo_rate,
            "solo_elapsed_s": solo_elapsed,
            "concurrent_hits": conc_hits,
            "concurrent_queries": conc_queries,
            "concurrent_hit_rate": conc_rate,
            "concurrent_elapsed_s": concurrent_elapsed,
        }

    def main():
        ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        ap.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://localhost:8000")
        ap.add_argument("--model", default="deepseek-v4-flash")
        ap.add_argument("--trials", type=int, default=5)
        ap.add_argument("--filler-words", type=int, default=800)
        ap.add_argument("--turns", type=int, default=3)
        args = ap.parse_args()

        with httpx.Client(timeout=10) as client:
            print("health", client.get(args.base_url + "/health").status_code)

        for i in range(1, args.trials + 1):
            print(f"\ntrial {i}/{args.trials}")
            try:
                r = run_trial(args.base_url, args.model, args.filler_words, args.turns)
                print(
                    "solo:",
                    f"hits={r['solo_hits']}",
                    f"queries={r['solo_queries']}",
                    f"hit_rate={r['solo_hit_rate']:.1%}",
                    f"elapsed={r['solo_elapsed_s']:.1f}s",
                )
                print(
                    "concurrent:",
                    f"hits={r['concurrent_hits']}",
                    f"queries={r['concurrent_queries']}",
                    f"hit_rate={r['concurrent_hit_rate']:.1%}",
                    f"elapsed={r['concurrent_elapsed_s']:.1f}s",
                )
            except Exception as e:
                print("trial failed:", repr(e))

    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

The failure on `edc82b61` was obvious with this shape: trial 1 reset/disconnected while reading `/metrics`, then later trials immediately hit `Server disconnected` or `Connection reset by peer`.

On `d0e1993` and `dad6ff88`, the same script completes normally for me.

I'm game to help with anything else you need. Just let me know.

Update after rechecking the recent long-context reports on 2x RTX PRO 6000 / TP=2.

I added a dedicated long-context decode-concurrency gate for the issue #8-like shape and also added the NVIDIA forum recipe/benchmark-gap scenario to the external reported gates. The important finding is that this does **not** currently look like a pure C=2 paged-MQA decode kernel cliff: warm-cache C=2 decode is healthy. The bad user-visible behavior is primarily the mixed scheduler shape where one request has started decode while another cold long prefill is still being admitted.

The retained scheduler change is an internal best-effort policy, not a user-facing flag: when decode has already been scheduled and the following request is still in long prefill, very long prefill chunks are capped more tightly so the active decode stream gets service more often. CUDA graph remains `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`.

Latest 2x RTX PRO 6000 / TP=2 refresh, MTP, FP8 KV, block size 256, prefix cache disabled unless noted:

| Streaming pressure matrix | 4 cases, 36 requests, failures 0, slow cases 0, max TTFT 64.503s, p99 ITL 1.156s |

| GSM8K 5-shot limit-200, MTP C=4 | exact_match_flexible 0.965, exact_match_strict 0.935 |

This is still not a data-center-grade solution for mixed long-prefill/decode fairness. It is a conservative improvement for the current edge/low-concurrency target: no public knob, no CUDA graph workaround, and no short-context/GSM8K regression in the refreshed gates. For 256K+ or four-card claims, I still think we need real 4-card gates before making commitments.

The current tradeoff looks reasonable for the intended edge / low-concurrency target up to the 128K-class range: the user-reported tail/fairness and continuous-pressure cases improved, short-context and prefill throughput did not materially regress, and prefix-cache stress is stable on the current branch.

Thanks for the detailed prefix-cache numbers. I ran the same reported shape again on the 2x RTX PRO 6000 path after the rebase:

- TP=2, MTP=1, FP8 KV
- prefix cache enabled, block size 256
- `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`
- default sparse MLA decode path
- 3 trials per filler point

The remaining mid-filler drop was real, but the cause was narrower than NCCL or the sparse MLA decode kernel. Active prefix protection was already present after the rebase. The extra loss came from `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.cache_blocks()` flooring `num_computed_tokens` to `lcm_block_size` before writing cache blocks. That dropped complete tail blocks which later chat turns could have used to complete the next LCM-aligned reusable segment.

I pushed `c79225692b71a277a179746e1841d98f054b8649`, which keeps hybrid lookup semantics LCM-aligned but no longer drops complete tail blocks on the cache-write side.

| filler words | before concurrent hit rate | after concurrent hit rate | delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 | 0.000 | 0.137 | +13.67 pp |
| 400 | 0.344 | 0.466 | +12.17 pp |
| 800 | 0.654 | 0.727 | +7.28 pp |
| 1600 | 0.766 | 0.808 | +4.25 pp |
| 3200 | 0.901 | 0.927 | +2.57 pp |

All post-fix sweep points had zero stress failures. A/B at 800 filler also showed that removing only the LCM floor was the useful part: keeping `alignment_tokens` reached 0.7269, while bypassing both floor and alignment was 0.7302, so I kept the narrower fix.

Validation run:

- `python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q` -> 66 passed
- harness prefix-cache diagnostic sweep above -> 5/5 filler points passed, zero stress failures
- harness local checks for the new diagnostics -> 88 passed

I also checked the machine after the run: no vLLM server process was left running, both GPUs were back to 2 MiB / 0% utilization, and `nvidia-smi -L` returned both RTX PRO 6000 GPUs normally. So this run did not reproduce the previous CUDA/NVML/host recovery issue. I would still phrase that narrowly: this stress run shows the fix path is stable under the reported shape; it does not prove user-space code can never trigger a driver/GPU fault again.

- BokuNoGF · comment · 2026-05-24T19:14:39Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4529713546)

Hello @jasl! Thanks very much for putting this PR together, incredible performance on dual DGX Sparks!

Sadly, some of the recent commits cause the nodes to run out of memory during startup soon after loading the weights, and the non-head node to become unresponsive. This happened with one of the changes **after** commit [6423e094be24acc090f906172e401d78b1bbfae8](https://github.com/jasl/vllm/commit/6423e094be24acc090f906172e401d78b1bbfae8) (which works fine), but **before or at** commit [c1b41cea0f5bfaf4636c2c2911ed77920268d027](https://github.com/jasl/vllm/commit/c1b41cea0f5bfaf4636c2c2911ed77920268d027) (which breaks in the same way as described below).

I tried setting `gpu_memory_utilization` to a much lower value (0.7), but that didn't fix it. Worker becomes unresponsive until forcibly restarted. [Other folks reported the same issue in the NVIDIA forums](https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/deepseek-v4-flash-official-fp8-running-across-2x-dgx-spark-tp-2-mtp-200k-ctx-recipe-numbers/370309/73), so don't think it's isolated to my setup.

Below are the startup logs and the kernel logs on the worker with the latest commit.

Let me know if I can adjust any settings or provide any additional information, or do any testing.

- jasl · comment · 2026-05-24T19:17:59Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4529720905)

> Hello @jasl! Thanks very much for putting this PR together, incredible performance on dual DGX Sparks!
> 
> Sadly, some of the recent commits cause the nodes to run out of memory during startup soon after loading the weights, and the non-head node to become unresponsive. This happened with one of the changes **after** commit [6423e094be24acc090f906172e401d78b1bbfae8](https://github.com/jasl/vllm/commit/6423e094be24acc090f906172e401d78b1bbfae8) (which works fine), but **before or at** commit [c1b41cea0f5bfaf4636c2c2911ed77920268d027](https://github.com/jasl/vllm/commit/c1b41cea0f5bfaf4636c2c2911ed77920268d027) (which breaks in the same way).
> 
> I tried setting `gpu_memory_utilization` to a much lower value (0.7), but that didn't fix it.
> 
> Below are the startup logs and the kernel logs on the worker with the latest commit:
> 
> **Build process (using eugr's script):**

- brianmiller · comment · 2026-05-26T03:11:26Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4539637447)

@jasl First result — **`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` confirmed broken on GB10**.

**Config:** vLLM `0.21.1rc1.dev339+g08aef36aa` (main + PR #41834), dual GB10 TP=2, 200GbE RoCE, driver 580.142, CUDA 13.0
- `--max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`
- `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}'`
- `--speculative-config '{"method":"deepseek_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'`

**What happened:** ~5 min after launch, the Ray worker on the TP1 node (gb10-2) died with `ActorDiedError: health check failed due to missing too many heartbeats`. The node then went completely unresponsive — required a power cycle to recover. Consistent with #40969.

```
(EngineCore pid=724) ERROR [core.py:1165]
ray.exceptions.ActorDiedError: The actor died because its node has died.
    class_name: RayWorkerProc
    name: vllm_Worker_..._TP1
    ip: 10.10.10.2
    the actor's node was terminated unexpectedly: health check failed due to missing too many heartbeats
```

**Next:** Retrying with `PIECEWISE` only (no `FULL`). Will report results for both 32K and 131K context.

- brianmiller · comment · 2026-05-26T03:27:58Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4539725829)

@jasl Second crash — **`PIECEWISE` only also crashes GB10**.

Same build, same config as before except `cudagraph_mode` changed from `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` to `PIECEWISE`. This time **both nodes** went down hard (gb10-1 and gb10-2 both unreachable via SSH, required power cycle).

So on GB10: `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` → kills worker node, `PIECEWISE` → kills both nodes. Neither CUDA graph mode is safe on GB10 with MTP=2 currently.

| 2 | PIECEWISE | 2 | 32768 | **Both nodes died** — full cluster unresponsive |
| 3 | enforce-eager | 2 | 32768 | **Both nodes died** — full cluster unresponsive |
| 4 | enforce-eager | off | 131072 | **Both nodes died** — full cluster unresponsive |

- jasl · comment · 2026-05-26T20:15:23Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4548412869)

Post-rebase SM120 validation update for the latest PR head (`27fd665bd`).

Branch state:
- PR branch `jasl/vllm:codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable` pushed to `27fd665bd`
- Dev branch `jasl/vllm:ds4-sm120-preview-dev` pushed to the same `27fd665bd`
- Harness notes were also updated with the latest crash-backlog and baseline evidence.

Test profile:
- 2x RTX PRO 6000 / SM120
- TP=2, MTP=2, FP8 KV, block size 256
- `max_model_len=131072`
- prefix cache disabled for the local quality baseline
- `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graph mode kept enabled
- baseline label: `20260527_post_rebase_f51bbc694_local_quality_full`

Summary:
- No GPU fatal reproduced in this run.
- No NVRM/Xid/UVM/`GPU lost from the bus` signal was observed during the baseline or the follow-up startup replays.
- The previous post-rebase startup/probe crash remains in the crash backlog as intermittent or state-dependent; I am not claiming it is fixed yet.

Passed phases:
- `server_startup`
- `long_context_probe`
- 59K/124K long-context latency matrix, C=1/C=2, cold, repeat=3
- DS4-style frontier context sweep
- DS4 story-recall semantic gate
- 124K decode concurrency, C=1/C=2
- mixed long/short arrival
- standalone streaming pressure matrix
- short-context MT-Bench-style throughput sweep, C=1/2/4/8/16/24
- GSM8K 5-shot limit-200
- random prefill sweep, ISL=1K/4K/16K/64K

Selected results:
- GSM8K limit-200: `exact_match_flexible=0.945`, `exact_match_strict=0.935`
- 59K C=1: TTFT mean `12.52s`, decode mean `144.86 tok/s`
- 59K C=2: TTFT mean `21.44s`, decode mean `75.46 tok/s`, min/max decode `10.38 / 137.19 tok/s`
- 124K C=1: TTFT mean `32.32s`, decode mean `108.52 tok/s`
- 124K C=2: TTFT mean `50.45s`, decode mean `63.62 tok/s`, min/max decode `14.63 / 108.33 tok/s`
- 124K decode-concurrency C=2: TTFT mean `49.83s`, decode mean `65.69 tok/s`, min/max decode `22.06 / 109.31 tok/s`, ITL p99 `0.138s`
- Mixed arrival `decode_then_59k`: 0 failures, primary TTFT mean `13.01s`, primary ITL p99 `0.128s`
- Mixed arrival `long_then_short`: 0 failures, primary TTFT mean `32.71s`, secondary TTFT mean `31.42s`, max primary ITL gap `1.004s`
- Standalone streaming pressure matrix: 36 requests, 0 failures, max TTFT `58.54s`, p99 inter-chunk gap `1.999s`
- Short-context output throughput C=1/2/4/8/16/24: `151.98 / 261.41 / 394.70 / 551.28 / 783.89 / 917.61 tok/s`
- MTP spec acceptance stayed around `68%`; per-position acceptance roughly `[84%, 51%]`
- Random prefill mean TTFT: ISL 1K `175ms`, 4K `671ms`, 16K `2.91s`, 64K `14.17s`

Known remaining observations:
- The full baseline process returned nonzero because bundled acceptance quality gates had generation/tool-call/embedded streaming failures, not because of a CUDA or driver crash.
- Generation matrix: 315 cases, 310 pass, 5 content-length failures.
- Tool-call gate: 235/270 points, 87%.
- A bundled acceptance streaming run had 1 request failure, while the standalone streaming pressure phase passed all 36 requests.
- C=2 long-context decode fairness is still the main performance limitation to watch; it is not currently a crash blocker on this SM120 run.

Follow-up startup replay:
- After the full baseline, I ran three fresh `server_startup -> long_context_probe` replays with the same 131K-capable serve profile.
- All three passed and showed no NVRM/Xid/UVM signals.

Given the evidence above, the RTX PRO 6000 path looks usable for the covered 128K-class local-quality matrix, but I would still keep the original fatal-driver event and GB10 reports as open crash-backlog items until we get a reduced deterministic reproducer or GB10-specific confirmation.
