- pasta-paul · comment · 2026-05-27T00:28:10Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4550181916)

@jasl — empirical validation of the RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition tuned configs in this PR. We are running [`canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP`](https://huggingface.co/canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP) on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM 12.0, sm_120) and the PR's tuned configs **directly fix the SM 12.0 numerical drift** we documented at [`#43564`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43564).

### Setup

vLLM HEAD `a02a3778f` (jasl ds4-sm120-preview-dev base) + the 3 still-open patches from [`#43564`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43564) (`#40923`, `#36889` reopen-candidate, workspace 4×) + [`#43722`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43722) (MarlinFP8 block-refuse) + [`#43723`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43723) (DSv4 `wo_a` scale fallback). After the MarlinFP8 refuse routes block-FP8 attention compressor layers (`compressor.fused_wqa_wkv` etc.) to `TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`, **without** this PR's tuned configs, Triton's default autotune (`num_stages=2`, default block sizes) produces:

```
Q: "What is 2+2?"
A: " 4*4=16, so 4*4=16, so 4*4=16, so 4*4=16, so 4*4=16, so..."  (degenerate loop from token 1)
```

After dropping in this PR's 6 linear-side configs (`N=1536/2048/4096/8192/16384, K=1024/4096`) + 10 MoE-side configs (`E=20/32/64/128/256, N=384/512/704/1024/1536/2048`) for `NVIDIA_RTX_PRO_6000_Blackwell_Server_Edition`:

```
Q: "What is 2+2?"
A: " 4\n\nWhat is your name? Answer: John Smith\nWhat is your quest? Answer: To find the
   Holy Grail, of course! ..."  (correct + coherent continuation)

Q: "Compute 17 * 23. Show your work step by step."
A: "We can compute 17*23 manually using the following steps:
    1) decompose ... (10+7)*(10+7) = 10*10 + 2*10*7 + 7*7 = 100 + 140 + 49 = 289.
    Wait, that's wrong because we forgot units: Actually, let's compute stepwise:
    17*23 = 17*20 + 17*3 = 340 + 51 = 391."   (correct answer, proper chain of thought)
```

300+ tokens of coherent multi-step math reasoning vs. degenerate loop with default configs. **This is a hard regression fix for SM 12.0 consumer Blackwell with block-FP8 quantized attention.**

### MTP acceptance also improved

Pre-tuned (default Triton configs):
```
vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total = N
vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total = 0.1365 * N  (13.65% acceptance over 30 problems)
```

Post-tuned (this PR's configs applied):
```
acceptance: 34.66% on free-form smoke prompts (87 / 251 drafts)
```

The remaining gap to canonical 70-80% acceptance traces to a separate bug class (MTP × `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v4` × thinking-mode in [`#34650`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34650) — emits content but reasoning_parser captures `reasoning_content=''` and `content=''`); not in scope for this PR.

### Coverage gaps we noticed

The 6 Server Edition linear configs cover N ∈ {1536, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384} × K ∈ {1024, 4096} with `block_shape=[128,128]`. For DSv4-Flash's `wo_a` shape (N=1024, K=512) and a few other compressor shapes, no Server Edition config ships in this PR and Triton falls back to default autotune. That coverage gap manifests as drift starting at ~100-150 generated tokens once those layers see fresh shapes. Not strictly this PR's scope, but flagging in case you want to add a couple more shapes during a re-run.

### What we'd like

1. Merge / merge-soon — this is a real correctness fix on the only viable block-FP8 kernel for SM 12.0 today (FlashInfer block-scale, DeepGemm, and Cutlass all refuse SM 12.0; per `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:496` traceback). MarlinFP8 also refuses block-FP8 after [`#43722`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43722) lands.
2. (Optional, nice-to-have) Add the N=1024/K=512 (`wo_a`) and a couple of other DSv4-Flash compressor shapes to the Server Edition config drop. Happy to PR if you'd prefer that path.

Cross-references: [`#43564`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43564), [`#43722`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43722), [`#43723`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43723), [`#43655`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43655).

> _Disclosure (per [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/AGENTS.md#accountability)): drafted with AI assistance; the empirical data above (smoke prompts, MTP acceptance numbers, kernel dispatch trace, error messages) was captured live on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition at 2026-05-26 with this PR's configs dropped into a jasl-based runtime. Reproducibility scripts public at [canada-quant/dsv4-flash-nvfp4-fp8-mtp](https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-nvfp4-fp8-mtp). The human submitter (@pasta-paul / canada-quant) defends every claim._

- pasta-paul · comment · 2026-05-27T03:44:14Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4551028731)

## Follow-up — `fp8_einsum` SM 12.0 dispatch gap (2026-05-27)

> _Disclosure (per [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/AGENTS.md#accountability)): drafted with AI assistance; the empirical evidence below was captured live on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM 12.0) against [`canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP`](https://huggingface.co/canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP) earlier today. The human submitter (@pasta-paul / canada-quant) defends every claim._

This PR ships `_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_sm12x` (cleanly fixes the first DeepGEMM Hopper-only assert on SM 12.0) but our end-to-end test on RTX PRO 6000 today exposes a **second DeepGEMM Hopper-only call site that this PR does not cover**: `fp8_einsum`.

### Reproducer

vllm-project/vllm@`e19b9b104` + this PR's full overlay (`vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/sm12x_deep_gemm_fallbacks.py`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/sm12x_mqa.py`, 16 RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition tuned config JSONs) + our 4 cherry-picks (#43655 rebased, #43722, #43723, #40923) + DeepGEMM bundled-source Python package install. Serve [`canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP`](https://huggingface.co/canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP) on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition, TP=4, `VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1` + standard MTP serve flags.

Result: engine init progresses past Marlin dispatch (your `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` SM 12.0 fallback fires correctly), Triton block-FP8 selected for attention compressors, MTP shared embeddings load, model loads (43.4 GiB / 33.8s). **At first forward pass, fails with:**

```
RuntimeError: Assertion error (csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/../heuristics/../../utils/layout.hpp:39): t.dim() == N
  at vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:317  fp8_einsum
  at vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/attention.py  (forward pass)
```

`vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:317 fp8_einsum` reaches `_fp8_einsum_impl` which is set by `_lazy_init` to `getattr(_dg, "fp8_einsum", None)` — and DeepGEMM's `fp8_einsum` asserts `t.dim() == N` for a Hopper layout that doesn't match what mainline DSv4 attention passes on SM 12.0.

### Root cause + the jasl fallback that mainline lacks

jasl/vllm@`27fd665b` (ds4-sm120-preview-dev HEAD) ships these additional files in `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/` that mainline (and this PR) do not include:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `fp8_einsum.py` | Triton SM 12.0 fallback for the `fp8_einsum` DSv4 attention call |
| `cutedsl_utils.py` | CuteDSL helpers used by the SM 12.0 dispatch glue |
| `dequant_gather_k_cutedsl.py` | Already in mainline post-#43149 |
| `fused_indexer_q_cutedsl.py` | Already in mainline post-#43149 |

jasl's `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` correspondingly dispatches:

```python
def fp8_einsum(...):
    if current_platform.is_device_capability_family(120):
        return _fp8_einsum_sm12x(...)  # imports from sm12x_deep_gemm_fallbacks
    _lazy_init()
    return _fp8_einsum_impl(*args, **kwargs)
```

which is structurally identical to your `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` SM 12.0 fallback shape in this PR — the gap is just that `fp8_einsum` didn't get the same treatment.

### What we'd ask

1. **Extend this PR (or land a follow-up)** to add `_fp8_einsum_sm12x` + `cutedsl_utils.py` mirroring the `_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_sm12x` pattern this PR already establishes. The jasl branch has both files plus the deep_gemm.py dispatch — straightforward port (probably ~80-150 line addition).
2. **Or open a sibling PR** so this one can land sooner — happy to file the follow-up myself if you point me at the right scope.

Without that, even with all of this PR + #43722 + #43723 + #40923 + #43655 (rebased), mainline vllm-project/vllm fails at first forward pass on SM 12.0 for any DSv4 artifact that exercises the `fp8_einsum` attention path (which is all of them).

### What we'd offer

The session that surfaced this gap also produced an empirically-verified RTX PRO 6000 recipe on jasl/vllm@27fd665b (Card D AIME-30 c=4 thinking: 24/30 correct, 0 CUDA errors, 91.6% MTP acceptance — [bench JSON](https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp/blob/main/benchmarks/rtxpro6000/aime30_c4_thinking_jasl27fd665b.json)). Happy to retest with any extended `fp8_einsum` fallback you ship; we have the box and the artifacts ready.

### Cross-references

- Parent tracker [#43564](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43564) — full phase summary at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43564#issuecomment-4550184475
- Our open companion PRs [#43722](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43722) (Marlin block-FP8 refuse) + [#43723](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43723) (DSv4 `wo_a` scale fallback)
- jasl/vllm `ds4-sm120-preview-dev` source for the missing files: https://github.com/jasl/vllm/tree/ds4-sm120-preview-dev/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops

cc @jasl @mgoin @pavanimajety @robertgshaw2-redhat @tlrmchlsmth @yewentao256.

@jasl Sorry to add one more thing: I noticed applying @wishstudio's fix on top of the head of this branch is that it seems like main branch reverted a bump of `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]` package from [4.5.1 to 4.5.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43230), which make the `cute.arch.fmin` function no longer available. This causes startup to fail. 

Reverting the `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]` package version to 4.5.1 fixes it.

- jasl · comment · 2026-05-27T05:16:37Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4551542635)

> @jasl Sorry to add one more thing: I noticed applying @wishstudio's fix on top of the head of this branch is that it seems like main branch reverted a bump of `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]` package from [4.5.1 to 4.5.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43230), which make the `cute.arch.fmin` function no longer available. This causes startup to fail.
> 
> Reverting the `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]` package version to 4.5.1 fixes it.
> 
> Once this revert is done, along with @wishstudio revert change makes it work on dual DGX Sparks, can confirm! 50+ tg t/s!

> Can you try with `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` ? Let's ensure the NCCL is not the root cause, 5-16 version should work, just prefill not good.

After several days of testing, I've summarized the following conclusions:

- The impact of caching must be ruled out. Every time I start VLLM to deploy v4 Flash, I delete the cache and let VLLM rebuild. Otherwise, strange crashes occur.

- It's not related to the nccl version, because even after upgrading, it still crashes. Since Torch warns of nccl version incompatibility, I eventually downgraded nccl to a compatible version.

- It's known to be related to the deployment of other models. Because I have 4x RTX PRO 6000, after deploying v4 Flash, I deployed qwen3.6 27b using a new VLLM instance. In this case, v4 Flash will always crash at some point, regardless of the setup.

- It's known that not using `--enable-expert-parallel` and only deploying v4 Flash results in the most stable setup. I've used this for several days without encountering the crashes I mentioned above.

- It's known that crashes like `[Errno 24] Too many open files: ...` will occur. After investigation by GPT, the problem was found to be due to an excessive number of files in the cache (specifically, the v4 flash cache). I counted the files in the v4 flash cache directory, and there were over 70,000 regular files.

In addition, the code I use is the pr code of 2026-05-16.

- jasl · comment · 2026-05-28T08:13:54Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4562011162)

Thanks, this log is very useful.

For this specific crash, the terminal error does **not** look like NCCL/P2P to me. The worker fails while Triton is writing a compile-cache group file:

```text
OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files: .../vllm_cache/torch_compile_cache/torch_aot_compile/.../inductor_cache/triton/.../__grp___deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum_kernel.json
```

So I would treat this one as compile-cache / file-descriptor pressure first. It can plausibly be amplified by running multiple vLLM instances and/or sharing a very large cache tree between DSv4 Flash and another model.

A few concrete checks that would help:

1. Check the effective fd limits of the actual API/worker processes, not only the login shell:

```bash
cat /proc/<api_or_worker_pid>/limits | grep -i "open files"
# or
prlimit -p <api_or_worker_pid> | grep NOFILE
```

vLLM tries to raise `RLIMIT_NOFILE` to 65535 during API-server startup, but systemd/container hard limits can still cap it lower. If you launch from systemd/docker/etc., please raise the hard limit there as well, e.g. `LimitNOFILE=` or docker `--ulimit nofile=...`.

2. For multi-instance testing, please try a separate cache root per instance/model instead of sharing the same DSv4 Flash cache tree, for example:

```bash
export VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/path/to/cache-dsv4-flash-instance-1
# and use a different VLLM_CACHE_ROOT for Qwen or another vLLM instance
```

Then start from a clean cache and see whether the `[Errno 24]` disappears. If separate cache roots make the issue disappear, that would strongly support the cache/fd-pressure diagnosis.

3. `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1` can be useful as a diagnostic only. I would not recommend it as a performance setting, but if it avoids the `Errno 24` crash, it is another signal that the failure is in the compile-cache path rather than NCCL.

Also, the 2026-05-16 PR snapshot is quite old now. The latest branch has had several SM120 stability fixes since then, and I just rebased it again onto current upstream/main. It is worth retesting with the latest branch before we attribute this to NCCL or expert parallelism.

If you can share the launch commands/env for both vLLM instances, the effective `/proc/<pid>/limits` output, and whether separate `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` directories change the result, that should make this much easier to pin down.

The default ulimit -n of my system is 1024.

The cache I mentioned above contains 70K regular files, and this cache directory is only used for v4 flash.

Now I have added the following code to the script to deploy v4 flash to deal with this problem:
```bash
ulimit -n 1048576

export VLLM_CACHE_ROOT="$HOME/depot/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/vllm_cache"
rm -r "$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT"
mkdir -p "$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT"
```

I changed the deployment method. Now I only use 2 RTX PRO 6000 graphics cards to deploy v4 flash. The prefill speed is much better than before. I no longer need to deploy with 4 cards. This should avoid the previous crash issues.


This is my previous -tp4 startup script (now I have switched to -tp2 for deployment):
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# ref: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834
# ref: https://github.com/jasl/vllm-ds4-sm120-harness/blob/main/baselines/20260511_sm120_isl_sweep_020e0c89a/repro_recipe.md

#source ~/depot/wsp/vllm-sm120/vllm/venv-ds4-sm120-full/bin/activate # ds4-sm120-full 分支(相对稳定)
#source ~/depot/wsp/vllm-dsv4-flash/.venv2/bin/activate # pr-41834 的05-14最新代码
source ~/depot/venv/vllm-dsv4-pr-41834/bin/activate # pr-41834 的05-16最新代码

export VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1
export DO_NOT_TRACK=1
export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1

#export TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0a

vllm serve ~/depot/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
    --served-model-name deepseek-v4-flash \

    --trust-remote-code \

| KV lifecycle | prefix disabled final idle KV `0.0%`; prefix enabled final idle KV `5.894%` |
| Runtime health | no server-unresponsive signal; CUDA/NCCL/driver/engine error counters all 0 |

| Prompt | C | TTFT mean | Decode tok/s | Decode min/max | ITL p99 |

I added the latest fixed-protocol C=2 repeat/profile data to the PR description.

New artifact label: `20260601_c2_fixed_protocol_repeat/20260601150253` on 2x RTX PRO 6000 SM120, same TP=2 / MTP=2 / FP8 KV / FULL_AND_PIECEWISE profile.

Summary:

| Shape | TTFT mean | Decode min/max | ITL p99 | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 59K C=2 latency matrix | 23.421 s | 0.124 | 0.824 s | stable slow-stream fairness issue |
| 124K C=2 latency matrix | 60.676 s | 0.094 | 1.112 s | stable slow-stream fairness issue |
| `long_long_59k_c2` mixed arrival | primary 22.281 s / secondary 26.455 s | 0.133 | 0.857 s | same long+long class |
| `long_long_124k_c2` mixed arrival | primary 59.104 s / secondary 63.952 s | 0.108 | 1.112 s | same long+long class |
| `decode_then_124k` mixed arrival | primary 30.492 s / secondary 31.292 s | 0.416 | 0.092 s | staggered decode protected |
| `long_then_short` mixed arrival | secondary TTFT 3.327 s | 0.314 | 0.088 s | short-after-long tail remains fixed |

This confirms the current pending-decode scheduler guard fixes the short-after-long starvation case, without claiming to solve simultaneous long+long C=2 fairness.

Nsys from the same serve profile points to `_accumulate_indexed_attention_chunk_multihead_kernel` as the primary remaining long+long C=2 target: 37.1% of captured CUDA time for `long_long_59k_c2`, 44.7% for `long_long_124k_c2`. Global decode-kernel gaps were only 0.152-0.159 s, much smaller than the per-request ITL p99, so the remaining symptom looks like request-level slow-stream fairness rather than a global decode stoppage.

I also tested a `HEAD_BLOCK=4` sparse-MLA probe. It reduced registers and raised occupancy in NCU, but worsened real microbench duration (`1.080 ms -> 1.246 ms` for the target chunk kernel), so that experiment was reverted and is not in this PR branch.

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-01T08:08:33Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4590705618)

Thanks for the precise report. I pushed a fix in [`0d585a054`](https://github.com/jasl/vllm/commit/0d585a054fb644870e6984d98bb3f29b1527a0cb).

The compressor no longer depends on `cute.arch.fmin`; the FP8 clamp now uses the equivalent `min(a, b) = -max(-a, -b)` form built only from `cute.arch.fmax`.

I could not reproduce the exact AttributeError on my SM120 host because its installed `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.5.2` does expose `cute.arch.fmin`, but I verified the reported failure mode directly by deleting `cute.arch.fmin` in-process and then compiling/running both sparse-attn compressor paths:

- C4 fused `compress_norm_rope_store_cutedsl`: passed with `cute.arch.fmin` removed
- C128 split `compress_norm_rope_store_cutedsl`: passed with `cute.arch.fmin` removed

Focused checks run:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_cutedsl_compat.py -q
python -m py_compile vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/sparse_attn_compress_cutedsl.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_cutedsl_compat.py
python -m ruff check vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/sparse_attn_compress_cutedsl.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_cutedsl_compat.py
```

Results: pytest `1 passed`, py_compile passed, ruff passed, plus the CUDA smoke above.

> 
>       --enable-expert-parallel
>       --enable-prefix-caching
>       --enable-prompt-tokens-details
>       --enable-chunked-prefill
>       --enable-auto-tool-choice
> 
>       --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4
>       --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4
>       --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4
> 
>       --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"thinking": true}'
>       --speculative_config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'
>       --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}'
> 
>       --no-enforce-eager
> 
>       --trust-remote-code
>       --host 0.0.0.0
>       --port 8000
> ```
> 
> ### DP=2 + EP
> First of all, I am not a professional in this area, I stumbled upon an article https://rocm.blogs.amd.com/software-tools-optimization/vllm-moe-guide/README.html#dp-with-ep which describes in detail the differences and usage scenarios between DP , the differences between TP, PP and usage scenarios, the article mentions that deepseek(V2/V3/R1) causes a waste of video memory due to MLA/MQA as TP copies the full KV cache on each GPU, I'm not sure if that situation exists with v4 as well, in my tests with all other parameters being equal:
> 
> TP=2 + EP available tokens are
> 
> ```shell
> vllm-sm120  | (EngineCore pid=639) INFO 06-01 19:50:53 [kv_cache_utils.py:1733] GPU KV cache size: 327,437 tokens
> vllm-sm120  | (EngineCore pid=639) INFO 06-01 19:50:53 [kv_cache_utils.py:1734] Maximum concurrency for 256,000 tokens per request: 1.28x
> ```
> 
> Everything is normal under TP mode, and the performance is excellent.
> 
> DP=2 + EP available tokens are
> 
> ```shell
> vllm-sm120  | (EngineCore_DP0 pid=773) INFO 06-01 17:58:09 [kv_cache_utils.py:1733] GPU KV cache size: 497,054 tokens
> vllm-sm120  | (EngineCore_DP0 pid=773) INFO 06-01 17:58:09 [kv_cache_utils.py:1734] Maximum concurrency for 256,000 tokens per request: 1.94x
> vllm-sm120  | (EngineCore_DP1 pid=774) INFO 06-01 17:58:09 [kv_cache_utils.py:1733] GPU KV cache size: 497,054 tokens
> vllm-sm120  | (EngineCore_DP1 pid=774) INFO 06-01 17:58:09 [kv_cache_utils.py:1734] Maximum concurrency for 256,000 tokens per request: 1.94x
> ```
>

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-01T14:56:07Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4593776430)

Thanks for the detailed DP=2 + EP report. I investigated this on the latest branch head and pushed a mitigation in `3af0ab3372ce53da88f2adf24901c067b010cf16`.

What I found:

- I could not reproduce the exact `device-side assert` / `load_binary` crash on the latest head.
- I did reproduce the risky precondition from your stack: `_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_kernel` was still being JIT-compiled during inference in the reported 256K, DP=2, EP, MTP=2, prefix-cache-enabled shape.
- The root cause was that this Triton kernel specialized on `M` (the current token count). With random or user-shaped prefill lengths, that can force a new binary per token count. That matches the repeated JIT/log pattern in your report and makes the `load_binary` failure path plausible.

The fix changes `M` from a Triton constexpr to a runtime value, so the same split bucket can reuse the same compiled kernel instead of compiling a fresh variant for every distinct prompt length.

Validation I ran after the fix:

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Static regression test for the kernel signature | passed |
| Direct GPU smoke for `M=1/17/257/300` vs torch reference | passed |
| 2x RTX PRO 6000, 256K max model len, DP=2, EP on, MTP=2, prefix cache enabled, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | passed |
| Random-length prefill soak lengths `257,300,513,560,1025,1088,2049,2112,4097,4160,8193,8256` | 12/12 passed |
| `_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_kernel` JIT count in that 12-case soak | 1 total occurrence, not repeated per length |
| GB10 reduced long-C2 gate, nomtp + mtp2 | passed, no engine/driver/GPU-lost errors |
| 8K x 1K PR performance regression gate, C=1/2/4 | passed; output tok/s speedup vs accepted baseline `1.00 / 0.99 / 0.99` |

On the RTX PRO 6000 DP=2 run, the server reported `GPU KV cache size: 499,309 tokens`, which is consistent with the capacity you observed. Please retest with the latest PR head when you can. Your original SHA `779d229dc36fc3b1cb965fd603e830f18def15ef` predates this fix.

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-03T16:14:10Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4614453195)

Pushed a refreshed branch at `6ad56ea41` and reran the full user-feedback matrix with the long-prefill/decode interference fix enabled by default.

Key change: when decode pressure is already present, the scheduler now defers a very-long prefill chunk for that step instead of allowing the worst long-prefill/active-decode overlap. This keeps `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graph compilation enabled and adds no public tuning flag.

Latest RTX PRO 6000 x2 results:

| Shape | Failures | TTFT mean | Decode tok/s | Decode min/max | ITL p99 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 59K C=1 | 0 | 11.649s | 139.639 | 0.989 | 0.021s |
| 59K C=2 | 0 | 18.041s | 139.333 | 0.956 | 0.022s |
| 124K C=1 | 0 | 29.653s | 106.097 | 0.989 | 0.035s |
| 124K C=2 | 0 | 45.620s | 105.511 | 0.934 | 0.031s |
| 124K decode-concurrency C=2 | 0 | 45.614s | 104.056 | 0.960 | 0.031s |

The exact long+long C=2 probe produced decode mean 101.621 tok/s, decode min/max 0.963, p99 ITL 0.0347s, and zero overlap steps in the scheduler trace. The tradeoff is intentional: the second long prefill can wait so the active decode stream keeps a stable token cadence.

Other gates from the same run:

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Full user-feedback matrix | OK, all phases exit 0 |
| Prefix-cache stress | filler 100/400/800/1600/3200 all OK, 0 failures |
| KV lifecycle | prefix-disabled final idle KV 0.0%; prefix-enabled final idle KV 5.843% |
| GSM8K limit-200 | flexible EM 0.950, strict EM 0.930 |
| GB10 reduced long-C2 | OK; 4 requests, 0 failures, p99 ITL 0.089s, no CUDA/NCCL/driver error signals |

Throughput profile on RTX PRO 6000 x2, MTP=2:

| Workload | C=1 | C=2 | C=4 | C=8 | C=16 | C=24 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Short MT bench output tok/s | 172.10 | 270.07 | 403.03 | 571.15 | 781.62 | 933.66 |
| Random 8K/1K output tok/s | 126.92 | 187.50 | 257.31 | 323.26 | 384.97 | 406.34 |
| Random 256/256 output tok/s | 147.12 | 233.33 | 355.04 | 506.79 | 723.25 | 808.45 |

Caveats: this is a fairness/availability fix, not a raw prefill kernel speedup. 256K+/four-card behavior is still unclaimed until separately gated, and a separate external high-concurrency sparse-MLA decode workspace-sizing report is now tracked by the harness stress gate rather than treated as fixed here.

- xermicus · comment · 2026-06-05T09:43:15Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4630175235)

The last commits may have introduced a regression: `TypeError: MLAAttentionManager.cache_blocks() got an unexpected keyword argument 'retention_interval'`

  The coordinator passes retention_interval= to every manager's cache_blocks (from #43447), but MLAAttentionManager.cache_blocks only takes (request, num_tokens, alignment_tokens=None). MLA models route through that override, so the engine dies on the first generate. Looks
  like the recent rebase pulled in the coordinator change but the MLA override never got the new kwarg.

  Adding retention_interval to the signature and forwarding it to super().cache_blocks(...) fixes it. SlidingWindowMLAManager.cache_blocks has the same signature and probably needs it too.

  Last commit that worked for me was 0d585a05 (pre-rebase); everything after carries this.

Thanks for catching this. The `retention_interval` mismatch was a real rebase integration issue: the coordinator can pass `retention_interval=` after the selective retention changes, so the MLA managers must accept and forward it as well.

The latest `jasl:codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable` now includes the fix. In particular, `MLAAttentionManager.cache_blocks()` and `SlidingWindowMLAManager.cache_blocks()` both accept `retention_interval` and forward it to `super().cache_blocks(...)`.

Validation on dual RTX PRO 6000 / SM120 after rebasing to current `upstream/main`:

- `test_hybrid_local_kv_retention_interval_survives_recycling` and related prefix-cache retention tests: 3 passed
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py`: 6 passed
- `py_compile` on the touched MTP / prefix-cache files: passed
- `ruff check` on the touched files/tests: passed
- short-context PR performance regression gate, 8K/1K C=1/2/4/8/16/24, MTP=2, prefix cache disabled, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`: passed against the latest complete accepted throughput baseline; all tok/s, TPOT, and speculative acceptance ratios stayed within the 5% regression threshold

I also made sure the MTP sampling conflict from the rebase preserved both upstream's FP64 Gumbel path and our draft sampling metadata expansion.

- brianmiller · comment · 2026-06-06T01:13:18Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4636760457)

Tested `8725eb974` on our dual GB10 / SM121 cluster. Everything is working — first time we've had CUDA graphs + MTP running stable on these nodes. Major improvement from our May 26 test where all 5 configurations crashed.

**Hardware:** 2x DGX Spark GB10 (SM121), 128 GB unified memory each, 200GbE RoCE, driver 580.142, CUDA 13.0, aarch64 / Ubuntu 24.04.4 / kernel 6.17.0-1014-nvidia

**Build:** `eugr/spark-vllm-docker` with Dockerfile patched to clone from `jasl/vllm` (the build script lacks `--vllm-repo`). vLLM `0.21.1rc1.dev751+g8725eb974.d20260605`, torch 2.11.0+cu130.

**Serve profile:** TP=2, MTP=2, FP8 KV, block size 256, max-model-len 131072, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, `--max-num-seqs 4`, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, prefix cache enabled.

### Short-context throughput (5 requests per C, max_tokens=512)

| C | Successful | Output tok/s |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 5 / 5 | 42.70 |
| 2 | 5 / 5 | 56.61 |
| 4 | 5 / 5 | 63.66 |

### Long-context (121K prompt tokens, max_tokens=256)

| Test | Elapsed s | Completion tokens | Status |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| C=1 cold | 110.7 | 61 | OK |
| C=2 (prefix cached) | 13.8 batch | 86 + 95 | OK |

### Comparison with our previous baseline (vLLM 0.20.2, enforce-eager, no MTP)

Single-request throughput improved from ~14 tok/s to **42.7 tok/s (3x)**. Zero crashes across all tests — previous session (May 26, `--apply-vllm-pr 41834`) crashed in all 5 configurations within seconds of CUDA graph warmup.

### GB10-specific notes

- **`gpu-memory-utilization 0.975` fails** — GB10 unified memory only has ~110/122 GiB free at startup (OS, Docker, etc. consume ~12 GiB). Reduced to 0.85 which starts cleanly. Might be worth documenting the recommended GB10 value.
- **First-time startup takes ~107 min on aarch64** — torch inductor + Triton JIT compilation is extremely slow on ARM64 Cortex-A78AE. Generates 227K Triton cache files (9.1 GB) and 1,775 torch compile cache files (305 MB). Subsequent starts reuse the cache. Your `STARTUP_TIMEOUT=900` would need to be much higher for first-time GB10 starts.
- **Build notes:** `--apply-vllm-pr 41834` (patching onto upstream main) does not work — must build from fork directly. The PR #43410 MiniMax revert in `eugr/spark-vllm-docker` conflicts with fork history and must be skipped. Torch pin (`--override`) is needed to prevent `uv pip install` from pulling CPU-only torch.


- hazyumps · comment · 2026-06-06T01:34:49Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4636849276)

**Field report: 2× GB10 / DGX Spark (sm_121, aarch64), TP=2 + EP over 200G RoCE — big prefill win on the latest PR head, plus a torch-version build trap worth flagging**

Rebuilt from `8725eb974` (this PR's head) on dual GB10 and benchmarked against our previous pin `dda4668b5`. The recent sparse-MLA prefill commits ("skip empty D512 sparse MLA tail blocks", "preserve ubatch prefill metadata", "restore Triton sparse MLA decode dispatch") are a **substantial** improvement here — well beyond the ~18% others reported.

**Config:** DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8, TP=2 + `--enable-expert-parallel`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-num-seqs 2`, MTP n=2, torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.2 base, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.1a`.

**Benchmarks** (no-think, unique prompts to defeat prefix cache, `ignore_eos`, token counts from `usage.completion_tokens`):

| Metric | `dda4668b5` | `8725eb974` | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single-stream decode | 38.8 tok/s | ~50 tok/s | +30% |
| Prefill 3.2k ctx | 6.05s (536 t/s) | 3.09s (1053 t/s) | ~2.0× |
| Prefill 7k ctx | 14.4s (492 t/s) | 6.24s (1134 t/s) | ~2.3× |
| Prefill 12.8k ctx | 27.1s (471 t/s) | 15.3s (835 t/s) | ~1.8× |
| 2-/4-concurrent agg | bursty stalls | 49 / 54 tok/s, scales clean | — |

Notably, concurrent load is now **stall-free** — 0 accumulating `shm_broadcast` markers, 0 preemptions across the runs. On our older build, MTP-on under concurrency was a wedge risk; here **MTP-on is both faster (~2× decode vs MTP-off: ~50 vs ~25 tok/s) and stable**. Prefill is identical MTP on/off, as expected.

**Build trap (cost us a few hours — may help other aarch64 builders):** the v0.22.0 rebase requires **torch 2.11.0** to *compile* — `csrc/libtorch_stable/cuda_view.cu` uses `torch::stable::Tensor::layout`, which doesn't exist in 2.10.0 (`error: class "torch::stable::Tensor" has no member "layout"`). But `requirements/build/cuda.txt` pins `torch==2.10.0`, and on aarch64 that resolves to the **CPU** wheel from the default index, silently downgrading the CUDA torch the base image installed → runtime `ImportError: libtorch_cuda.so: cannot open shared object file` (or an `undefined symbol: c10::cuda::CUDAStream::query()` if you swap torch post-build against a mismatched version). The fix that worked: compile against `torch==2.11.0+cu130`, and make sure the *runtime* torch is also `2.11.0+cu130` (the `use_existing_torch.py` pass didn't strip torch from `requirements/build/cuda.txt` for us). Is the `torch==2.10.0` pin intentional, or should it track 2.11.0 given the `torch::stable` usage?

Happy to share the benchmark scripts. Thanks for the SM12x work — this is a real step up on consumer Blackwell.

- tobymao · comment · 2026-06-07T05:17:50Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4641514454)

### MTP-triggered tensor-parallel deadlock in DeepSeek-V4 MoE (SM121, TP=2, 2-node)

Reporting a serving-stability issue on this branch (built at `49910eea6`). Distinct from — and surfaced *after* — the breakable-cudagraph fix (`5de1c6cad`), which did resolve an earlier o_proj-Triton-GEMM hang.

**Hardware / config:** 2× DGX Spark (GB10 / **SM121**), TP=2 across 2 nodes, NCCL over RoCE. `--speculative-config '{"method":"deepseek_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 200000`, `--max-num-seqs 8`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`, PIECEWISE cudagraph, prefix caching on.

**Symptom:** intermittent silent hang during decode (~40 min into a sustained workload). Engine `num_requests_running=1`, `Avg generation throughput: 0`, both GPUs 96% util / ~16 W (collective spin-wait), **no error logged**, never self-recovers (requires restart).

**py-spy at the hang (both ranks):**
```
TP1: ncclAllReduce ← _maybe_reduce_final_output (fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py:416) ← MoE forward   [waiting at MoE final all-reduce]
TP0: default_unquantized_gemm (layers/utils.py:98) ← gate_linear.py:141 ← _moe_forward_shared (moe_runner.py:134)   [still at the MoE gate, not progressing]
```
So TP1 is blocked at the MoE all-reduce while TP0 is stalled earlier in the same layer (between the gate and the reduce) and never reaches the matching collective.

**Confirmed trigger = MTP** (controlled A/B, same build & workload):
- MTP **on**: deadlocks reproducibly at the above stacks (~turn 56 / ~41 min).
- MTP **off** (drop `--speculative-config`): runs clean well past the same point (turn 88 / 60 min) — no hang.

*(Edit: I initially speculated this was a `_fused_output_is_reduced` divergence across ranks causing mismatched all-reduce — that's not it; that flag is a load-time constant, identical on all ranks. Looking deeper into whether TP0 is stalled in a kernel vs an upstream control-flow desync; will follow up with repeated per-rank py-spy + native stacks.)*

Happy to share the repro workload.

- tobymao · comment · 2026-06-07T15:30:02Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4643103915)

**Follow-up with more data — and a correction to my earlier guess.** Reproduced again on `49910eea6` (2× GB10/SM121, TP=2). Sharing observations only; I'm explicitly *not* claiming a mechanism this time.

**Two terminal symptoms, same apparent root (a worker forward-step GPU op that never completes):**
1. *Silent spin* — `num_requests_running=1`, `generation_tokens_total` frozen, both GPUs 96% util / ~16 W, no error logged, needs restart.
2. *Crash* — after `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (1800s), EngineCore `TimeoutError` in `shm_broadcast.dequeue` → `EngineDeadError`, preceded by ~28 min of *"No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds"* (worker not consuming).

**Crash input-dump at the hang (the triggering step):**
```
total_num_scheduled_tokens=3
scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={...: [-1, -1]}   # MTP step, both draft tokens -1 (rejected/invalid)
num_computed_tokens=[88301]                     # ~88K context
```

**py-spy (both ranks, captured ~60 s into the hang):**
```
cudaStreamSynchronize <- at::native::_local_scalar_dense_cuda  (.item())
  <- _c128a_effective_topk_width (flashmla_sparse.py:1122 -> positions.max().item())
  <- _build_attention_metadata   (the NEXT step's metadata build)
```
Important caveat: that `.item()` is the first sync of the *next* decode step, so it only **surfaces** a kernel from the **prior forward** that never completed — it is **not** the bug site. The actual stuck kernel is GPU-side; I have not localized it (would need cuda-gdb / compute-sanitizer).

**MTP on/off (same build + workload):**
- MTP **on**: hangs (silent spin or the timeout-crash above) within tens of minutes of sustained decode.
- MTP **off** (drop `--speculative-config`): one clean 60-min / 88-turn session, no hang.

**cudagraph mode (low n):** `PIECEWISE` hung after ~40 min; a single `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` run hung within ~1 min at the same `.item()` sync (n=1, not conclusive).

Happy to run cuda-gdb / compute-sanitizer to localize the GPU kernel, or share the full py-spy dumps + input-dump.

turns out i was unknowingly on nccl 2.28.9. torch 2.11.0+cu130 hard-pins nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.28.9, which shadowed the 2.30.4 the image had built, so all the mtp hangs were on 2.28.9.

pinned nccl 2.30.4 and re-ran the same mtp=2 workload that used to deadlock at ~40 min. no hang, mtp working (~69% draft acceptance, ~25 tok/s). looks like 2.30.4 fixes it at mtp=2.

thanks for your amazing work

- brianmiller · comment · 2026-06-07T18:23:45Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4643615766)

Follow-up test of `ad75ac7a8` on our dual GB10 / SM121 cluster. Rebuilt from the June 7 branch head — 22 new commits since our June 6 test (`8725eb974`).

**Build:** `eugr/spark-vllm-docker` @ `94fc91b` with Dockerfile patched to clone from `jasl/vllm`. vLLM `0.21.1rc1.dev784+gad75ac7a8.d20260607`, CUDA 13.3.

**Serve profile:** Same as June 6 — TP=2, MTP=2, FP8 KV, block size 256, max-model-len 131072, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, `--max-num-seqs 4`, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE.

**Startup:** Healthy in ~140s — Triton cache from previous build was mostly compatible (vs 107 min cold compile on June 6).

### Short-context throughput (5 requests per C, max_tokens=512)

| C | June 6 (`8725eb9`) tok/s | **June 7 (`ad75ac7`) tok/s** | Delta |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 42.70 | 39.32 | -8% |
| 2 | 56.61 | 54.83 | -3% |
| 4 | 63.66 | 69.74 | **+10%** |

### Long-context (121K prompt tokens, max_tokens=256)

| Test | June 6 (`8725eb9`) | **June 7 (`ad75ac7`)** | Delta |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| C=1 cold prefill | 110.7s | 121.3s | +10% slower |
| C=2 req 1 (prefix cached) | 10.4s | 10.3s | same |
| C=2 req 2 (prefix cached) | 13.8s | 13.3s | same |

### Summary

- **C=4 throughput improved 10%** (63.7 → 69.7 tok/s), consistent with @alexbi29's RTX PRO 6000 report.
- C=1/C=2 short-context slightly slower (~3-8%). Cold 121K prefill ~10% slower. Likely tradeoff from the concurrent workload optimizations (multi-head prefill accumulate, prefill starvation protection, autotune key fix).
- Prefix-cached C=2 latency unchanged — decode path unaffected.
- For multi-user serving, the C=4 improvement outweighs the single-request regression.
- Zero crashes, zero CUDA/NCCL errors across all tests.
- Startup with cached Triton kernels: **140s** (vs 107 min cold compile on June 6). Cache was mostly reusable across the 22-commit delta.

Agent findings:

  - #44454 — its own description says behavior-preserving; only effect is KV tokens +1.16% = the +1.3% bump we measured. Not it.
  - #44455 "Pack K/V into the content dim" (the sibling that would change KV memory layout) — not in the build. Confirmed only [1/N] landed, not [2/N]–[4/N]. So KV layout is unchanged.
  - #44699 — the standalone metadata build() is byte-identical to the V3.2 builder DSV4 used to inherit; only the backend class structure changed (standalone DeepseekV4FlashMLABackend vs subclass).

  Where this lands

  The dominant cost (attention) runs on byte-identical kernels over an unchanged KV layout, yet is 13% slower at ≥8K. With kernel code, KV layout, metadata build, indexer, and tile/chunk params all identical, the only thing left is a systemic graph-capture/dispatch effect
  — most consistent with #44699 turning the attention backend from a V3.2 subclass into a standalone class, changing how the breakable CUDA graph captures/breaks the attention-dominated long-prefill forward. That's invisible to a code diff and can't be measured here (the
  real config needs CUPTI; eager mode removes the very graph effect).

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-09T15:28:05Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4661334684)

I reproduced the GB10 multi-user prefix-cache retention issue and pushed a targeted fix to the PR branch.

Workload used for the before/after check:

- 2x GB10, TP=2
- prefix cache enabled
- MTP off for the reduced repro
- FP8 KV
- `max_model_len=421888`
- `max_num_seqs=4`
- `max_num_batched_tokens=4096`
- C=4, two rounds, ~400K-token prompts

Before the fix, the warm round had one request lose the cached long prefix and re-run a full ~400K prefill:

| warm request | TTFT | scheduler first computed tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 9.280s | 399872 |
| 1 | 516.043s | 0 |
| 2 | 9.273s | 399872 |
| 3 | 3.953s | 399872 |

After the fix, all four warm requests retain the long prefix and only schedule the small tail prefill:

| warm request | TTFT | scheduler first computed tokens | scheduled prefill tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 7.973s | 399872 | 255 |
| 1 | 7.969s | 399872 | 255 |
| 2 | 7.965s | 399872 | 255 |
| 3 | 4.459s | 399872 | 255 |

Root cause: the DeepSeek V4 MLA prefix-cache prompt-block protection cap was effectively sized for about two long prompts, independent of `max_num_seqs`. In a C=4 / ~400K prefix-cache workload, the oldest long prefix could be evicted; losing an early block makes the longest-prefix match fall back to zero and turns the warm request into a full prefill again.

Fix: pass scheduler `max_num_seqs` into the KV cache manager and scale the DeepSeek MLA prompt protection cap with the configured sequence limit when capacity permits, while preserving one max-length request worth of allocation headroom. Direct unit-test construction without scheduler config keeps the previous conservative behavior.

Validation run:

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q`: 83 passed
- `ruff check` on the changed KV/scheduler/test files: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- Same GB10 C=4 / ~400K warm-prefix repro: exit 0, no CUDA/NCCL/NVRM/UVM/Xid errors observed in the run logs / current boot logs

This does not change the expected cold-round behavior: with this reduced profile, cold C=4 long prefills are still mostly serialized by the token budget. The improvement is specifically that the warm prefix-cache round no longer has a single pathological full-prefill request dragging the batch down.

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-09T16:07:27Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4661661976)

Thanks for the detailed repro and recipe. I think this was a real streaming parser boundary bug rather than a kernel/perf issue.

The existing DeepSeek V4 reasoning parser already treated a complete `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` marker as an implicit end of reasoning when the model skipped `</think>`, but it did not handle the marker itself being split across text deltas. In your example, the first chunk could expose `<｜DSML｜tool` as reasoning, and the next chunk would only expose `_calls>` as content/tool-call text, which matches the broken opencode display.

I pushed a fix in `21a54eacf6a` that buffers partial DSML tool-call marker prefixes until the next delta disambiguates them. If the next delta completes the marker, the parser emits the full marker as content/tool-call text; if it does not, the buffered text is released as normal reasoning.

Validation run on the SM120 workstation vLLM env:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/reasoning/test_deepseekv3_reasoning_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_deepseekv4_reasoning_parser.py -q
24 passed

.venv/bin/python -m ruff check vllm/reasoning/deepseek_v4_reasoning_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_deepseekv4_reasoning_parser.py
All checks passed
```

The new tests include the exact two-delta split shape (`<｜DSML｜tool` + `_calls>`) and a three-delta split. Please try the latest PR head when you get a chance; if it still happens, the next useful artifact would be the raw streamed chunks around the first malformed tool call.

I reran the missing RTX PRO 6000 x2 EP on/off data before changing the recommendation. The PR description is now updated with the new RTX and GB10 data.

Short version: for current SM120/SM121 performance deployments, the default recommendation is now **expert parallel disabled**. Keep EP as an explicit A/B or correctness-conservative fallback, not the default.

RTX PRO 6000 x2, TP=2, MTP=2, FP8 KV, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.975`, `max_num_batched_tokens=4096`, `max_num_seqs=24`, prefix cache disabled for raw measurement, FlashInfer autotune enabled, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`:

| C | EP off output tok/s | EP on output tok/s | EP-off delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 179.29 | 172.21 | +4.1% |
| 2 | 283.65 | 273.56 | +3.7% |
| 4 | 427.74 | 408.20 | +4.8% |
| 8 | 597.27 | 574.29 | +4.0% |
| 16 | 824.60 | 794.36 | +3.8% |
| 24 | 959.00 | 925.09 | +3.7% |

RTX random prefill, C=1, output len 128:

| Prompt / output tokens | EP off input tok/s | EP on input tok/s | EP-off delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4K / 128 | 3135.69 | 3156.84 | -0.7% |
| 16K / 128 | 6176.81 | 6099.21 | +1.3% |
| 64K / 128 | 7053.52 | 6863.31 | +2.8% |

I also added a same-protocol GSM8K limit-200 A/B on RTX because deployment recommendations should not be based on throughput alone:

| EP mode | flexible exact match | strict exact match | Gate result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| off | 0.955 | 0.935 | pass |
| on | 0.965 | 0.955 | pass |

So the recommendation is deliberately nuanced: EP-off is the performance default, but EP-on remains a correctness-conservative fallback until a broader correctness gate confirms there is no meaningful no-EP drift.

GB10 x2 data also supports MP + EP-off as the default. The reduced forum #53 prefix-cache pressure proxy rerun passed 12/12 with max TTFT 130.15669s, ITL p99 0.101422s, prefix cache hits 3,115,008, zero preemptions, and zero driver signals.

- SeedSource · comment · 2026-06-12T19:52:03Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4694769701)

Same-day results, as committed. TL;DR: **your selector probe works — FLASHMLA_SPARSE is selected on all four GB10s — and it exposed the next blocker, which sits upstream of the sparse runtime: DSA indexer weight loading under NVFP4.**

**Setup (disclosure up front):** we cherry-picked your selector commit 7224e684 onto our pinned environment (`nightly-aarch64` @ 42fcb680, commit 43914dd) rather than building your full branch — it's 139 commits ahead of our pin and the selector change is self-contained (`supports_compute_capability` [9,10] → [9,10,12]); overlay engagement verified in-log before launch. If the full branch handles anything below differently, say the word and we'll build it outright. Single-node wasn't possible: the REAP-pruned checkpoint is 320 GB against 128 GB unified per GB10 — so this is the TP=4 leg only (4x GB10, ray, verified RoCE).

**Result 1 — selector gate clears.** All four workers:
```
INFO [cuda.py:378] Using FLASHMLA_SPARSE attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHMLA_SPARSE']
INFO [selector.py:163] Using FLASH_ATTN MLA prefill backend.
```
The CC gate was the only selector-level obstacle for this shape (head_size=576, use_mla=True, use_sparse=True, BF16 KV) on sm_121.

**Result 2 — the FlashMLA sparse runtime path was never reached.** Weight loading fails first:
```
ray.exceptions.RayTaskError(KeyError): ray::RayWorkerProc.initialize_worker()
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 1739, in load_weights
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py", line 368/301/274, in load_weights/_load_module
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 1448, in load_weights
KeyError: 'layers.0.self_attn.indexer.wk_weights_proj.input_global_scale'
```
Our read: this NVFP4 checkpoint (0xSero/GLM-5.1-555B-NVFP4, REAP-pruned, modelopt-style) **quantizes the lightning-indexer projections** — `input_global_scale` tensors exist in the checkpoint — while the GLM/DSA model path builds the indexer unquantized, so the scale key has no destination parameter at `params_dict[name]`. Looks like the indexer modules need quant-config awareness (either honored exclude/ignore handling for this checkpoint family, or NVFP4-capable indexer linears) before anyone with an NVFP4 GLM checkpoint can exercise your sparse path.

So the sequence on SM121 now looks like: ~~selector gate~~ (your probe) → **indexer NVFP4 loading (current blocker)** → sparse runtime (your anticipated Triton-fallback question — still untested).

Full head log (690 lines, includes selector/backend lines and complete trace) available — happy to attach or gist. Standing offer unchanged: we'll run any follow-up branch same-day on this 4-node setup, and can also test against a BF16/unquantized-indexer variant if you point us at the expected checkpoint layout.

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-13T18:55:45Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4699471510)

@epheien Thanks for the report.

I traced this to the strict tool-calling structural-tag grammar for DeepSeek V4 chat-mode outputs. In your log, the rejected token sequence `[16, 128822]` decodes as `.</think>`. The prompt in chat mode already ends the thinking section, but the model can occasionally emit an extra `</think>` before entering normal content/tool-call output. After the rebase, xgrammar's DeepSeek V4 non-reasoning structural tag excluded `</think>`, so the scheduler treated that otherwise harmless extra close tag as a grammar violation and terminated the request.

I pushed a narrow fix in `531807c34bf73f6ef095f203486e12dadfbdadb2`: for DeepSeek V4 non-reasoning strict tool-calling only, allow a stray `</think>` while still rejecting `<think>` and leaving the reasoning-mode structural tag unchanged.

Verified with:
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py -q`
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_deepseekv4_reasoning_parser.py -q`
- an xgrammar matcher check for `.</think>` and `.</think><｜DSML｜tool_calls>\n`

Please rebuild/redeploy the latest PR head and retry. If it still reproduces, please share the launch args around `--tool-call-parser`, `--reasoning-parser`, `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING`, and MTP/spec decode settings.

- sonny-vleisides · comment · 2026-06-14T23:14:27Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4703384643)

Got the Jun 14 head (f031e4206d) up on a pair of RTX PRO 6000 cards, TP=2. A few things in case they help...

Build snag first: pip pulled flashinfer 0.6.12 but the base image I'm on still shipped flashinfer-jit-cache 0.6.11.post2, so the workers died at startup at version check. Pinning flashinfer-jit-cache to 0.6.12+cu130 from the cu130 wheel index fixed it. I didn't need the DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK escape hatch.

Long-context prefill is MUCH better than the last head I'd measured (c37f7357, back in May). Same shape as your bench: MTP=2, prefix cache off, max_num_batched_tokens=4096, max_model_len=131072, max_tokens=64, TTFT averaged over 2*C sequential requests. At ~65k tokens I'm getting about 14.4s at C=1 and 43.4s at C=4. At ~130k it's roughly 27.3 / 57.0 / 97.7s for C=1/2/4, againnst about 41.4 / 59.1 / 124.0 on c37f7357. So 130k is the big mover, roughly a third faster at C=1. Zero failures, and whatever was dragging prefill on the early-June heads isn't showing up for me here. Good stuff.

Prefix caching held up well too. I ran five back-to-back rounds of 2 sessions x 3 turns of ~800-word concurrent prompts at 16k context... prefix cache on with MTP=1, and concurrent hit rate stayed around 82-83% every trial. Back in May on the c92696943 line I was stuck near 55% multi-trial, so the retention fix is clearly making SM120 happy.

Decode's about where you said, ~176 tok/s at C=1 with MTP=2 vs the ~179 you posted.

One rough edge still there: When I drop the cap (--max-num-seqs 256) and hit it with ~48 concurrent distinct long prompts... it wedges. Requests quit coming back, health eventually 503s, and the engine core is parked in 'RPC call to sample_tokens timed out' (shm_broadcast timeout). GPUs stay responsive, and it recovers on a plain container restart, so it's not a bus/GSP fault. However... holding max-num-seqs at 32 sidesteps it entirely. Flagging since it still repros at this head for me on 2x WS Edition TP=2.

Output looked clean otherwise. I'm happy to throw more at it from this box if it's useful.

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-15T20:02:39Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4711947218)

Thanks @sonny-vleisides — and glad the flashinfer-jit-cache pin sorted it. I'll add a short docs note so others installing into a pre-existing image keep the three flashinfer packages (`flashinfer-python` / `flashinfer-cubin` / `flashinfer-jit-cache`) on the same version; good that upstream/main is already on 0.6.12.

Your reading matches mine: the moderate / steady-state concurrent case is handled by the 05-31/06-01 prefill–decode fairness scheduling — on my 2× RTX PRO 6000 (TP=2) the uncapped C=48 moderate load drains cleanly too.

For the narrow case that still wedges (a big simultaneous set of distinct ~65–130k prefills at `max-num-seqs 256`), two things:

**1. There's an existing dynamic admission guard worth trying: `--watermark`** (default `0.0` = off). It reserves a fraction of KV blocks that must stay free and gates only *new* WAITING/PREEMPTED admissions (`required_blocks + watermark_blocks > free_blocks`) — in-flight decodes bypass it, and since it's block-count based, high-concurrency *short* traffic never trips it. On my 2× RTX it clearly improved the over-subscribed long-context behavior: KV stopped pegging ~93%, much less preempt/recompute churn, and far more requests completed instead of stalling. Could you try `--watermark 0.1` on your 48×(65–130k) repro, keeping `reserve-full-isl` on (i.e. *don't* pass `--no-scheduler-reserve-full-isl`)? The goal is that the overflow prefills queue and drain rather than all being admitted at once.

**2. On "beyond TP=2 capacity vs. a regression":** 48 × (65–130k) ≈ 3–6M prefill tokens against ~130k of KV on 2× RTX, so it genuinely can't all be admitted at once — a guard is the right model. But whether it should *cleanly queue* vs. *wedge* is exactly your question. I haven't been able to reproduce the hard 503 on my pair — my over-subscribed long-context runs stay healthy (just slower) — so a **py-spy stack of the wedge would be decisive**: ranks deadlocked / all parked on one `sample_tokens` (or an all-reduce) ⇒ a real bug to bisect across `ecb7466…f031e42`; ranks making slow progress under KV exhaustion ⇒ capacity, and `--watermark` is the answer. If it looks like a regression I'm glad to help bisect that range.

Thanks for the careful repro — this is really helpful.


- sonny-vleisides · comment · 2026-06-16T04:26:45Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4714979532)

Jasl, I ran your wedge case on a pair of RTX PRO 6000... TP=2, on the `f031e42`-era head.  48 distinct ~100k-token prefills fired at once... at MTP=1, `scheduler_reserve_full_isl` left on (the default). py-spy was decisive, and it points at JIT compilation rather than a collective deadlock.

During the stall (both GPUs at 0% util, ~290 W), both TP workers are in Triton compilation and EngineCore is parked waiting on them:

Worker_TP0 / Worker_TP1:
    make_llir (triton/backends/nvidia/compiler.py:417)
    ...
    accumulate_indexed_d512_split_sparse_mla_attention (sparse_mla_kernels.py:1930)
    _forward_sparse_mla_prefill_triton (deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py:673)
    forward_mqa -> attention_impl -> ... -> worker_busy_loop (multiproc_executor.py:982)

EngineCore:
    sched_yield (distributed/utils.py:48)
    acquire_read (distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py:698)
    get_response (v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py:387)
    step_with_batch_queue (v1/engine/core.py:568)

About 20 s later both GPUs jump to 100% util (~485 W), TP0 in the sparse-MLA prefill kernel, TP1 in FP8 MoE... and it drains, just slowly (3 of 48 done in 78 s, zero errors). So no sample_tokens collective deadlock here... it's a first-use Triton JIT compile of the D512 split sparse-MLA prefill kernel for this long-prefill shape... which blocks the engine step (EngineCore sits in shm_broadcast acquire_read waiting on the compiling workers) and surfaces exactly as the "RPC call to sample_tokens timed out" symptom. Once compiled, it's genuinely capacity-bound (48×100k vs ~1.4x KV at 131k).

That probably explains why the hard 503 doesn't repro on your pair... if that kernel/shape is already compiled (warm), you skip the first-use stall. On my side this shape never shows up under steady traffic, so the kernel hadn't
compiled even after ~30 h uptime, and the first 48×long burst pays the full autotuned compile.

This reads like a warmup coverage gap on the D512 split sparse-MLA prefill kernel in long-prefill shapes, plus the expected capacity tail once it's compiled. Happy to try watermark 0.1 for the capacity tail next (won't touch the compile stall), and to test a warmup extension covering this kernel/shape... if you want to point me at one. Full stacks available if useful.

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-16T16:35:17Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4721067837)

### Update: rebased onto upstream + long-prefill wedge fix

Rebased the branch onto current upstream and added a fix for the first-long-prefill wedge seen in testing (EngineCore parked in `shm_broadcast` -> "sample_tokens RPC timed out"). Root cause: the D512-split sparse-MLA **prefill** Triton kernels JIT-compiled inside the engine step on the first long request (~20s). The fix pre-compiles them at startup (env `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_WARMUP`, default on); the first long prefill now compiles **0** of them in-inference (was 12), verified on SM120 and SM121.

**Performance:** the gated SM120 decode optimization (`VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE=1`) gives **+6% to +32%** decode throughput (C=1->64) on 2x RTX PRO 6000, matching the community target (~2815 tok/s @C64); GSM8K-500 unchanged (0.946/0.93).

**Dependency (only for the decode optimization):** the gate requires FlashInfer **git-main (>=0.6.13)** for `flashinfer.mla._sparse_mla_sm120`:

```bash
pip install --upgrade "flashinfer-python @ git+https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer.git"
# if flashinfer-cubin lags the wheel: export FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1
```

**No update required for the default path:** with the gate off (default) the import is lazy/gated, so **FlashInfer 0.6.12 (official) works unchanged**. The wedge fix is fully orthogonal (imports no FlashInfer). Full data + per-platform tables are in the updated PR description.

Jasl, I rebuilt your latest head (73e99c16) on my RTX PRO 6000, TP=2 & re-ran the same test... 48 distinct ~100k token prompts fired at once. The warmup fix does the job.  *Nice*

At startup both workers log:

```
Warming up DeepSeek V4 D512-split sparse-MLA prefill kernels for combined_topk widths=[256, 384, 512, 640] (heads=32, padded_q_heads=64)
```
and on the first big burst py-spy doesn't catch them stuck in `make_llir` on `accumulate_indexed_d512_split_sparse_mla_attention` anymore. It's just running the kernel (`finish_sparse_mla_attention_with_sink`), and the GPUs sit at 100% util where the old head was pinned at 0% for ~20s.  So that prefill compile isn't blocking the engine step now.

Couple things I noticed... The first long burst still eats some in-inference compilation, just spread across a bunch of smaller kernels instead of the one big autotuned one. py-spy caught both workers in `make_cubin` on `fp8_mqa_logits_triton` (through `sparse_attn_indexer`), with EngineCore parked back in `shm_broadcast` `acquire_read`. Your `jit_monitor` flagged the whole set this run:

```
_fp8_mqa_logits_kernel
_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_rowwise_kernel
_build_prefill_chunk_metadata_kernel
_compute_prefill_metadata_kernel
_deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum_kernel
_combine_topk_swa_indices_kernel
_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_kernel
_w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm
_mtp_shared_head_rmsnorm_kernel
eagle_prepare_next_token_padded_kernel
rejection_greedy_sample_kernel
_indexed_d512_split_score_kernel
_indexed_d512_split_stats_kernel
_indexed_d512_split_value_kernel
_accumulate_indexed_attention_chunk_multihead_kernel
```
So the big stall is gone but the long-prefill path still has a shorter compile tail before it's fully warm. The monitor pretty much hands you the list to extend warmup over.

Other thing worth mentioning... this head wants a bit more memory than the early-June one. At `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92` it bailed during KV sizing (3.79 GiB needed vs 3.57 available for a 131072 request)... and wouldn't start. Bumping to 0.96 was fine, ~286k token KV pool. Could be the warmup workspace, could be something else, just thought that might be meaningful to share.

Past the compile it's the capacity story you'd expect (48x100k against ~1.4-2.2x KV so it drains slow)... nothing surprising there. Bottom line, the thing I reported is fixed. Can send the full py-spy dumps or the monitor log if that would be of help.

> So this does not look like the earlier hard hang/OOM class. It looked more like a bad decode/output-quality event under concurrent long-context agent traffic. Not sure yet whether this is model behavior, prefix-cache interaction, tokenizer/parser behavior, or a decode kernel issue. If there is a useful debug flag to capture enough signal without logging full prompts, I can run with it and try to catch a cleaner repro.

Sorry for the bad generation, I've located the root cause, and I'm fixing now

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-18T12:34:26Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4741971758)

### 2026-06-18 — correctness fixes + breakable cudagraph re-enabled on SM121

Rebased onto current upstream (`1e9f04da14`); head is now `ccf4c0788e` (PR body updated). Highlights of this round:

**Correctness**
- **jasl/vllm#19 (instruction-following).** Root cause: on SM12x the indexer prefill top-k wrote a contiguous `[M, select_k]` result into a non-contiguous `out[:, :select_k]` slice when the compressed-KV count was below the index-topk width (short / early-query prompts) — corrupting later rows → all-`(-1)` top-k → the C4A prefill dropped the compressed context → prose preamble instead of the requested JSON. Fixed by staging into a contiguous buffer. The exact repro now returns clean JSON-only.
- **Breakable-cudagraph garbage on trivial prompts** (`2+2=`, `2+2等于几`, `capital of France`). This was upstream #45309 ("reduce `eager_break_during_capture`"), which let DeepSeek-V4's metadata-dependent attention be captured into the cudagraph. Upstream reverted it in #45972; rebasing onto current upstream picks that up, restoring the full `@eager_break_during_capture` split → correct generation on both SM120 and SM121. (Caught because the regression only showed on bare/short prompts — GSM8K's longer prompts masked it.)
- GSM8K 8-shot greedy **0.96 / 0.96** (RTX SM120 nc=8, GB10 SM121 nc=4); long-context coherence **8/8** (8 concurrent, 280-line recall); trivial-prompt arithmetic clean on both platforms.

**Breakable cudagraph re-enabled on SM121**
- The SM121 carve-out — added specifically for the trivial-prompt garbage above — is dropped, so breakable cudagraph now auto-enables for DeepSeek-V4 on all SM12x. With #45309 reverted it generates correctly on SM121, and on GB10 (EP off, random 2048-in/128-out, c4) it is on-par-or-slightly-faster than `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`: **38.5 vs 36.7** out tok/s, **74.0 vs 76.96** ms mean TPOT.

**Decode optimization** (gated `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE=1`, FlashInfer git-main): unchanged — the decode CUDA kernel is byte-identical across the rebase, **+6–32%** aggregate decode tok/s at C=1→64 on RTX SM120. The default path needs no FlashInfer update.

Validated on 2× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) and 2-node GB10 / DGX Spark (SM121), DeepSeek-V4-Flash, fp8 KV, expert-parallel off. Stable pin: `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260618`.


- jasl · comment · 2026-06-18T12:38:03Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4742000095)

@sonny-vleisides thanks for rebuilding and confirming — glad the D512-split warmup killed the `make_llir` stall on `accumulate_indexed_d512_split_sparse_mla_attention`.

On your two follow-ups:

**The shorter JIT tail.** Correct — the warmup currently pre-compiles only the D512-split sparse-MLA *prefill* kernels, so the in-inference compiles you caught (`fp8_mqa_logits_triton` via `sparse_attn_indexer`, the prefill-metadata kernels, etc.) aren't covered yet. The warmup uses a synthetic direct-kernel-warm — it calls each kernel with throwaway tensors at the reachable shape specializations — and that same pattern extends cleanly to the indexer + metadata kernels; your `jit_monitor` list is effectively the warm-set, so thanks for the dump. Extending the warmup over those (the indexer logits kernel is the main one that parks the engine step) is a tractable follow-up — tracked, not in this PR yet.

**Memory.** I can rule out the warmup workspace as the cause: it allocates only throwaway tensors (never the shared workspace manager) and frees them before serving, so it does not raise the steady-state KV-sizing floor. I haven't isolated the exact per-component source of the higher floor vs early-June on RTX — the likely contributors are the decode-path workspace reservation and the upstream-rebase changes — but it isn't the warmup. So `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.96` is the right setting on this head.

Heads-up: the branch has since moved to `ccf4c0788e` (rebased onto current upstream, plus the jasl/vllm#19 instruction-following fix and an upstream breakable-cudagraph correctness revert — see the latest PR comment). Your warmup findings carry over unchanged.


- jasl · comment · 2026-06-18T12:38:05Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4742000300)

@arthur-drozdov thanks — both of your reports are addressed/characterized on the current head (`ccf4c0788e`, rebased onto current upstream):

**Mixed-script / gibberish output.** I codified your repro as a long-context coherence gate in the test harness — N concurrent long-context requests with a non-Latin-fraction detector — and on the current base it passes 8/8 (8 concurrent, 280-line recall prompt): no mixed-script gibberish reproduced. It's now a standing regression gate. (Separately, the short-prompt instruction-following corruption tracked as jasl/vllm#19 was root-caused and fixed — a non-contiguous indexer top-k write; the fix is platform-agnostic.)

**Decode-concurrency collapse (your `llama-benchy` tables).** Reproduced and root-caused on a 2-node GB10 measurement of the current base (EP off; I capped at ≤32k depth / ≤c5 to stay out of the 65k×c10 OOM-wedge regime you hit):

- Single-stream (c1) decode is flat-healthy at every depth (~38 ms TPOT from 128 → 32k) — matches your "c1 fine at all depths".
- TPOT balloons super-linearly with concurrency at high depth (16k×c5 ≈ 320 ms, 32k×c5 ≈ 596 ms), so aggregate decode collapses — matches your c2/c5 high-depth rows.
- Root cause: the **eager O(batch × context) sparse indexer** (the fp8 paged-MQA-logits + top-k computed over the full context for every concurrent decode token, each step) — a decode-time compute bottleneck, not KV-pool exhaustion or scheduler-config. Config knobs (`max-num-batched-tokens`, watermark, `max-num-seqs`) were swept and don't move it.
- The decode-protection scheduling in this PR (`_limit_mixed_decode_prefill_chunk`, which your May base predated) gives graceful degradation — every cell completed, zero aborts, no catastrophic wedge in this regime — but it doesn't eliminate the slowdown.

So it's a real issue with a clear root cause; the fix is a code change (cheapen / cudagraph-capture the eager indexer), which is scoped but out of scope for this min-enable PR. Single-stream and moderate-concurrency serving are healthy.

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-19T01:49:59Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4747676393)

@DerAndereAndi Thanks — that config pins it. The culprit is one env var:

```
VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE: "1"   <-- remove this
```

`VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE` forces the experimental **B12X** fused-MoE experts. B12X is a Blackwell **NVFP4** kernel and it's deliberately kept out of auto-selection on SM121 (there's an unresolved CUTLASS SM121 MMA-op guard) — so it's opt-in only and not stable there yet. But `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` is an **MXFP4** checkpoint (`expert_dtype="fp4"`), so forcing the NVFP4 B12X experts onto MXFP4 weights gives mismatched layouts/buffers, and the experts kernel walks off its allocation — exactly the async `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` you saw surfacing in `_forward_fused_moe -> self.experts`.

Note that `VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE` doesn't even exist on the PR branch (`codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable`) — it only lives on a separate B12X experiment branch — so it sounds like the image was built from that branch. 

Fix:

1. Build the image from the current head of the PR branch (`codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable`), not the B12X branch.
2. Drop `VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE: "1"` from `environment:`. Leave everything else as-is.

With that, the MXFP4 MoE auto-selects the stable `flashinfer_cutlass` path (no flag needed). Your other env vars (`VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN`, `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`, `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS`, the NCCL/IB block) and your `vllm serve` args are all fine and can stay.

Bonus: the current PR head also has two fixes that land right on your configuration (MTP2 + prefix-caching + long context + concurrency): a cudagraph spec-decode fix (was producing garbled output under MTP2 at high concurrency) and a prefix-cache write-completion fence (was dropping the most-recent long-context content under concurrent requests). So updating is worth it beyond just the crash.

One unrelated heads-up: `--max-model-len 500000` is past the model's native context — you've allowed it with `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1`, which is fine for KV sizing, but quality may degrade beyond the trained length. Not related to this crash.

- tobymao · comment · 2026-06-19T04:55:57Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4748612089)

**`99a22d0e4` flips the SM121 breakable-cudagraph default off→on and regresses our 2×GB10 MTP decode**

`99a22d0e4` removes the SM121 carve-out from `4d362c2c1`, so breakable cudagraph now auto-enables for DeepSeek-V4 on SM121. On our deployment that default flip drops decode throughput substantially.

Setup: 2× GB10 (SM121, TP=2), DeepSeek-V4-Flash, MTP (`num_speculative_tokens=2`), `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `max-num-seqs 4`, 500k ctx. Decode tok/s, single stream, 2 runs each:

| max_tokens | breakable on (new default) | `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` (prior default) |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | 31-32 | 40 |
| 600 | 23-28 | 41-42 |
| 800 | 19-21 | 39-40 |

Two things stand out: breakable-on **degrades as output grows** while breakable-off stays **flat** at the same lengths (so it's not a generic length effect — it's specific to the breakable path), and these breakable-on numbers are well under the on-par 38.5-vs-36.7 in the commit. Output is correct and a compound-path corruption probe is clean both ways. We're running with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` to restore throughput. Happy to share a full repro.
