- jasl · comment · 2026-06-19T08:35:25Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4749908299)

@1zilc Thanks for the report. The log you pasted is the **APIServer** side (`EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue`) — the actual crash stack lives in the **worker** process (`Worker_TP*` / EngineCore) log, which isn't in the paste. Could you grab that part? It's what names the failing kernel/op.

That said, two things in your setup are the most likely cause:

1. **You replaced the image's FlashInfer with git main:**
   ```
   pip install --upgrade "flashinfer-python @ git+https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer.git"
   ```
   `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE=1` selects the SM120 sparse-MLA decode runner built against the **specific** FlashInfer the image pins (the PR#3395 kernel). FlashInfer main has moved past that API, so the override can mismatch the kernel — which is also consistent with the endless `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` recompiles in your log. Please drop that line and use the FlashInfer the `ccf4c07` image already ships.

2. **The config is right at the memory edge:** `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95` + `--max-num-seqs 16` + `--max-model-len 512k` + `--enable-expert-parallel` drove `GPU KV cache usage: 98.2%` immediately before the death. Try `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` and a smaller `--max-num-seqs` (4–8) for headroom.

If it still dies after (1) using the pinned FlashInfer and (2) backing off the memory knobs, post the **worker** stack trace and I'll dig into the specific kernel.


- jasl · comment · 2026-06-19T08:35:27Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4749908554)

@tobymao Thanks — this is a precise report, and the degrade-with-length vs flat split is exactly the breakable-cudagraph signature.

What's happening: `99a22d0e4` re-enables breakable cudagraph for DeepSeek-V4 on SM121, and breakable mode also **disables the torch.compile pipeline** (it's equivalent to `-O.mode=none`) and runs the attention eagerly every decode step. So you lose inductor fusion and pay an un-captured per-step cost that accumulates with output length, while full-capture + compile stays flat — which matches your table.

Why it's on: under **MTP + high concurrency + long context**, the DSv4 per-token sparse-MLA attention captured into one FULL graph cross-contaminates concurrent requests (garbled output); eager-breaking that attention under spec-decode is the current fix. So it's a genuine correctness-vs-throughput tradeoff. For a single-stream / low-concurrency deployment like yours, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` is the right setting — correct and faster, as you found.

It was re-enabled expecting a perf win on GB10, so your data (it's a regression for MTP decode) is exactly what's needed. I'm going to look at (a) whether the default should be off, with breakable documented as the high-concurrency-correctness setting, and (b) whether that high-concurrency fix can be done without giving up torch.compile (e.g. a piecewise-capture path that keeps compile on). Thanks for the clear numbers.


- jasl · comment · 2026-06-19T09:54:59Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4750493503)

@tobymao Update: I went with your finding. The current PR head now **defaults DeepSeek-V4 to FULL_AND_PIECEWISE + torch.compile (no breakable-cudagraph auto-enable)** on both SM120 and SM121 — because I measured the same regression on RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) too, not just GB10:

| max_tokens | breakable ON | breakable OFF (new default) |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | ~103 tok/s | ~160 |
| 600 | ~55 | ~175 |
| 800 | ~45 | ~172 |

So after you update, you get the fast path by default and can **drop `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`** (it's the default now). Correctness on the new default is clean (GSM8K-200 0.96, long-context concurrent recall 64/64, bare prompts fine). Breakable stays available as an opt-in (`VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`) for the MTP + long-context + high-concurrency correctness case. Thanks again — your numbers are exactly what nailed this down.


- arthur-drozdov · comment · 2026-06-19T13:53:48Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4752158639)

Another datapoint from dual DGX Spark (2x GB10 / SM121, TP=2) on current head `e92d21ef8d38`.

A real agentic workload with prompts around 150k tokens is reporting client-side throughput around:

```text
Input:  1440 tok/s
Output: 0.943 tok/s
```

I captured the server metrics to separate actual decode speed from the prefill-dominated end-to-end number.

Runtime/config:

```text
vllm: 20260613.dev331+ge92d21ef8.d20260619
torch: 2.11.0+cu130
flashinfer: 0.6.13 (image-pinned)
nccl: 2.30.7
model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
tp=2 over Ray
max_model_len=300000
max_num_seqs=2
max_num_batched_tokens=4096
gpu_memory_utilization=0.85
kv_cache_dtype=fp8
block_size=256
prefix caching enabled
FULL_AND_PIECEWISE + torch.compile (new default; no breakable override)
VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE=1
MTP/speculative disabled
```

Prometheus delta covering four completed requests:

```text
avg request prompt tokens:            149,944.5
avg generated tokens:                     307.25
avg prefill KV-computed tokens:         62,520.5
avg request prefill time:                  52.78 s
avg request decode time:                   11.85 s
avg E2E latency:                            64.88 s
avg request queue time:                     0.000017 s
avg TPOT:                                   38.71 ms  (~25.8 tok/s decode)
preemptions:                                 0
```

So the sub-1 tok/s client number is not the steady decode kernel rate: once decode starts, it is around 25-26 tok/s. It is output tokens amortized over a very long prefill/TTFT.

One particularly clear request admitted a 149,740-token prefix query with zero cache hits. It took roughly two minutes from admission to completion and produced 311 tokens. During that interval:

```text
Running=1, Waiting=0
GPU utilization: ~96% on the active samples
KV cache usage: ~29-37%
no preemptions
no CUDA/NCCL/Xid/OOM errors
no active clock throttling
RDMA links up, no link errors
```

The vLLM logger also went quiet for about 110 seconds during that long prefill, then reported:

```text
Avg prompt throughput: 14974.5 tok/s, generation: 5.3 tok/s
10 seconds later: prompt 0, generation 25.8 tok/s, request complete
```

The burst logger value therefore overstates effective wall-clock prefill throughput; the per-request histogram gives about 1.2k KV-computed tok/s for these recent requests, close to the client observation.

Is this prefill/TTFT range expected for dual GB10 at ~150k context, or should the adaptive/chunked D512 prefill path with `max_num_batched_tokens=4096` be making better wall-time progress? Happy to collect a specific trace/counter if useful.

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-19T16:28:07Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4753277732)

**This round's fixes are on the PR head now** (tag `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260620`), validated on 2× RTX PRO 6000 / SM120 and 2-node GB10 / SM121. cc @arthur-drozdov @tobymao @DerAndereAndi @1zilc

- **Breakable-cudagraph now defaults OFF again** for DeepSeek-V4 on SM12x (@tobymao). The 2026-06-18 head had re-enabled it, and it was regressing MTP decode (degrading as output length grew), so `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` is the default again and decode is restored. `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` is no longer needed (`=1` still opts in).
- **MTP + long-context + high-concurrency recall/garble fix** (@arthur-drozdov). DeepSeek-V4's *writable* sliding-window caches weren't copy-on-write'd for spec decode, so a shared final prefix-cache block could be written-while-read under concurrent identical-prefix traffic → corrupted the KV the sparse-MLA decode reads → dropped most-recent "needle" (or occasional mixed-script output). Fixed in the KV-cache coordinator. Long-context coherence is now **64/64 on SM120 and GB10** (was ~9% miss); GSM8K 0.965/0.97, tool-call 89%, jasl/vllm#19 still passing, decode throughput unchanged.
- Plus a prefix-cache write-completion fence.

Config notes for the recent crash reports:
- **@DerAndereAndi** — the illegal-memory-access is `VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE=1` forcing experimental NVFP4 B12X experts onto the MXFP4 model (unstable on SM12x). Drop that env and run the PR branch as-is.
- **@1zilc** — `gpu-memory-utilization 0.95` + `max-model-len 512k` + `max-num-seqs 16` + expert-parallel drives the KV cache to ~98% (it's in your log) — that's the likely OOM. Try `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` and/or a lower `--max-num-seqs` / `--max-model-len`.

FlashInfer (only relevant if you enable `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE=1`): if you want a newer FlashInfer, install it correctly — `pip uninstall -y flashinfer-jit-cache` first, then install matching `flashinfer-python` + `flashinfer-cubin` (e.g. the `0.6.13.dev20260619` nightly). A bare `pip install --upgrade flashinfer-python` leaves `flashinfer-cubin` / `flashinfer-jit-cache` stale, and FlashInfer then raises a version-mismatch error at startup (and re-JITs kernels).

@arthur-drozdov — your ~150k-prefill / TTFT datapoint is a separate (perf) topic, not part of this batch; I'll follow up on it separately.

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-20T07:41:24Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4756883416)

**This round (rebased onto current `upstream/main`) — highlights**

- **Long-context garble on SM12x fixed (packed-KV int32 overflow).** The fused KV layout on main makes the indexer KV block stride large; the SM12x paged-MQA-logits kernels did `block_idx * stride` in int32 → overflow past 2³¹ at high block ids → IMA on SM120 / wrong-memory garble on SM121. Both (rowwise + non-rowwise) kernels now compute the block offset in int64. (conc=1 only exercised the rowwise path; conc=8 exposed the non-rowwise one.)
- **FlashMLA prefill combine: per-request compressed top-k** — fixes a latent multi-request prefill correctness bug (non-first prefill requests read stale workspace; no-op at a single prefill).
- **New opt-in prefill switch `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL=1` (default off).** Routes prefill through the packed FlashInfer sparse-MLA SM120 path; defers to the default FlashMLA indexed-D512 prefill when off. It shares the decode gate's `_sparse_mla_sm120` kernels, so it has the **same FlashInfer version requirement** (main / 0.6.13) — one shared build, no separate version for prefill.

**Validation** (GB10 2-node / SM121, MTP=2): long-context coherence **68/68** (8-concurrent), GSM8K-200 **0.965**, prefix-cache restored (42–46% hit). llama-benchy: prefill **1595–1722 tok/s** at depth, decode **40 tok/s @ C=1 holding 38–42 out to 32K**.

**Prefill perf — and how the packed switch relates to the default `INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS=4096` gate.** The default FlashMLA prefill is unchanged this round (the fixes above are correctness). The packed switch and that 4096 gate are **mutually-exclusive routes, not additive**: enabling the packed switch *bypasses* the FlashMLA indexed-D512 split path **and its 4096 gate** entirely (an `if/else` over the same sparse-MLA prefill). So the trade-off is **context-dependent**:

- **Short/medium prefill (4–8k):** the packed +7.5% (2026-06-17 A/B @ 8k, N=10) was measured against a baseline using the *old 8192* gate, where an 8k prefill did **not** take the split path. The current 4096 gate already routes that band to the split kernel (its own +9–59%, biggest at 4–8k) — so it likely captures most of the packed gain, and **gate-4096 may win** here. Net packed-over-gate-4096 is unproven; it needs a same-build *packed-ON vs gate-4096-default* A/B.
- **Long context (≥64k → 256K+):** the 4096 gate is **moot** (any long prefill clears it, so the FlashMLA baseline is *already* the split kernel) — so it's purely kernel quality. There the packed kernel shows a genuine, **growing** gain: ~+10% over the split at 64k (N=12) vs +7.5% at 8k, and the fork's hand-tuned kernel widens to +47% @ 64k vs +27% @ 8k (headroom). So the packed switch is fundamentally a **long-context** lever; its value should be judged at long context — we don't yet have a same-build >256K number.

Net: default-off is the right call until a same-build A/B — at long context specifically — shows the packed kernel beats the gate-4096 FlashMLA route.

- brianmiller · comment · 2026-06-20T19:17:25Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4759734864)

## GB10 TP=2 Benchmark — `88ec87e` (June 20)

Dual NVIDIA GB10 (Grace Blackwell, SM121), TP=2 over 200GbE RoCE, CUDA graphs `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, MTP=2, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`.

### Short-context (512 tok output, 5 requests per concurrency)

| Concurrency | tok/s | Mean latency |
|-------------|-------|-------------|
| C=1 | 40.56 | 12,528ms |
| C=2 | 56.51 | 15,477ms |
| C=4 | 69.59 | 22,155ms |

### Long-context (121K prompt tokens, warm prefix cache)

| Test | Time | tok/s |
|------|------|-------|
| 121K prefill C=1 (cached) | 5.5s | 35.30 |
| 121K cached C=2 | 5.5s / 11.0s | 33.6 / 18.0 |

### vs previous build (`5d1584e`, June 10)

| Metric | 5d1584e | 88ec87e | Delta |
|--------|---------|---------|-------|
| C=1 | 42.50 | 40.56 | −4.6% |
| C=2 | 56.63 | 56.51 | −0.2% |
| C=4 | 72.31 | 69.59 | −3.8% |
| 121K cached prefill | 9.2s | 5.5s | **−40%** |
| 121K cached C=2 | 9.2/11.1s | 5.5/11.0s | **−40% / −1%** |

Short-context decode is slightly slower (~3-5%), but prefix cache performance improved dramatically — 40% faster on cached 121K prompts. The MTP+prefix cache stability fixes (COW shared blocks, write-completion fence, int64 block offsets, eager-break cudagraph fix) are all working well. No crashes across the full benchmark suite.

Stable, running in production. Thank you @jasl!

services:

      - /home/andreas/.cache/tilelang:/cache/tilelang
      - /home/andreas/.cache/triton-ds4:/cache/triton
      - /home/andreas/.cache/torchinductor-ds4:/cache/torchinductor
      - /home/andreas/.cache/torch_extensions-ds4:/cache/torch_extensions
    environment:
      VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN: "1"
      VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE: "0"
      VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB: "256"
      VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH: "0"
      VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE: "1"
      VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL: "1"
      TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST: "12.1a"
      FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST: "12.1a"
      NCCL_NET: IB
      NCCL_IB_DISABLE: "0"
      NCCL_IB_HCA: "rocep1s0f1,roceP2p1s0f1"
      NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME: "enp1s0f1np1"
      NCCL_CROSS_NIC: "1"
      NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE: "0"
      NCCL_IGNORE_CPU_AFFINITY: "1"
      NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX: "2"
      NCCL_DEBUG: WARN
      VLLM_HOST_IP: "${LOCAL_IP}"
      GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME: "enp1s0f1np1"
      TP_SOCKET_IFNAME: "enp1s0f1np1"
      HF_HUB_OFFLINE: "1"
      TRITON_CACHE_DIR: "/cache/triton"
      TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR: "/cache/torchinductor"
      VLLM_CACHE_ROOT: "/cache/vllm"
      FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE: "/cache/flashinfer"
      TILELANG_CACHE_DIR: "/cache/tilelang"
      NODE_RANK: "${NODE_RANK}"
      HEADLESS: "${HEADLESS}"
      MASTER_ADDR: "${MASTER_ADDR}"
    command:
      - bash
      - -lc
      - >
        exec vllm serve
        /models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
        --served-model-name deepseek-v4-flash
        --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --trust-remote-code
        --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 1
        --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256
        --max-model-len 500000 --max-num-seqs 4
        --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80
        --enable-prefix-caching
        --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'
        --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4
        --distributed-executor-backend mp
        --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice
        --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4
        --reasoning-config '{"reasoning_parser":"deepseek_v4","reasoning_start_str":"<think>","reasoning_end_str":"</think"}'
        --enable-flashinfer-autotune
        --nnodes 2 --node-rank ${NODE_RANK}
        --master-addr ${MASTER_ADDR} --master-port 25000
```

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-22T12:36:08Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4768339342)

@DerAndereAndi @1zilc — thanks for the configs and logs. I tracked down and fixed **two distinct** long-context (256k+, MTP=2) crashes. Both land on a new pinned tag **`sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260622b`** (`5ba0f19f02`); the rest of the branch is unchanged from the 2026-06-21 audit head. Full details are under **Update 2026-06-22** in the PR description — summary:

**1. MTP draft-sampler float32 (most likely @DerAndereAndi's).** The MTP probabilistic draft sampler passed **bf16** draft-head logits into the Triton top-k/top-p kernel, which asserts `logits.dtype == torch.float32` → the worker dies, and the TP peer then reports a CUDA error. It fires on **any MTP + non-greedy request** (top-k / top-p / temperature) and is **independent of the FlashInfer gates**, so it reproduces "even without flashinfer" — matching your report. Greedy decoding returns *before* the sampler, which is why greedy GSM8K never surfaced it. Fixed by casting the draft logits to float32 (matching the main sampler). Validated on 2× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120): a 256k sustained sampling soak (temp 0.7 / top_p 0.9, 9 concurrent workers, MTP=2, EP) that used to crash on the *first* sampled request now runs clean (200+ requests).

> The error log you shared is from a 06-19 build during **startup** memory profiling (`cudaErrorNotPermitted` in the cudagraph dummy run), and you noted your runtime crashes are different — so that one isn't representative. If a crash recurs on the new build, a fresh runtime stderr would help confirm there isn't a third path.

**2. Packed-prefill output slice (@1zilc's `84 vs 83`).** With `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL=1`, the packed prefill path sliced the query to `num_prefill_tokens` under MTP/cudagraph padding but passed the **unsliced** output to the kernel, tripping `output.size(0)==num_tokens (84 vs 83)` (then cascading to an illegal access). Fixed by slicing the output symmetrically. This path is gated — the default FlashMLA prefill loops over `q.shape` and was never affected. @DerAndereAndi you also run `PREFILL=1`, so this one applies to you too.

**To pick up the fixes:** rebuild / pull from `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260622b`. Interim workaround without rebuilding: `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL=0` avoids #2, but #1 needs the new build (or greedy decoding).

**One note for `--max-model-len 500000`:** the sparse-MLA / indexer workspaces are sized by `max_model_len` and aren't SM12x-arch-gated yet, so they take a large fixed slice of VRAM and leave a thin KV budget at long context — see #42856 for the workspace-shrink. That's a memory-headroom concern, separate from the two crashes above.

Thanks again for the detailed reports — please let me know how the new tag holds up.

- wingcomm · comment · 2026-06-23T15:39:20Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4780859510)

Here's the warmup issue:

**Summary**
On the `codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable` branch (HEAD 5ba0f19f), the DeepSeek-V4
D512-split prefill warmup never runs. `model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py`
**Summary**
On the `codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable` branch (HEAD 5ba0f19f), the DeepSeek-V4
D512-split prefill warmup never runs. `model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py`
imports `_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS` from
`models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py`, but that module constant was replaced by
the env var `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS` (envs.py:184).
The import raises ImportError, which is swallowed by the surrounding
`except ImportError` → the whole warmup self-skips at DEBUG.

**Impact**
The D512-split prefill kernels are not pre-compiled, so the first long chunked
prefill (> MIN_TOKENS, default 4096) JIT-compiles `_indexed_d512_split_*` during
inference — a latency spike, and on FULL-capture builds historically a hang/crash.
This silently negates the warmup PR #41834 added. The DEBUG message
("split kernels or helpers are unavailable on this build") is misleading — the
kernels are present; only the stale import fails.

**Where (HEAD 5ba0f19f)**
- kernel_warmup.py:403  imports the removed constant
- kernel_warmup.py:424  uses it as the max_model_len guard
- flashmla.py:79,109   already read envs.VLLM_..._MIN_TOKENS (constant no longer defined)
- envs.py:184          VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS = 4096

**Repro**
Serve DeepSeek-V4-Flash on SM12x. At startup the line
"Warming up DeepSeek V4 D512-split sparse-MLA prefill kernels …" never appears;
the first >4096-token prefill triggers jit_monitor warnings for
`_indexed_d512_split_{score,stats,value}` / `_indexed_d512_chunked_merge_*`.

**Fix**
Drop the dead import item and point the guard at the env var (envs is already
imported). 2-line change; patch below. Validated in production — after the fix the
warmup line fires and the first long prefill JITs 0 D512-split kernels.

**Optional hardening**
The broad `except ImportError → logger.debug(...)` is what hid this for weeks.
Consider logging at WARNING (or not catching) when the warmup env flag is ON but
the import fails, so a future symbol rename surfaces instead of silently no-op'ing.

PR-ready patch (saved at …/scratchpad/d512-warmup-import-fix.patch, applies with git apply from repo root):

--- a/vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py
+++ b/vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py
@@ -400,7 +400,6 @@
         from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.nvidia.flashmla import (
             _INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MAX_TOPK,
-            _INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS,
             _INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOPK,
             DeepseekV4FlashMLAAttention,
         )
@@ -421,7 +420,10 @@
         if not is_triton_sparse_mla_enabled_for_platform():
             return
-        if getattr(runner, "max_model_len", 0) < _INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS:
+        if (
+            getattr(runner, "max_model_len", 0)
+            < envs.VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS
+        ):
             return

- wingcomm · comment · 2026-06-23T15:59:05Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4781039449)

DeepSeek-V4-Flash on GB10/SM121 — silent worker-wedge (preliminary report)

Status: characterized; root cause not yet pinned. py-spy of the wedged worker is now armed and a stack will follow at the next occurrence (~1 day). Sharing what we have so far. Raw log excerpts are in Appendix A.

TL;DR

After ~1–2 days of healthy serving, the engine silently stops generating — requests sit "Running" with throughput pinned at 0, KV cache frozen, and it never recovers. /health keeps returning 200 the whole time; only a real generation request reveals it. No error of any kind is logged — no Triton JIT, no operation not permitted, no CUDA error, no NCCL timeout, no OOM, no traceback. Only a full restart clears it. This is distinct from the (now-fixed) JIT-during-inference hang/crash class — those are neutralized by VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE=1 + piecewise prefill; residual Triton JITs now complete as harmless latency blips.

Environment

- 4× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121 / cc 12.1, aarch64), one TP rank per node, TP=4/EP=4, NCCL over RoCE (200G).
- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash. vLLM built from jasl/vllm@codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable.
- Seen on a93b9098 (fi0613), 8f93ea34, and currently 72261a7a (PR #41834 head) — spans builds, not a single-commit regression.
- Key config: cudagraph_mode=FULL → auto FULL_AND_PIECEWISE; MTP num_speculative_tokens=2; max_model_len=1048576; max_num_batched_tokens=32768; kv_cache_dtype=fp8; gpu_memory_utilization=0.85; prefix caching ON (~97% hit); FlashInfer 0.6.13 packed SM120 decode enabled.

Signature (established across 3 incidents — raw logs in Appendix A)

- Avg generation throughput → 0 with requests stuck in Running (not Waiting); KV-cache % frozen; no forward progress, indefinitely. (Appendix A.1)
- /health and /v1/models stay 200; a real POST /v1/chat/completions hangs.
- In the longer-lived captures, EngineCore logs No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds, repeating every 60s — i.e. the engine is blocked waiting on a worker's batch response over the shm-broadcast/zmq channel. (Appendix A.2, A.3)
- Does not self-heal; recovers only via sparkrun stop + relaunch.

What it is NOT (ruled out)

- Not the JIT-during-inference class — last Triton JIT was 22–47h before each wedge (exact timestamps in Appendix). Many kernels JIT safely as blips during normal operation.
- Not GPU/hardware — dmesg clean (no Xid / NVRM / nvidia faults) across all nodes.
- Not OOM — earlyoom never fires; ~40%+ host mem free at the wedge.
- Not RoCE/fabric drift — static IPs intact, links up, zero NCCL errors/timeouts logged.
- Not a malformed-request crash — those produce loud tracebacks / EngineDeadError; this is silent with the API server still alive.

Frequency / timing

┌──────────┬───────────────────┬─────────────────┐
│ incident │       build       │ uptime to wedge │
├──────────┼───────────────────┼─────────────────┤
│ 8        │ a93b9098 (fi0613) │ ~43.5h          │
├──────────┼───────────────────┼─────────────────┤
│ 9        │ 8f93ea34-warmfix  │ ~50h            │
├──────────┼───────────────────┼─────────────────┤
│ 10       │ 72261a7a          │ ~23.7h          │
└──────────┴───────────────────┴─────────────────┘

MTBF ~24–50h and load-dependent, not a fixed clock (uptimes don't cluster).

The one correlation clue (incident 10)

The freeze hit immediately after a large prefill, mid mixed-batch:
06:51:33  prompt 31238.1 tok/s, gen 0.1, Running: 2, Waiting: 1, KV 75.1%
06:51:43  prompt 0.0,           gen 0.0, Running: 2, Waiting: 1, KV 75.1%   <- frozen
06:51:53  prompt 0.0,           gen 0.2, Running: 2, Waiting: 1, KV 75.5%   <- still frozen
So it wedged during/just after a heavy mixed prefill+decode step, not at idle. The active prefill path is the D512-split sparse-MLA Triton prefill (accumulate_indexed_d512_split_sparse_mla_attention → _forward_sparse_mla_prefill_triton, confirmed via a live py-spy). Note that path's startup warmup is currently self-skipping on these builds due to a separate import bug we're reporting (kernel_warmup.py imports the removed _INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS) — unlikely to be the wedge itself, but flagging the overlap.

Hypotheses (unproven — the stack will decide)

1. CUDA-level deadlock in a sparse-MLA kernel under a rare batch shape. Notably, the last JIT before both incidents 8 and 9 was the same kernel, _indexed_d512_chunked_merge_state_kernel (the D512 chunked-merge prefill path; Appendix A.2/A.3) — so the D512 prefill path keeps showing up adjacent to the wedge, though hours before it.
2. Worker desync — a worker stops servicing the shm-broadcast loop (stuck in acquire_read) while the GPU is idle.
3. NCCL collective stall — can't fully rule out: our 2-min real-generation watchdog restarts the serve long before the 30-min TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC / flight-recorder would fire.
4. Prefix-cache + MTP interaction — we run prefix caching + spec-decode; recent branch work touched block-sharing COW/fences here.

What we've instrumented / what's next

- Real-generation watchdog (sliding window, ≥2/3 probe failures) auto-recovers it hands-off in ~6–8 min. /health is useless for this (it doesn't force a forward pass) — a real generation probe is required.
- py-spy is now armed (ptrace enabled) to dump the wedged Worker_TP + EngineCore stacks before teardown at the next wedge → should distinguish hypotheses 1–3 immediately. Stack to follow.

Questions for you

- At the next wedge, do you want us to hold off the watchdog and let it run to the NCCL flight-recorder / 30-min heartbeat dump (to confirm/exclude an NCCL stall)?
- Any specific env/logging you'd like captured next time — e.g. NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, TORCH_NCCL_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE, VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG?
- Is there a known batch-shape / MTP / prefix-cache edge you'd want us to try to reproduce deliberately, rather than waiting for organic traffic?

---
Appendix A — log evidence

All excerpts are from the real-generation watchdog's pre-teardown snapshots of the in-container serve log (/tmp/sparkrun_serve.log). Timestamps are UTC. Two complementary signatures: the engine-side throughput flatline (incident 10, snapshotted fast) and the EngineCore shm-broadcast stall every 60s (incidents 8 & 9, snapshotted later).

A.1 Incident 10 — 72261a7a — engine throughput flatline (freeze caught in ~18s)

Run start 06-22 07:08:27, wedge 06-23 06:51:43 → 23h43m uptime.
# healthy, generating normally:

@wingcomm — thank you, this is an exceptional report. Two parts:

**1. D512 warmup import bug — fixed and shipped.** Confirmed exactly as you diagnosed: `kernel_warmup.py` imported the removed `_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS`, the `ImportError` was swallowed, and the default-on warmup silently self-skipped. Fix (`28fef2c703`, tag `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260624`): dropped the dead import, pointed the guard at `envs.VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS`, and — your optional hardening — raised the swallowed-import log from DEBUG to **WARNING** (the early gate already confirms the warmup was requested, so a failed import there is a real problem, not a benign skip). Validated on 2×RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) with the D512 JIT gate: warmup-OFF → 12 in-inference split-kernel JITs, **warmup-ON → 0**, and the `Warming up DeepSeek V4 D512-split…` line now fires. Credit is yours.

**2. The silent worker-wedge.** The `No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60s` (every 60s) is the decisive signal: EngineCore (the writer) can't get a free shm-broadcast block because **a worker stopped consuming** — one rank's busy-loop is stalled and never reads/runs/returns the batch. With the wedge landing *during/just after a large prefill in a mixed batch* on TP=4/EP=4 over RoCE, my money is on a rank **stuck inside `execute_model`** — either a NCCL collective stall/mismatch (a rare mixed prefill+decode+MTP batch makes one rank issue a different number of all-reduce/all-to-all ops → silent deadlock until the heartbeat) or a CUDA deadlock in the sparse-MLA prefill. Your py-spy will settle it. Answering your three:

1. **py-spy first** — it discriminates all three hypotheses in one capture. Please grab **all four `Worker_TP` ranks + EngineCore** with `py-spy dump --native` (we need the C-stack into NCCL/CUDA, not just Python). A collective mismatch shows up as *different ranks parked in different collectives*; a desync shows the wedged worker at `acquire_read` like your idle baseline; a CUDA deadlock shows it deep in a kernel launch.
2. **Then**, only if py-spy shows a collective: don't wait 30 min — set `TORCH_NCCL_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE=8192`, `TORCH_NCCL_DUMP_ON_TIMEOUT=1`, and lower `TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC` to ~300–600 so the flight recorder dumps in 5–10 min; hold the watchdog just that long. Add `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` + `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`.
3. **Deliberate repro** is hard at MTBF 24–50h, but bias the odds: a sustained mixed-arrival soak — large (1M-class) prefills interleaved with decodes, MTP2, prefix-cache on, EP=4 — varying prefill sizes to hit edge batch shapes through the `_indexed_d512_chunked_merge_*` path that keeps appearing adjacent to your wedges.

The warmup fix above removes the JIT-during-inference confound you flagged (the D512 kernels are now pre-warmed), so the late `_indexed_d512_chunked_merge_state_kernel` JITs should disappear — one less variable. Please post the stacks when you have them; the all-ranks `--native` dump is what we need.


- wingcomm · comment · 2026-06-23T22:43:19Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4784111482)

Update — deployed 28fef2c703, then caught the wedge live with native stacks. It's not a collective stall and not a CUDA deadlock — it's an in-inference Triton JIT-compile cascade.

First: your warmup import fix works. On our 4×GB10/SM121 TP4 box the Warming up DeepSeek V4 D512-split… line now fires and startup JITs are 0 (was self-skipping via the stale import). Thanks for the fast turnaround.

Then we caught a wedge in the act. py-spy --native is dead on this aarch64 box (UNW_EBADREG from libunwind), so for C-stacks I used gdb -p <pid> -ex "set sysroot /proc/<pid>/root" -ex "thread apply all bt" — the sysroot makes gdb symbolize the in-container libs. All 4 Worker_TP ranks + EngineCore, captured while paused.

The decisive part — rank0 was progressing, not stuck.

rank0 first sample — blocked in a stream sync triggered by a .item():
cuStreamSynchronize (libcuda) → cudaStreamSynchronize (libcudart)
 → at::native::_local_scalar_dense_cuda                     # .item() GPU→CPU readback
 (py) _c128a_effective_topk_width  sparse_mla.py:384        # max_pos = int(positions.max().item())
    → build_c128a_topk_metadata → _build_attention_metadata → execute_model
rank0 re-sampled ~3 min later — moved into Triton compilation:
llvm::Module::print / AssemblyWriter::printFunction  (libtriton.so)   # LLVM codegen
…later: cuLaunchKernelEx → __triton_launcher…launch()
rank1, rank2: cuStreamSynchronize (waiting on the stream/peer). rank3: cuLaunchKernelEx → __triton_launcher. EngineCore: acquire_read → get_response (the shm-broadcast wait — the symptom, just waiting on the busy worker). GPUs at the wedge: mixed 10–96% util / 18–86 W (not the uniform full-spin of a HW/collective deadlock).

Conclusion: rank0 moving sync → LLVM codegen → kernel launch proves it isn't deadlocked — it's grinding through JIT compiles. Zero NCCL frames on any rank ⇒ not a collective stall. It's a slow in-inference Triton compile cascade that oscillates: compile → tokens flow → next uncovered shape → stall. So both hypotheses (collective mismatch, CUDA deadlock) are refuted for this wedge.

Why the warmup fix didn't end it: 0 startup JITs, but Triton specializes per shape/stride, and a 1M-context variable-length workload keeps producing new specializations that JIT mid-inference. 16 distinct kernels have JIT-compiled during inference since startup, each exactly once (so the in-process cache works — this is coverage, not a cache bug):
_indexed_d512_split_score / _split_stats / _split_value
_indexed_d512_chunked_merge_acc / _chunked_merge_state
_accumulate_indexed_attention_chunk_multihead
_fp8_mqa_logits / _fp8_paged_mqa_logits_rowwise / _combine_topk_swa_indices
_compute_prefill_metadata / _build_prefill_chunk_metadata
eagle_step_slot_mapping_metadata / eagle_prepare_next_token_padded
_mtp_shared_head_rmsnorm / _tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm / _deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum
Stalls cluster on the C128A-metadata path and the chunked-merge kernels.

Likely reframe of the earlier "silent wedges": we had no native stacks for those (ptrace was off then), but this strongly suggests they were the same cascade — our compile cache is ephemeral (/tmp, wiped each restart) and our 2-min watchdog restarted at ~4–6 min, i.e. mid-compile, so they looked permanent and "JIT-free" (jit_monitor only logs a compile after it completes; a kill mid-ptxas/codegen never logs).

Our side: persisting the Triton/Inductor cache to a durable bind so the shape set accumulates across restarts instead of re-paying every time. (We also wired an on-demand NCCL flight-recorder dump into the watchdog in case a true collective stall ever appears — but this wasn't one.)

Questions:
1. Can warmup be extended to the runtime shapes of these kernels — especially the C128A-metadata path and the chunked-merge kernels? Or is the specialization space too large to enumerate (→ persistent cache + accepting first-touch compiles is the realistic path)?
2. _c128a_effective_topk_width does int(positions.max().item()) — a data-dependent device→host sync on the hot path. It's where the CPU first blocks on pending GPU work, but it's also a per-step sync that kills CPU/GPU overlap. Could that max be hoisted/precomputed to drop the sync?
3. Any knob to bound the prefill shape space (fixed chunk sizing / padding) so warmup can be complete?

Happy to share the full all-ranks gdb dumps.

Resolution of the silent-wedge thread + packed-prefill validation

Following up on the silent worker-wedge we reported. With native stacks (gdb, since py-spy --native is UNW_EBADREG on aarch64), we refuted both the NCCL-collective and CUDA-deadlock hypotheses — caught all 4 ranks with rank0 progressing cuStreamSynchronize → llvm::Module::print (Triton LLVM codegen) → cuLaunchKernelEx. It's a Triton JIT-compile cascade in the D512 chunked sparse-MLA prefill, not a deadlock — long-context prefills hit uncovered kernel shapes that compile mid-inference; our watchdog was killing them mid-ptxas, which made them look permanent.

The fix is your own VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL flag (currently off-by-default). Enabling it routes prefill through the FlashInfer _SparseMLAPagedAttentionRunner instead of the Triton path. We validated it correctness-first on GB10/SM121, TP4:
- Needle-in-haystack retrieval correct on both 4.4K- and 48K-token chunked prefills (vs the Triton baseline); deterministic math/primes match.
- 48K chunked prefill → 0 new JITs (Triton path fires the _indexed_d512_chunked_merge/split cascade here).
- 2.5h soak: JIT count flat, zero D512 prefill JITs, no wedge/crash.

It eliminates the prefill-JIT class entirely and moots the D512-split warmup machinery. Would you consider promoting it to default for SM12x? Happy to share full logs.

One open question: even with packed prefill, a single large-context prefill monopolizes the engine (~26s for ~48K, concurrent requests block) — each chunk is a heavy multi-second step that doesn't yield to decodes. Is there planned work on SM120 prefill throughput or mid-chunk scheduling?

Doing some more testing, curious to see if there's any way to tune the kernel to improve prefill latency:

Long-context prefill on GB10 (sm_120) is memory/latency-bound — request: a dense prefill path that skips the indexer's KV scan

Running DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 4× DGX Spark GB10 (sm_120, TP=4) on the sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview line, with VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE=1 + ..._PREFILL=1 (packed FlashInfer). The packed prefill has been great — eliminated the D512 Triton JIT cascade, 0 in-inference JITs, correct at 150K (needle retrieval ✓). Thank you.

The remaining pain is fresh-context prefill latency: request_prefill_time_seconds p99 ≈ 240 s for ~500K-token cache-miss prefills (TTFT p99 ≈ 640 s when one is queued behind another). A controlled 153K fresh prefill measured 102 s ≈ 0.66 ms/token (→ ~4.5 min at 415K).

Profile (4-node, nvidia-smi -l 2 across the prefill):
- SM clock pinned ~2450–2500 MHz (near max) throughout
- Power only ~63 W avg / 79 W peak vs ~86 W ceiling, oscillating down to ~37 W between chunks
- Identical on all 4 ranks; decode for contrast profiles flat ~37 W (NCCL spin-wait)

Read: clocks maxed but power well under ceiling + heavy oscillation ⇒ memory/latency-bound (idle-waiting on LPDDR5X ~273 GB/s), not compute-bound — there's real headroom the kernels aren't capturing.

Ask (in order of effort):
1. Is a dense prefill path feasible? DSA's lightning indexer is fundamentally a decode optimization (sparse KV reads during gen). During prefill we populate full KV anyway, and the indexer adds an O(N²)-ish scoring scan on top — a strong suspect for the memory stalls. A prefill that runs attention densely (reuse the existing packed/FlashMLA dense path) and builds the index lazily would skip that scan and needs no new sm_120 kernel — it's scheduling/routing. Could you confirm whether the indexer scan dominates prefill traffic (an nsys range would isolate indexer vs attention), and whether a dense-prefill toggle is in scope?
2. Indexer/attention/merge fusion to cut LPDDR5X round-trips.
3. Noting use_fp4_indexer_cache is hard-gated to sm_10x (indexer.py:274-283) — it'd help here but needs an sm_120 FP4-indexer port (third_party/fmha_sm100 only). Lower priority given the effort.

Happy to run any profiling config you'd like reproduced on real GB10 hardware.

@wingcomm — consolidating replies to your three write-ups (the gdb wedge diagnosis, the packed-prefill validation, and the cache-miss prefill profile). Thank you for all of it — the native-stack work on aarch64 especially is the kind of evidence that's hard to get and easy to misattribute.

### 1. The wedge = in-inference Triton JIT cascade, and the `.item()` sync — fixed & shipped

Confirmed against the code on every point. `int(positions.max().item())` in `_c128a_effective_topk_width` (`models/deepseek_v4/sparse_mla.py`) is a real per-step device→host sync on the C128A metadata path — and it's now **gone**: it sources the max position from the CPU-side `CommonAttentionMetadata.max_seq_len` instead (no sync; decode value is identical, only chunked prefill sees a safe slightly-wider 128-aligned top-k). It's in the latest validated head, tag `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260626` (`c766cbc6ff`), GSM8K + long-context coherence revalidated. Thanks for flagging it.

On extending warmup (Q1/Q3): for **stock DSv4-Flash** the prefill kernel shape space is already finite and warmup-complete — `combined_topk` is fixed at 640 regardless of context length, and the D512-split warmup enumerates the full `{256…1152}` set. The chunked-merge kernels (`_indexed_d512_chunked_merge_*`) are the one un-warmed family, but they only fire when `combined_topk > 1152`, and DSv4-Flash caps at 640 — so on stock DSv4-Flash they should be unreachable. **Question back:** did your gdb actually catch the *merge* kernels compiling, or only the split + C128A-metadata ones? If you genuinely saw merge-kernel codegen at 1M/TP4, something's escaping the 640 cap on your config and we'd want your `combined_topk` / `window_size`. (The C128A *metadata kernel* itself is already JIT-stable — one compile — so the stall clustered there is the `.item()` sync stalling the launch stream around the *downstream* compiles, not a metadata recompile.) Persisting the Triton cache to a durable bind is the right belt-and-suspenders regardless.

### 2. Promoting packed prefill (`VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL`) — we want to, and your soak moves it forward

Our own DeepSeek-reference replay agrees with you: on the compressed-KV (C4A) layers packed matches the reference for non-first prefills (cosine ~0.96) while the default FlashMLA combine diverges (~0.56–0.74, stale workspace) — so packed is the *more*-correct path, and the `≤64`-scratch case under MTP plus the "84-vs-83" padding case are both already handled in code. The one thing we owe before flipping the default: the flag was shelved on a single signal — GSM8K at concurrency 8 came in ~0.90 (packed) vs ~0.95 (FlashMLA), and that measurement didn't include MTP. Your needle + 2.5 h flat-JIT soak demonstrate retrieval correctness and stability but not that aggregate-accuracy-under-concurrency number, so our gate to promote is a **GSM8K nc=8 with MTP** re-run; our replay predicts parity.

One implementation caveat worth stating: this flag only activates when the FlashInfer-SM120 sparse-MLA kernel is present — stock vLLM wheels don't ship it (`is_deep_gemm_supported()` is False and released flashinfer has no `_sparse_mla_sm120`), which is exactly why it's opt-in and why our stock validation boxes default to Marlin (W4A16, GSM8K-correct on both SM120 and SM121). So "promote to default" means default-on *when the kernel is present*; stock-deps users are unaffected.

On a single large prefill monopolizing the engine: that's stock vLLM-v1 chunked prefill, not DSv4-specific (no DSv4 scheduler). Today's only lever is a smaller `long_prefill_token_threshold` — finer chunks interleave decodes more often, at some prefill-throughput cost. True mid-chunk yielding is upstream scheduler work we don't have in flight in this PR.

### 3. Cache-miss prefill latency — your memory-bound read is right; dense-prefill isn't free, but fusion is the win

Confirmed from the code: during prefill the SM120 indexer top-k is **two-pass** — it materializes the full `(num_q, seq_len_kv)` **fp32** logits in global memory then re-reads them in a separate top-k pass. For a ~150K prefill that's hundreds of MB of fp32 logits written-then-read **per layer** over ~273 GB/s — exactly your "clocks pinned, power well under ceiling, oscillating between chunks" signature.

But a dense-prefill toggle isn't pure routing: the compressed-layer prefill attention is data-dependent on the indexer top-k (`_forward_prefill` reads `topk_indices_buffer` / `c128a_prefill_topk_indices` → `combined_indices`, and the kernel gathers *only* those slots). There's no full-context dense MLA prefill kernel in-tree (the only index-free path is the 4096-token SWA window), and "dense + lazy index" changes DSA's intended prefill semantics — a correctness-bearing kernel project, not a flag.

**The better lever is your #2 (fusion):** a fused score+top-k kernel that keeps the M×N scores in SRAM and emits only the top-k indices would kill the dominant LPDDR5X round-trip with no semantics change. We can quantify the share first — **happy to run an nsys indexer-vs-attention range-split on our 2-node GB10** and post it; the ops are cleanly separable in the timeline. On the FP4 indexer (#3): correct it's hard-gated to sm_10x, and the sm120 FP8 topk fallback also early-returns for FP4 Q — so it's a kernel port (q-side FP4 quant exists; no sm120 FP4 logits/top-k *consumer*). Bandwidth-aligned but real work, lower priority, agreed.

---

One more that may help directly: we just synced the branch onto current `upstream/main` and measured a **~+80% cold-prefill `ctx_pp` jump** on GB10 (decode flat), reproduced across two runs — inherited from upstream's prefill / scheduler work, not an SM12x change of ours. If you share your build SHA we can tell you whether you already have it. Tag `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260626` (`c766cbc6ff`) is the synced + validated head.

This is the analysis:

**Fatal `operation not permitted` from un-warmed Triton specialization of `_deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum_kernel` (o_proj) on unaligned prefill chunks**

**Env:** DeepSeek-V4-Flash, SM120 / `NVIDIA_GB10` (DGX Spark), 2-node TP=2 (cross-node), fp8 KV, MTP spec-decode (`num_speculative_tokens=2`), chunked prefill (`max_num_batched_tokens=8192`), `enforce_eager=False` (`cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`). vLLM `v20260621.dev284+g76dff54c2`.

**Symptom:** a TP worker dies mid-inference; the peer rank then blocks in the cross-node collective until its `sample_tokens` RPC times out (~5 min) → `EngineDeadError` and the whole server shuts down.

```text
models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/o_proj.py -> fp8_einsum.py:145 _deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum_kernel[grid](...)
triton/compiler/compiler.py:465 _init_handles -> driver.active.utils.load_binary(...)
RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: operation not permitted
```

**Trigger:** the failing step is the **tail chunk of a chunked prefill** — prompt 266,603 tokens, prefix-cache hit, remainder scheduled = **1131 tokens**. `1131 % 16 = 11`.

**Root cause:** the o_proj einsum (and the other prefill kernels) is Triton-specialized on the `num_tokens` divisibility-by-16 predicate. `_deepseek_v4_sparse_mla_attention_warmup` only warms `num_tokens = prefill_tokens` (= `max_num_batched_tokens`, a multiple of 16), so **only the divisible-by-16 specialization is compiled/loaded during warmup**. The first real prefill chunk whose token count is not a multiple of 16 JIT-loads the *unaligned* variant during inference; `load_binary` returns `cudaErrorNotPermitted`, which the driver raises when a module load coincides with CUDA-graph stream capture in the process — so it is fatal rather than a latency spike.

This is consistent with `jit_monitor` already warning earlier in the same run (non-fatal, before any capture) for exactly these kernels:

```text
Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: _deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum_kernel
... _w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm, _tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_kernel,
... _build_prefill_chunk_metadata_kernel, _compute_prefill_metadata_kernel
```

i.e. the warmup already intends to keep these out of the inference path (the chunked-prefill and D512-split dummies), it just misses the `% 16 != 0` class.

> The odd-sized batch in our case followed a `Missing cached draft probabilities ... falling back to legacy speculative rejection behavior` warning, but the fatal kernel is a generic prefill kernel — any unaligned prefill chunk reproduces it regardless of spec-decode.

**Suggested fix:** in `_deepseek_v4_sparse_mla_attention_warmup`, add an unaligned-token prefill dummy run mirroring the existing aligned pair, so the unaligned specialization compiles outside capture:

```python
unaligned = prefill_tokens - 1 if prefill_tokens % 16 == 0 else prefill_tokens
if unaligned > 1 and unaligned % 16 != 0:
    runner._dummy_run(num_tokens=unaligned, skip_eplb=True, is_profile=True,
                      force_attention=True, create_single_prefill=True)
    runner._dummy_run(num_tokens=unaligned, skip_eplb=True, is_profile=True,
                      force_attention=True, create_single_prefill=True,
                      profile_seq_lens=unaligned * 2)
```

I am trying the patch now, will take some time to see if this solves it for sure.

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-28T10:48:44Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4825851554)

Thanks for the excellent analysis — the root cause is exactly right: the o_proj `_deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum_kernel` JIT-loads a fresh cubin for the prefill chunk's token count, and when that `cuModuleLoad` lands during CUDA-graph capture it returns `cudaErrorNotPermitted` and kills the worker (which then hangs the cross-node peer in the collective → `EngineDeadError`). The `jit_monitor` warnings are the harmless *compile* hook; the fatal path is the cubin *load*, which it doesn't cover — that's why you saw warnings earlier in the run but a crash later.

One correction that matters for the fix, though: it's **not** a `% 16` divisibility class. `num_tokens` is declared `tl.constexpr` in that kernel, so it specializes on the **exact** token count (plus three input strides that scale with it: `a_stride_group = T·d` and the two scale strides via `align(T,4)`). So warming `prefill_tokens - 1` only pre-compiles the single size 8191 — a real tail of 1131 (or any other) is a different cubin and still JITs mid-inference. Enumerating tail sizes in warmup can't work either, since the tail size is effectively continuous.

The robust fix is a one-kernel edit: demote `num_tokens` (and those three token-dependent stride args) from `tl.constexpr` to runtime args. `num_tokens` is used only for masking, the loop is over `hidden_size`, and the grid is host-computed via `cdiv`, so it's numerically identical and perf-neutral — and it collapses the kernel to a **single cubin for all chunk sizes**, so the existing 8192 warmup then covers everything. (This mirrors what the kernel's own producer `_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant_per_head` already does.)

Good news on scope: o_proj is the **only** DeepSeek-V4 prefill kernel with this constexpr-on-token-count pattern — the others take the token dim as a runtime arg or via the grid, so they're not at risk of this particular crash.

I'm implementing + validating this now (reproduce the in-inference einsum JIT on an unaligned tail, then confirm 0 in-inference JIT across varied tail sizes with unchanged correctness on a 2× GB10 setup) and will push to the branch. Thanks again for the precise repro and the full log — that made it quick to pin down.


- jasl · comment · 2026-06-28T12:43:12Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4826130057)

Fix pushed — commit `8571496a4c` on `codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable`.

Validated at the kernel level on a GB10: with `num_tokens` (and the three token-count-dependent strides) demoted to runtime, the o_proj einsum now compiles to a **single cubin across every prefill token count** I tested — 256/260/512/743/999/1130/1131/1147/8191 — vs **one cubin per size** before (9 → 1). So there's no per-size `cuModuleLoad` during inference, which closes the `cudaErrorNotPermitted`-under-capture window you hit. Outputs are bit-identical to the old kernel (the demotion is purely a JIT-key change), so no numerical or perf impact.

That should stop the recurring crash. Note your log also shows a handful of *other* kernels JIT-compiling once on the first prefill (`_combine_topk_swa_indices`, `_mtp_shared_head_rmsnorm`, the eagle/sample kernels, etc.) — unlike the einsum those are token-count-*independent*, so they JIT at most once rather than per chunk size, and they only emitted the non-fatal `jit_monitor` warning, not the crash. We're tracking a broader startup-warmup pass to pre-compile those too, but it's separate from this fix.

Could you pull the branch and confirm the crashes stop on your setup? Thanks again for the precise repro + full log.


- wingcomm · comment · 2026-06-29T00:33:45Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4828022483)

### Packed FlashInfer SM120 prefill hangs the GPU on multi-request prefill batches (silent engine wedge)

Reporting a reproducible hard wedge on the packed FlashInfer SM120 **prefill** path (`VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL=1`), which became default-on in `fd76d65d4`. Captured live across all ranks. **Still reproduces against the current PR tip** (history through `367ed7c66`); it is a **distinct failure mode** from the recently-landed prefill fixes — see "Not the same as…" below.

**Environment**
- 4× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), TP=4 / EP=4, RoCE CX7 fabric, vLLM-native `torch.distributed` (no Ray)
- Build: this PR's `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260626` snapshot (`c766cbc6`), FlashInfer 0.6.13, CUDA 13.2
- Flags: `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE=1`, `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL=1`
- Args: `--max-model-len 524288 --max-num-seqs 3 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-chunked-prefill --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL"}'` (engine runs FULL_AND_PIECEWISE for the indexer backend)

**Symptom (silent wedge)**
- Engine stops progressing under load; `/health` and `/metrics` keep returning 200, but `generation_tokens_total` / `iteration_tokens_total_count` are frozen and `num_requests_running=0`.
- EngineCore repeatedly logs `shm_broadcast.py:705 "No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds"`.
- Any real `/v1/chat/completions` hangs (no first token). Only a full engine restart recovers.

**Root cause (py-spy, all TP ranks identical)**
```
_forward_prefill   vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashinfer_sm120_decode.py:398
forward_mqa        vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py:323   # if num_prefills > 0: self._forward_prefill(...)
forward_mqa        vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashinfer_sm120_decode.py:217
attention_impl     vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py:507
... model.forward ...
__call__           vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py:254               # inside a replayed CUDA graph
_model_forward     vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:3793
```
EngineCore is correspondingly blocked in `acquire_read` (`shm_broadcast.py:698`, via `multiproc_executor.get_response`) waiting for the worker batch result — i.e. the worker never returns.

Line 398 sits in the packed-prefill **SWA per-request-local position-remap** block, which the code comments mark as **"No-op at num_prefills==1"** — it only executes for **multi-request prefill batches (num_prefills > 1)**.

**Native stack of the wedged worker (gdb):**
```
#0  __GI_sched_yield
#1-9  libcuda.so.1
#10  cuLaunchKernel
#11  libcudart.so.13
```
Thread is RUNNING, busy-spinning in `sched_yield` inside the driver while trying to enqueue a launch → the CUDA stream is **not draining**, i.e. a prior kernel on the stream is hung on-device, so the next `cuLaunchKernel` spins forever. There is **no `ptxas`/`make_cubin`/LLVM in the stack** and no `cuModuleLoad`, so this is a runtime **GPU kernel hang**, not a JIT compile or module-load.

**Not the same as the recently-landed prefill fixes**
This is a different failure than the prefill JIT/crash issues fixed in this PR over the last few days:
- `8571496a4` (unaligned chunked-prefill → o_proj fp8-einsum cubin load during cudagraph capture → `cudaErrorNotPermitted` worker death → `EngineDeadError`): that is a **JIT/`cuModuleLoad` crash**. Ours has no `cuModuleLoad`, no `cudaErrorNotPermitted`, the worker does **not** die, and the JIT counter stays flat.
- `78e0a1bb4` (warm full D512-split width range) / `7c5730303` (warm MTP path): warmup/JIT-latency fixes, not on the packed-FI prefill path. Our wedge is `cuLaunchKernel` spin on an already-compiled kernel, so warmup does not address it.

**What we've since observed**
- Diagnostic corroboration that this is a hang, not a slow-but-advancing prefill: during the wedge **all of `{generation_tokens_total, iteration_tokens_total_count, prompt_tokens_total}` AND `kv_cache_usage_perc` are frozen** across the whole event (sampled from `/metrics`, which keeps serving 200). A legitimately busy chunked prefill instead keeps `prompt_tokens_total`/`iteration` and/or KV rising — those move here only up to the freeze, then flatline.
- Exposure is concurrency-gated: the same build has run 35h+ with **no recurrence under light/serial traffic**, but wedges under sustained concurrency where prefills batch (num_prefills > 1) — e.g. it surfaced during a GSM8K run at concurrency 8.

**Trigger hypothesis**
The hang is in the `num_prefills>1` SWA index-remap path of packed prefill, replayed inside a CUDA graph. With `max_num_seqs>1`, concurrent prefills batch together (num_prefills>1) and exercise it; a bad index/offset for a particular concurrent-prefill shape appears to drive the downstream sparse-MLA prefill kernel into an on-device hang.

**Questions for maintainers**
1. Is this a known limitation of the packed SM120 prefill at num_prefills>1, especially under CUDA-graph capture?
2. Given `fd76d65d4` makes packed prefill default-on whenever the SM120 FI backend is active, should it be gated off for multi-request prefill batches and/or when cudagraph is enabled until the kernel/index path is hardened?
3. Any guidance on the index math in the SWA per-request-local remap block (`flashinfer_sm120_decode.py` ~388–400) that could produce OOB block offsets for num_prefills>1?

Happy to provide full py-spy/gdb dumps from all four ranks and a repro recipe.

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-29T05:26:11Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4829259663)

Thanks for the exceptionally detailed report — py-spy + gdb across all ranks is exactly what's needed here.

I spent significant time trying to reproduce this on **2× GB10 (TP=2)** and **could not trigger the wedge**, even matching your exact serve config (`--max-model-len 524288 --max-num-seqs 3 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-chunked-prefill`, MTP=2, `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, `PREFILL=1`+`DECODE=1`) under sustained GSM8K-shaped concurrency at nc=8. I also varied greedy vs top-k sampling, short vs long prompts, and FlashInfer builds both **before and after #3615**. The serve stayed healthy across hundreds of requests in every case.

A few questions to help isolate it — my strong suspicion is your **4-node TP=4 / EP=4** topology (or your exact FlashInfer build) is load-bearing:

1. **Exact FlashInfer commit?** "0.6.13" is ambiguous — the *released* 0.6.13 wheel ships **without** the SM120 sparse-MLA kernels, so you must be on a nightly/main build. Which commit (`flashinfer.__git_version__`)? Specifically, is it **before or after #3615** (`49f2abf`, 2026-06-16, *"fix(topk): eliminate multi-CTA radix top-k stream hangs on SM120/SM121"*)? Really helpful — pinning the exact commit settles a lot. `49f2abf` = #3615 with nothing after, so we agree: #3615 is **necessary but not sufficient**, and your "bad indices + a top-k that *hangs* rather than *degrades* on them under TP=4/EP=4" framing matches what we see. On 2-node TP=2 the packed `cu_base` path mis-indexes the non-first prefill requests but the top-k tolerates it (degraded, not fatal), which is exactly why we can't reproduce the freeze.

**Candidate fix** is up at [`jasl/vllm@experiment/c4-cu_base-prefill-drop`](https://github.com/jasl/vllm/commit/4214cea78b) — it removes the redundant `cu_base` rebase on the packed FlashInfer-SM120 **prefill** path. `top_k_per_row_prefill` already emits request-local compressed top-k positions (the kernel subtracts `rowStart = cu_seqlen_ks`), and the SM120 **decode** path consumes the same buffer with no rebase and is validated — so the prefill-side rebase double-subtracts the base and mis-indexes `req>0` at `num_prefills>1`. Dropping it just mirrors the decode path. (Distinct from the FlashMLA-path rebase, which is a separate code path we're leaving alone.)

```diff
--- a/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashinfer_sm120_decode.py
+++ b/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashinfer_sm120_decode.py
@@ class DeepseekV4FlashInferSM120DecodeAttention(DeepseekV4FlashMLAAttention):
             if self.compress_ratio == 4:
                 assert self.topk_indices_buffer is not None
+                # The indexer (top_k_per_row_prefill) already emits request-local
+                # compressed top-k positions (rowStart = cu_seqlen_ks is subtracted
+                # inside the kernel), so feed the buffer slice straight to the
+                # global-slot mapping exactly as the validated SM120 DECODE path does.
+                # The previous cu_base rebase double-subtracted that base and
+                # mis-indexed req>0 at num_prefills>1.
                 prefill_local = self.topk_indices_buffer[num_decode_tokens:num_tokens]
-                # Rebase the indexer's BATCH-GLOBAL compressed top-k positions ...
-                comp_lens = (
-                    swa_metadata.seq_lens[num_decodes:num_reqs] // self.compress_ratio
-                )
-                cu_base = (torch.cumsum(comp_lens, dim=0) - comp_lens).to(torch.int32)
-                req_local = (
-                    swa_metadata.token_to_req_indices[num_decode_tokens:num_tokens]
-                    - num_decodes
-                ).long()
-                base_per_token = cu_base[req_local].unsqueeze(1)
-                prefill_local = torch.where(
-                    prefill_local >= 0, prefill_local - base_per_token, prefill_local
-                )
                 global_indices, topk_lens = compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens(
                     prefill_local,
                     swa_metadata.token_to_req_indices[num_decode_tokens:num_tokens],
                     attn_metadata.block_table[:num_reqs],
                     block_size,
                     swa_metadata.is_valid_token[num_decode_tokens:num_tokens],
                 )
```

3. **FlashInfer bumped to ≥ `nightly-v0.6.13-20260619`, patch *not* applied** → tests the "top-k tolerance" half.

If (2) alone clears it, that's the cleanest outcome. If only (2)+(3) together do, then both the indexing and a post-`49f2abf` kernel change are load-bearing, and we'll chase which upstream commit. Update from the soak — a significant one, plus some commit archaeology that narrows it.

**The `cu_base` fix did not eliminate the hang class.** Arm #2 (`367ed7c66` + `4214cea78b`, FlashInfer `49f2abf`) ran clean ~16h, then froze with the identical silent-wedge signature (real-gen timeout, gen/iter counters frozen, `shm_broadcast` every 60s). Same intermittency / MTBF as before.

**But it wedged in a *different* op.** py-spy across all ranks caught:
```
mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang   vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang.py:549
forward                       vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py:940
... (inside vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py:254)
```
the **MHC prenorm GEMM via TileLang/TVM-FFI** — not the `_forward_prefill`/`cu_base`/top-k path of incident-14. Native gdb is the same mechanism: `cuLaunchKernelEx → __GI_sched_yield` busy-spin (`libtvm.so` → `libcuda`), **no `ptxas`/`nvrtc`/`cuModuleLoad`** → a **GPU kernel hang, not a JIT**.

**The reframe that matters most:** the Python frame is the **victim, not the culprit** — it's just the *next* op trying to `cuLaunchKernel` when the GPU/stream is *already* hung. So `_forward_prefill` (inc-14) vs `mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang` (inc-15) likely just reflects which op launched into an already-wedged stream. Your `cu_base` fix is still correct and may well have closed the prefill-path freeze, but **some kernel is hanging on-device and stalling the stream, and the observed launch site varies.**

**Commit archaeology — where I think this lives.** We scanned the PR history against the symptom:
- The **MHC commits** (`1381809` avoid MHC GEMM JIT per token count, `93400dd` keep optimized MHC path, `16c1667e` *remove* ineffective MHC warmup, `aaef91a` drop CustomOp wrapper) are all about **compilation**. Ours is a runtime hang with no JIT in the stack — so these don't apply, even though `mhc_*` is the victim frame.
- The genuinely relevant lineage is the **CUDA-graph + MTP hang** work, all already in our build: `95fc9073b` *"Fix DeepSeek V4 MTP small-batch graph hangs"*, `285b542b8` *"eager-break DeepSeek-V4 attention under FULL cudagraph for spec-decode"*, `6c92b0972` default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. Our freeze is **inside a CUDA-graph replay, under MTP spec-decode + FULL(_AND_PIECEWISE) cudagraph** — exactly that regime. Those fixes are present and didn't fully close it, which points at a **residual cudagraph + MTP + attention stream-ordering hang** rather than a specific MHC or top-k kernel bug.
- For completeness: nothing newer helps either. HEAD has moved `367ed7c66 → a5ebb5f66` (2 commits: a 06-29 upstream merge + "self-size C128A prefill workspace + de-dup warmup backend set") — neither touches the MHC/TileLang path or stream/launch ordering.

Net: the evidence points away from any single kernel (top-k or MHC) and toward a residual cudagraph + MTP + attention stream-ordering hang. The natural discriminators would be MTP-off vs `enforce-eager`/`cudagraph_mode:NONE`, plus a GPU-side capture (NCCL flight-recorder / CUDA trace) to name the actual in-flight kernel rather than the Python victim frame — happy to run whichever is most useful to you on the 4-node box, and the fresh py-spy + gdb dumps (worker + EngineCore, all ranks) are saved and available. The live 4-node session offer also stands once your switch is in.

- jasl · comment · 2026-06-30T10:14:59Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4842266147)

Thanks for the incident-15 detail and for running arm #2 to ~16h — that's exactly the data point we needed. Two findings from tracing the EP path in `a5ebb5f66b`, one of which rules a hypothesis *out*.

**We can rule out the cudagraph-mode / collective-desync angle.** The tempting story was: at `--enable-expert-parallel` + DP=1, the per-layer combine is `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` (`moe_runner.py:447-453`, fires for `ep_size>1`); on 4 non-NVLink GB10s `should_custom_ar()` is False (`custom_all_reduce.py:150,241`) so it falls to raw pynccl on `current_stream()` (`pynccl.py:186`) and gets captured into the FULL graph; meanwhile the cross-rank cudagraph-mode MIN-sync is gated on `data_parallel_size>1` (`gpu_model_runner.py:3902`, `dp_utils.py:197`) and skipped at your DP=1 — so a single divergent step would replay an unmatched collective and wedge. The structural facts all check out, **but the trigger cannot fire**: every cudagraph-dispatch input (`num_tokens`, `num_reqs`, `uniform_decode`, mode) is a pure function of the `SchedulerOutput` that's broadcast once and dequeued byte-identically by every worker (`multiproc_executor.py:374/387`), so all SPMD ranks pick the same `(mode, BatchDescriptor)` and issue the same captured collectives in the same order. The one architectural per-rank branch — cascade attention — is dead for MLA (`use_cascade_attention()` returns False in the base backend, no MLA backend overrides it). And MTP's draft loop is a static `range(num_speculative_tokens-1)` (`llm_base_proposer.py:704`); accepted/rejected counts only change masking *contents*, never the dispatch `num_tokens` or the collective count. So the `dp>1` gate is genuinely not a correctness gap for EP — the divergence it guards against is created by independent DP scheduling, which DP=1 doesn't have. **Net: not worth chasing the DP-sync / captured-collective-desync path.**

**What survives.** With dispatch divergence out, the floating victim frame (your reframe is right — it's the next launch onto an already-dead stream) plus `cuLaunchKernelEx → sched_yield`, no JIT, and EP-only points at an **on-device multi-CTA cooperative-kernel hang of the same *class* as FI #3615, but in a kernel #3615 didn't touch** — triggered by the extra SM contention EP=4 adds. #3615 fixed the FlashInfer sampler radix-topk (which vLLM disables on SM120 anyway), but the same GB10 context-time-slice starvation (a peer CTA preempted past its slice while others spin on an arrival counter, no timeout) can hit any hand-rolled cooperative kernel. Two concrete candidates on the decode path: the NCCL collective kernels themselves (now far more numerous per step under EP), and our own lightning-indexer top-k `persistent_topk.cuh` (cooperative_topk is gated off for family-120, so decode top-k routes there; its GMEM spin-barrier has no co-residency guarantee or timeout). We can't name the kernel from code alone — it needs a GPU-side capture at an actual wedge.

**To name it, the two cheap discriminators + the capture:**
1. **Does the wedge survive `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` (or `enforce-eager`)?** That removes the captured collectives from the FULL decode graph. If it still wedges, the hang is a plain on-device kernel race independent of capture (favors the cooperative-kernel hypothesis); if it stops, capture is implicated after all.
2. **Does it survive with `--enable-expert-parallel` off (pure TP=4)?** Isolates whether the EP combine collectives are the contention source vs. just a victim.
3. **GPU-side capture to NAME it:** NCCL flight recorder — `TORCH_NCCL_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE=20000`, `TORCH_NCCL_DUMP_ON_TIMEOUT=1`, `TORCH_NCCL_ENABLE_MONITORING=1`, `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=COLL` — on a real collective deadlock the watchdog dump lists the last enqueued collective per rank and any op-count mismatch directly. Pair it with a health-freeze watchdog (poll `/health` + the iter counter; on 200-but-frozen, fire `py-spy dump --native` + `gdb -p … 'thread apply all bt'` + trigger the NCCL dump on **all** ranks). If the NCCL flight recorder shows all ranks with matched, completed collectives and one stuck *compute* kernel, that points at `persistent_topk`/an indexer cooperative kernel rather than NCCL.

Could you confirm DP=1 (no `--data-parallel-size`), and if you get a cycle, the single most decisive data point is whether the wedge survives `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`. We're bringing our own 4-node GB10 box up to TP=4/EP=4 now and will run the same capture; we'll share whatever the flight recorder names.

- jasl · comment · 2026-07-02T04:18:21Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4862154151)

Thank you — this is genuinely useful, please don't stop. A 6-node PP=3 GB10 serve of a *second* DSA model (GLM-5.2) on this backend is exactly the generalization signal I want for the merge case.

A few notes on your open questions:

- **You shouldn't need `--enforce-eager`.** The sparse-MLA warmup (`VLLM_ENABLE_DEEPSEEK_V4_SPARSE_MLA_WARMUP`, on by default) exists precisely to pre-compile the aligned prefill/decode shapes before cudagraph capture, so the `num_tokens % 16` in-graph JIT shouldn't fire. Its gate keys off the *attention backend*, not the model, so `GlmMoeDsa` on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` should be covered. If you have cycles, **please try dropping `--enforce-eager`** — I'd expect a meaningful throughput jump over the eager ~25 tok/s (which is compute-bound as you noted). If it *does* JIT in-graph, that's a warmup-coverage gap on my side and your repro would let me fix it directly.
- **`gpu-memory-utilization 0.80` is the right setting** on GB10. The NVFP4 autotuner's transient workspaces during the autotune→serve transition aren't reflected in the util headroom, and on unified memory they share the same pool — so 0.85 being marginal is expected. `--watermark` is a cleaner lever than pushing util higher; you're not leaving much on the table at 0.80.
- **Slow load:** the 160–515 s spread *across ranks* looks like NVMe/CPU contention plus per-rank NVFP4 dequant / indexer setup rather than raw I/O on the ~71 GiB itself. If you can profile disk-read vs dequant vs indexer-prep separately, that'd be interesting.

On your offer — the three most valuable to me:
1. **The cudagraph-on run above** (drop `--enforce-eager`) — the headline, and it doubles as a validation that the warmup generalizes to a second DSA model.
2. **Single-sequence long-context TTFT at 256k → 1M** — I can share a needle-recall coherence check so it validates correctness at extreme context, not just that it runs.
3. **TP2 × PP3 correctness**, since I mostly test TP — pipeline-parallel DSA coverage I don't otherwise exercise.

Any of those would be a big help. Thanks again for putting 6× GB10 behind this.

- aligningmyself · comment · 2026-07-02T11:38:38Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-4865269740)

Update — worked through your list. 6× GB10 (DGX Spark, `sm_121a`), GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsa`), TP=2×PP=3, PR #41834.

**Ask #1 — dropped `--enforce-eager` (the headline).**

- **Zero in-graph JIT.** Came up on `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, captured clean — no `num_tokens % 16` "operation not permitted" during capture. So the default sparse-MLA warmup **covers `GlmMoeDsa`** exactly as you predicted (the gate keys off the backend, not the model). The warmup generalizes to a second DSA model on SM121 — no warmup-coverage gap to fix on your side. ✅
- Correct (greedy, temp 0): `17×23`→**391**, `60mi/1.5h`→**40 mph**, capital of Australia→**Canberra**.
- Stable.
- **Throughput only moved ~+6–8%**, though — not the jump we both expected:

| | eager | cudagraph-on |
|---|---|---|
| C=1 | 8.0 tok/s | **8.5** |
| C=8 agg | 25.4 | **27.4** |
| C=16 agg | 25.5 | **27.5** |

The *why* is the interesting part, and it lines up with @wingcomm: **our 6-node decode is interconnect-latency-bound, not launch-overhead-bound.** TP=2×PP=3 puts a lot of cross-node collectives on every decode step, and this fabric is **NCCL-over-TCP** (200 GbE ConnectX-7, but `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` / `NET_PLUGIN=none`). GPUs spin-wait on comms, so cudagraph's launch-overhead reduction mostly isn't on the critical path: the same mechanism @wingcomm cited for PIECEWISE costing ~40%. Net: **cudagraph-on is safe here (no JIT, correct), but it isn't the throughput lever on this topology.**

Worth flagging *why* we're on TCP, since it likely generalizes to any multi-node GB10: **GPUDirect RDMA isn't available on GB10's unified memory** — there's no discrete GPU memory for the NIC to DMA into, so the OFI plugin's DMABUF GDR registration fails (`ibv_reg_mr_iova2`) and the standard workaround is `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` + TCP. RoCE host-staging (RDMA without GPU-direct) might beat TCP latency, but I haven't gotten it stable for NCCL here. So the comm-bound wash between eager and cudagraph is probably **representative of multi-node GB10**, not an un-tuned fabric: which is itself the useful signal: on this class of box, capture mode isn't where the decode throughput lives.

**Ask #3 — TP2×PP3 correctness.** Covered by the above: same TP=2×PP=3 world size, correct in both eager and cudagraph-on. Pipeline-parallel DSA works end-to-end.

**Ask #2 — long-context TTFT 256k→1M. This surfaced a GB10 serving ceiling in the sparse indexer: probably the most useful thing in this reply.**

Walking context up under enforce-eager, single-sequence:

| context | prompt_tokens | result |
|---|---|---|
| 256k | 262k | ✅ serves |
| 384k | 393k | ✅ serves, **TTFT 143 s** (reproducible across 2 runs) |
| 512k | 524k | ❌ **`persistent_topk` fails**; request wedges the engine |

The error (`sparse_attn_indexer.py:728` → `torch.ops._C.persistent_topk`, `topk.cu:136`):

```
RuntimeError: launch_persistent_topk ... persistent_topk would oversubscribe and the
FilteredTopK fallback requires >=128KB smem per block (have 101376).
total_ctas=90 > num_sms*occupancy=48 (TopK=2048, vec_size=4, ctas_per_group=90, smem=48688).
```

(That full trace is the 1M cudagraph-warmup instance, `total_ctas=90`. The 512k **serving** trip is the same failure at a smaller shape: `total_ctas=62 > num_sms*occupancy=48`.)

**On GB10 (SM121):** the indexer's `total_ctas` grows with accumulated context; past ~48 it oversubscribes the GB10's `num_sms*occupancy=48`. The `FilteredTopK` fallback needs ≥128 KB shared-mem/block, but GB10 exposes only **101376 B (~99 KB)** — so the fallback is also unavailable, and the request hard-fails. Two things worth flagging:

- It trips at **serving**, not only cudagraph warmup. Chunked prefill (4096-token chunks) does *not* keep `total_ctas` bounded, because the indexer's top-k is over the full accumulated context, not the query chunk. (It also trips the cudagraph warmup dummy-run at large `--max-model-len` — a separate init-time failure with the same root.)
- The serving ceiling is **~(384k, 512k) on GB10**, well below the KV-memory ceiling (~1.03M tokens at util 0.80). So the **kernel, not memory,** caps long-context on this hardware.

Reads like a hardware-limit assumption (SM count + smem-per-block) that holds on datacenter GPUs but not GB10. Two directions on your side: (a) GB10-aware tiling that keeps `total_ctas ≤ num_sms*occupancy`, or (b) a `FilteredTopK` fallback that fits GB10's ~99 KB smem. **Happy to test a patch on the 6× GB10 rig.**

I didn't pin the cutoff finer than (384k, 512k) — each probe wedges the engine and needs a restart, and the band is tight enough to act on. **Please send the needle-recall check** and I'll run it at 256k/384k (the working regime) to validate correctness at depth, not just that it serves.

---

@wingcomm — a data point for your capture-vs-cooperative-kernel-race question: a *second* DSA model (`GlmMoeDsa`, not the one you're running) on 6× GB10 under `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` captured and served clean across my runs — no wedge. Caveat: my soak windows are far shorter than your ~45h MTBF, and it's a different model + topology (PP=3 vs your 4-node), so weak evidence at best. If it'd help discriminate, I can run a longer soak on the FULL decode graph and report whether it wedges.
