@mzzhome-ai — your two failures are on the community image
(`0.26.1rc1.dev191+gaef9bd1e9`, this PR's `d64074e6f0` applied onto a different base), which is
neither this branch's previous head nor its current one. If they still bite you after moving to
`sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260802`, please say so and include the engine config dump line;
we have the 4-node shape wired up now and can re-run it directly.

### Two defects found and fixed

**1. `num_speculative_tokens` must equal `dspark_block_size`, not merely reach it.**
The validator accepted `>=`, and its own error message recommended exceeding it
("Use `num_speculative_tokens=5` or larger (e.g. 7)"), as does the HF model card. The drafter
emits exactly one block per pass, so the extra slots are structurally unreachable. Measured with
a prose workload (`scripts/run_dspark_acceptance_probe.sh` in our harness):

| configuration | mean acceptance length (3 samples) | avg draft acceptance rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nst=5 probabilistic | 2.15 / 2.16 / **2.19** | 22.9 / 23.2 / **23.8%** |
| nst=7 probabilistic | 1.61 / 1.75 / 1.95 | 8.7 / 10.7 / 13.6% |
| nst=5 greedy | 1.82 / 2.06 / **2.23** | 16.4 / 21.2 / **24.5%** |
| nst=7 greedy | 1.57 / 1.66 / 1.75 | 8.2 / 9.5 / 10.8% |

All three samples per configuration are shown rather than a single figure — the probe reads
whatever `SpecDecoding metrics` lines vLLM flushed inside its window, and a low sample means
"not much steady traffic in that slice", not a worse drafter. Both `nst=7` runs also hit
connection errors partway through (5/8 and 2/8 completions returned), so read their spread as
noisier than the `nst=5` rows.

**The structural result does not depend on any of that**: the 7th draft position accepted
**0.000 in every sample**, and the 6th accepted 0.000 in all but one sample (0.004 there).
`nst=7` drafts 40% more tokens per step and cannot accept the last two.

The validator now requires equality.

@allenh1 — your [reference config](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5151513526)
runs `num_speculative_tokens: 7` as a design point; on this measurement that is 2 of every 7
drafted tokens (~29%) spent on positions that never accept, for worse acceptance overall. Worth
dropping to 5. (Thank you for posting the
full config — we have recorded it as our known-good 4-node reference, including the delta against
the configuration that fails on identical hardware.)

One caveat on measuring this yourself: **use prose**. On counting or repeated text the Markov head
alone reaches 68–100% acceptance even with the neural draft path degraded, which hides the effect
entirely. @kelnei flagged this in the original report and it is worth repeating.

**2. `method: "mtp"` was silently rewritten to `"dspark"`.**
The auto-detection preserved an explicitly requested method only for
`eagle`/`eagle3`/`dflash`/`dspark`. Since 0731 folded the DSpark draft into the main checkpoint,
`dspark_block_size` is now present in *every* DSv4 config, so `method: "mtp"` fell through to the
dspark branch, was rewritten, and then failed validation with a DSpark message the user never
asked for. An explicitly requested method is no longer overridden.

### MTP is gone in 0731

This is a model-side change, not something this branch can restore. `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`
ships **no MTP heads**: `enorm`, `hnorm`, `e_proj`, `h_proj` and `shared_head` are all absent from
the weight index, and `mtp.{0,1,2}.*` now carries the DSpark-style `main_norm` / `main_proj`
structure (matching `dspark_target_layer_ids: [40, 41, 42]`). Fixing defect 2 lets the request
keep `method="mtp"`, but it then fails at weight load. The MTP code paths are retained for older
checkpoints.

**If you were running MTP2, DSpark nst=5 is the replacement.**

### Also absorbed

- [#49335](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49335) (@Wollac) — mxfp8 activation scales
  swizzled after DP/EP dispatch. Inert at DP=1, taken for the multi-node DP users of this branch.
  Verified non-vacuous: its test passes with the fix and fails with the `mxfp8` term removed.
- [#50686](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50686) (@ateska) — consecutive assistant
  messages merged in prompt encoding. Reproduced here before taking it; note it also helps the
  default `drop_thinking=True` path by removing a spurious mid-turn `<|end_of_sentence|>`, which
  the PR description does not call out.
- [#50693](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50693) (@xijiaat) — **test only**. This branch
  does not have that failure: `_prefill_workspace_topk_bound` returns early for
  `compress_ratio <= 1` and never reaches the buffer. The regression test is valuable anyway and
  is now carried (adapted, since it asserts upstream's inlined workspace tuple and ours differs).

### Performance

`llama-benchy` on 0731 + DSpark nst=5, versus the **full** recorded range of the MTP2 baselines on
the previous checkpoint. Cross-checkpoint, so read it as a sanity band rather than a controlled A/B:

| metric | prior MTP2 range (n=10) | 0731 + DSpark | vs band |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pp2048 @ d8192 | 1339.11 – 1400.81 | **1432.23** ± 11.74 | **above** |
| pp2048 @ d16384 | 1308.77 – 1344.68 | **1356.56** ± 11.78 | **above** |
| pp2048 @ d32768 | 1089.05 – 1226.63 | **1250.75** ± 2.18 | **above** |
| ctx_pp @ d8192 | 1757.16 – 1876.01 | 1816.97 ± 5.89 | inside |
| ctx_pp @ d16384 | 1769.85 – 1842.16 | 1817.43 ± 1.43 | inside |
| ctx_pp @ d32768 | 1595.87 – 1756.01 | 1740.22 ± 2.87 | inside |
| tg128 @ d8192 | 36.27 – 43.08 | 41.72 ± 5.09 | inside |
| tg128 @ d16384 | 34.59 – 43.14 | 37.92 ± 9.92 | inside |
| tg128 @ d32768 | 32.77 – 42.91 | 34.88 ± 5.78 | inside |
| ctx_tg @ d8192 | 38.52 – 43.01 | 39.37 ± 2.34 | inside |
| ctx_tg @ d16384 | 39.29 – 43.07 | **35.07** ± 0.67 | **below, −10.7%** |
| ctx_tg @ d32768 | 38.02 – 42.73 | 40.70 ± 6.85 | inside |

**Batched prefill (pp2048) is above the historical band at all three depths** (+2.2% / +0.9% /
+2.0%) — the only consistent directional move here. Clearing the max of ten prior runs at all
three depths says more than any single one of those margins would: +0.9% is inside this metric's
own resolution, so read the consistency rather than the magnitudes. No sign of DSpark being
slower than MTP2 was.

One caveat reported rather than buried: **`ctx_tg @ d16384` sits 10.7% below its historical
minimum**, the only metric outside its band. It is non-monotonic against our own neighbouring
depths (39.37 at d8192, 40.70 at d32768, where history has d16384 ≈ d8192), which points at a
single-run artifact rather than a depth-specific regression — but it is unresolved until
repeated.

A warning if you benchmark this branch yourself: the `±` in a benchy row is the spread of the three
runs *inside one invocation*, and it is routinely 5–30× smaller than the build-to-build spread. Our
full history spans 31% on tg128 @ d32768 and ~1.3% on ctx_pp. Anything under ~15% on tg or ~2% on
ctx_pp is not resolvable this way.

### Correctness

| | DSpark nst=5 | no speculation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K (8-shot, flexible) | 0.9394 | 0.9500 |
| GSM8K (8-shot, strict) | 0.9363 | 0.9484 |
| instruction-following (JSON-only) | PASS | PASS |
| long-context recall, c=1 | 2/2 | 2/2 |
| illegal-access / assertion in serve log | 0 | 0 |
| draft acceptance (prose) | mean 2.08, 21.7% | — |

The GSM8K gap (1.06 pp flexible / 1.21 pp strict) is **not** resolvable from single runs — our
measured single-run spread on this gate is ~1.1 pp. We are following up with three runs per cell.
It is well short of what a broken draft path would cost. Note `0731` is the first checkpoint where
the strict and flexible extractors disagree at all; on every prior baseline they were identical.

### Reference configuration

2x GB10 (sm_121), TP=2, the shape everything above was measured on:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --max-model-len 49152 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
```

No environment variables are needed: `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE` and
`..._PREFILL` both default to on. (`TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.1a` is a *build*-time setting for
GB10, not a serve one.) For multi-node, add `--nnodes`, `--node-rank`, `--master-addr`,
`--master-port` and `--headless` on the workers in the usual way.

Notes that cost us time and may cost you some:

- `num_speculative_tokens` **must be 5** — see defect 1 above.
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` is mandatory: DSv4's `fp8_ds_mla` attention asserts an fp8 KV layout, so
  the default `auto` fails at model construction. Not DSpark-specific.
- On multi-node GB10, pin `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7` on **every** node; a rebuild silently reverts
  it to torch's bundled version and a per-node mismatch hangs the NCCL handshake.
- 4-node TP=4 works (we ran @mzzhome-ai's shape); @allenh1's posted config is a good starting point
  if you are on Ray rather than mp.

### Dependency pins on this head

torch 2.13.0 · triton 3.7.1 · FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 (python **and** cubin, matched) ·
nvidia-nccl-cu13 2.30.7 · tilelang 0.1.12 · nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.0 · quack-kernels 0.6.1

AI assistance was used for this update; every measurement quoted above was run on real hardware
and every claim was checked against the code or the logs before posting.

- mzzhome-ai · comment · 2026-08-02T17:21:02Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5159488836)

### Confirmed working on 4x DGX Spark (GB10, sm121): both failures fixed, generation speed doubled

Follow-up to my earlier report in this thread (the `num_tokens > 64` crash on the FlashInfer SM120 path, and the `swa_metadata missing tile_sched entry for compress_ratio=1` assertion on `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4`). **Both are gone**, and DSpark speculative decoding is now running in production here.

**What I built**

Tag `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260802`, commit `9a94c542926ab4da2024ae46e47c9efcf5826476`.

I rebuilt **only vLLM**, inside the community image `eugr/spark-vllm:nightly-20260802`, deliberately leaving its torch 2.11, FlashInfer 0.6.17 and system NCCL 2.30.7 untouched — this branch is main plus patches, and that image already ran main on those versions.

```
export TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.1a
export MAX_JOBS=6
pip install -v --no-build-isolation --no-deps .
```

`--no-deps` matters on a metered link: without it pip pulls torch 2.13 over the wire. `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.1a` brings the build down to about 25 minutes on the Spark's own CPU. Missing build dependencies in that image were `setuptools-rust`, `setuptools-scm` and `cmake`.

**Configuration** — 4 nodes, TP=4 with expert parallelism, RoCE between nodes, official BF16/FP8 checkpoint of `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`.

Worth stating explicitly, since it is probably not the default assumption for a 4-node setup: **no Ray**. This runs on the multiprocessing backend, `--distributed-executor-backend mp --nnodes 4 --node-rank N`, with `--headless` on the three workers and the rendezvous on the rank-0 node. Each node is launched by hand with the same script. I don't expect the executor choice to affect the kernel paths at issue here, but if anyone reproduces under Ray and sees different behaviour, that's the difference.

```
--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
--enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 1
--enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256
--max-num-seqs 4 --max-model-len 1000000 --max-num-batched-tokens 30000
--max-cudagraph-capture-size 48 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune
--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --load-format instanttensor --trust-remote-code
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.84
```

No `--attention-backend` override is needed any more: the default now resolves correctly on sm121. The `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` workaround from my earlier comment should not be carried forward.

**Results**

| | before (no draft) | with DSpark |
|---|---|---|
| single stream | ~30 tok/s | **~60 tok/s** |
| 2 concurrent | ~50 tok/s | **~80 tok/s** |

Acceptance rate, from `/metrics`: **33-45% on prose**, 60-80% on structured/repetitive output, mean acceptance length 2.4-4.2. Stable across long agentic sessions.

**Two notes that may be useful to others on this hardware**

1. The new check requiring `num_speculative_tokens == dspark_block_size` is the right call. With 7 against the model's declared block size of 5, acceptance collapsed to 8-13% **silently** — no warning, just a draft nobody accepts. An error is much better than that.

2. Sizing the CUDA graph capture: the decode batch is `max_num_seqs * (K+1)`, so 4*6 = 24 here. Anything below that and decode silently falls back to eager, which cancels most of the gain.

**Why the speedup is this large on a multi-node Spark cluster.** Watching the interconnect during a request, prefill moves ~30 GB/s between nodes while decode drops to ~1 GB/s — decode is latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound, so the link sits mostly idle. Speculative decoding spends exactly that idle latency. It also means the draft and request concurrency compete for the same slack: my concurrency-2 bonus fell from +67% to +33% once the draft was on.

THANKS for the quick turnaround on this!
Happy to keep testing patches on this cluster — four GB10 nodes over RoCE is an awkward shape to come by.

- alexbi29 · comment · 2026-08-03T09:44:07Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5164782204)

Heads-up on a crash we root-caused while running this branch in production
(DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, SM120, TP2 + expert parallelism, DSpark k=5). It is
reachable on stock `main` too, but the DSv4 hash-MoE path is what makes it fatal
rather than silent, so it is likely to bite anyone on this branch.

**Symptom.** `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` on every TP rank after a few
minutes of bursty concurrency, surfacing at an unrelated sync point
(`gpu/async_utils.py` `copy_event.synchronize()`). Independent of
`--async-scheduling`. Often preceded by the spec-decode acceptance rate
collapsing (we saw mean AL 1.53 at 249 drafted tok/s just before one fault).

**Chain.**

1. The sampler forms a token id as `block_idx * BLOCK_SIZE + idx` over a tile
   whose out-of-vocab tail lanes are `-inf`. On a fully `-inf` logits row the
   reduction settles on a tail lane and emits `token_id == vocab_size`
   (`129280 == 15*8192 + 6400`). Three sites: `sample/gumbel.py` and two in
   `spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py`.
2. Nothing bounds a sampled token id, so it reaches `input_ids`.
3. `dsv4HashTopkSoftplusSqrt` does `tid2eid[token_id * 6 + lane]` with no bound
   on `token_id`, reads past the `[vocab_size, 6]` table, and returns a garbage
   "expert" — in our dumps the bit pattern of a neighbouring float tensor.
4. That value either faults immediately on `input[warp * num_experts + expert]`
   or is written into `topk_ids` and later kills
   `_swiglu_limit_pad_aware_kernel` / `moe_sum_vec_kernel`, both of which guard
   the `expert_map` gather with a sign check only.

Only 3 of 43 layers are hash-MoE (`num_hash_layers=3`), which is why it is
intermittent.

**Fixes filed upstream:**

- #50843 — bound the tile-local argmax to `vocab_size` in the samplers (the root
  cause; Python/Triton only, no rebuild)
- #50844 — bound `token_id` before the `tid2eid` gather in the hash-MoE router
- #50845 — bound the `expert_map` gathers in four MoE kernels (defence in depth;
  also fixes one that was entirely unmasked)

#50843 alone stops the crash for us. #50844 is still worth having since
`prompt_token_ids` come from the API and the kernel should not trust that a token
id is in range. Note `get_local_expert_id()` in `moe_align_sum_kernels.cu`
already applies exactly the bound that #50845 adds to its neighbours, and this
branch's own `d64074e6f0` ("bound the block-table gather in
compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens") is the same bug class.

**Verification.** 40-minute randomized-concurrency run at the load that
previously faulted in 90 s - 5.5 min: zero out-of-range `input_ids` (was
~78/min), zero coredumps, zero faults. Reproducer and CUDA-core-dump recipe in
the PR descriptions.

Two things we did **not** resolve, in case they ring a bell:

1. We could not build a synthetic input that makes the tile argmax select an
   out-of-vocab lane (neither an all-`-inf` nor an all-NaN row does it). The
   causal link is from a clean A/B under production load: unclamped ~78
   bad ids/min, `gumbel.py` clamped only 4 over ~15 min, all three clamped
   0 over 30 min. So the fix is validated but the precise trigger is not.
2. Whatever produces that degenerate logits row is still there. The clamp makes
   the sampled id addressable; it does not make the row meaningful.


- fuzzifikation · comment · 2026-08-03T14:33:28Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5167733816)

**SM120 DSpark draft-decode gap (`num_tokens > 64`) on the stock-deps path**

Testing **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731** on **2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, 96 GiB each)**, TP=2, EP enabled, vLLM **0.26.0** (stock deps), with DSpark:

```
--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}'
--block-size 256
```

Once the engine gets past model load / KV allocation, the DSpark drafter decodes with `num_speculative_tokens` (7) tokens and dies in the SM120 FlashInfer sparse-MLA decode path:

```
tvm.error.InternalError: Check failed: num_tokens > 64 (7 vs. 64) :
Decode (num_tokens <= 64) must go through sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv3_2
or sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4; got num_tokens=7
```

Stack: `DSparkSpeculator._generate_draft` → `dspark.py` draft layer forward → `DeepseekV4FlashInferMLASparseAttention._forward_decode` → `flashinfer_trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` → `sparse_mla_sm120_paged_attention` (TVM `ICHECK_GT(num_tokens, 64)`).

Root cause I traced in `flashinfer/mla/_sparse_mla_sm120.py`: the SM120 DSV4 **decode** dispatch requires `page_block_size == 64` (`_DECODE_DSV4_PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE`), but the model runs at `--block-size 256`. So a small (≤64 token) draft decode fails the `page_block_size == 64` gate, falls through to the generic paged-attention orchestrator, and that path hard-asserts `num_tokens > 64`.

This looks squarely like the SM12x draft-path integration this PR is building — is there a plan to make the DSpark draft cache use a 64-token block size (or otherwise route the ≤64-token draft decode to the dedicated `sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4` kernel) for the stock-deps path? Happy to test a build of this branch on the RTX PRO 6000 config, including the non-spec baseline.

- tobymao · comment · 2026-08-03T16:28:44Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5169039345)

**Output corruption under concurrent load, bisected to `DeepseekV4EagerScratchPool`.**

We run DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 from this branch (4-GPU TP=4 SM12x deployment, 1M context, DSpark spec decode, fork tag synced past v0.26.1rc0) and hit production output corruption that bisects to the eager scratch pool.

**Symptom.** Under concurrent mixed prefill+decode load, a random co-batched request's output degenerates: leaked `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` tokens mid-sentence, multilingual token salad in English text, terminal single-token repetition. Quiet or serial traffic never triggers it (~40 clean trials including 415k-token prompts and 16k-token generations).

**Bisection** (load harness: two concurrent long-context `reasoning_effort=max` streams + short-request churn with mid-stream client aborts; ~15-min rounds):

| build | rounds | result |
|---|---|---|
| this branch, pool active | 7 | corrupt 7/7 — reproduces with spec decode on *and* off, and with two unrelated suspect-reverts |
| same build, only `eager_scratch_pool = None` at the construction site | 2 | clean 2/2 |
| pre-pool build (v0.26.0-era) | 2 | clean 2/2 |

**Mechanism (from reading `eager_scratch.py`).** The aux storage is sized with `max()` across the fp4-indexer / global-topk / compressor template families, so all three families alias the same bytes from offset 0, per the comment's assumption that they are temporally disjoint. The attention eager break runs the indexer/compressor on parallel aux streams, and under load the disjointness breaks — one consumer clobbers another mid-read (garbled top-k indices → attention over wrong KV → corrupted logits for whichever request is co-batched). A second potential hazard is the cross-layer reuse of each template under the same aux-stream overlap.

**Fix.** We are currently validating `sum()` sizing with per-template base offsets (costs only the aux views' footprint, keeps the Q-buffer win) and will follow up here with results and a patch. If the cross-layer reuse also proves racy, event-ordering — or defaulting the pool off behind a flag — may be needed.

<details>
<summary>Self-contained reproducer (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving DSv4-Flash from this branch)</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproducer: DSv4 output corruption under concurrent mixed load.

Targets any OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash from the
SM12x branch (eager scratch pool active). Runs the load mix that triggers
the race, scans every stream for the corruption signature, prints a verdict.

  python3 dsv4_corruption_repro.py http://HOST:8000/v1 deepseek-v4-flash

Set OPENAI_API_KEY if the endpoint requires auth.

Load shape (one round, ~15 min on a 4-GPU TP=4 SM12x deployment -- slower or
differently-shaped hardware may need more rounds; the defect is a timing race):
  - "victim":  ~90k-token prompt, reasoning_effort=max, top_p=0.95, 16k gen
  - "partner": ~300k-token prompt, same sampling, 16k gen
  - churn:     a stream of ~30k-token requests, each hard-aborted mid-generation
Corruption signature: leaked BOS special tokens mid-text, dense non-Latin
runs in English output, or long single-token repetition.

No external deps; filler text is synthesized (any text works -- the trigger
is batching, not content).
"""
import itertools
import json
import os
import re
import socket
import sys
import threading
import time
import unicodedata
import urllib.request

BASE = (sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://localhost:8000/v1").rstrip("/")
MODEL = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "deepseek-v4-flash"
ROUNDS = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 2
URL = BASE + "/chat/completions"
HEADERS = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
if os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
    HEADERS["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY']}"

BOS = re.compile(r"begin▁of▁sentence|begin_of_sentence")


def filler(n_tokens: int, salt: int) -> str:
    """~n_tokens of varied pseudo-code so prefix caching can't collapse it."""
    words = ("def parse config batch tensor stream index cache block quant "
             "route merge scan flush emit align pool slot fuse probe grid "
             "shard chunk").split()
    out = [f"# corpus salt {salt}\n"]
    rng = itertools.cycle(range(7919))
    for i in range(n_tokens // 8):
        k = (i * 31 + salt * 7 + next(rng)) % len(words)
        out.append(f"{words[k]}_{i % 997}(x{i % 89}, y{(i * 13) % 61})"
                   + ("\n" if i % 6 == 5 else "; "))
    return "".join(out)


def nonlatin(text: str) -> int:
    return sum(1 for ch in text
               if ord(ch) >= 0x2E80 and unicodedata.category(ch).startswith("L"))


def max_run(text: str) -> int:
    best = cur = 1
    toks = text.split()
    for a, b in zip(toks, toks[1:]):
        cur = cur + 1 if a == b else 1
        best = max(best, cur)
    return best if toks else 0


def stream_request(label: str, ctx_tokens: int, max_tokens: int, salt: int,
                   results: dict, abort_after: int | None = None):
    body = {
        "model": MODEL,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content":
                      filler(ctx_tokens, salt) +
                      "\n\nWrite an exhaustive design review of this code. "
                      "Think carefully and be thorough."}],
        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
        "reasoning_effort": "max",   # long generations widen the exposure window
        "top_p": 0.95,
        "stream": True,
    }
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, json.dumps(body).encode(), HEADERS)
    text, onset = [], None
    try:
        resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=7200)
        for raw in resp:
            raw = raw.decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()
            if not raw.startswith("data: ") or raw == "data: [DONE]":
                continue
            try:
                d = json.loads(raw[6:])
            except ValueError:
                continue
            for ch in d.get("choices", []):
                delta = ch.get("delta") or {}
                piece = (delta.get("reasoning_content") or "") + (delta.get("content") or "")
                if piece:
                    text.append(piece)
                    if onset is None and (BOS.search(piece) or nonlatin(piece) >= 3):
                        onset = sum(len(t) for t in text)
                        print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {label}: "
                              f"CORRUPTION ONSET at ~{onset} chars", flush=True)
            if abort_after and sum(len(t) for t in text) >= abort_after:
                try:  # hard client abort mid-generation (part of the churn)
                    sock = resp.fp.raw._sock
                    sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER,
                                    b"\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00")
                except Exception:
                    pass
                resp.close()
                break
    except Exception as e:
        results[label] = {"error": str(e)[:120]}
        return
    full = "".join(text)
    results[label] = {
        "chars": len(full),
        "bos_leaks": len(BOS.findall(full)),
        "nonlatin": nonlatin(full),
        "max_token_run": max_run(full[-4000:]),
        "onset": onset,
    }


def churn_loop(stop: threading.Event, results: dict):
    i = 0
    while not stop.is_set():
        stream_request(f"churn{i}", 30_000, 8_000, salt=100 + i,
                       results=results, abort_after=2_000)
        i += 1


for rnd in range(1, ROUNDS + 1):
    print(f"=== round {rnd} ===", flush=True)
    results: dict = {}
    stop = threading.Event()
    threads = [
        threading.Thread(target=stream_request,
                         args=("victim", 90_000, 16_000, rnd * 2, results)),
        threading.Thread(target=stream_request,
                         args=("partner", 300_000, 16_000, rnd * 2 + 1, results)),
        threading.Thread(target=churn_loop, args=(stop, results)),
    ]
    for t in threads[:2]:
        t.start()
    time.sleep(60)          # let the big prefills get going before churn
    threads[2].start()
    for t in threads[:2]:
        t.join()
    stop.set()
    threads[2].join()

    corrupt = False
    for label in ("victim", "partner"):
        r = results.get(label, {})
        bad = bool(r.get("onset") or r.get("bos_leaks") or
                   r.get("nonlatin", 0) > 20 or r.get("max_token_run", 0) > 30)
        corrupt |= bad
        print(f"  {label}: {r} -> {'CORRUPT' if bad else 'clean'}", flush=True)
    print(f"round {rnd} verdict: {'CORRUPT' if corrupt else 'clean'}", flush=True)
```

</details>


- tobymao · comment · 2026-08-03T19:40:01Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5170919503)

**Validation follow-up.**

- **`sum()` sizing (per-template base offsets): tested, insufficient.** With the cross-template aliasing removed, we still hit 1 corrupt round of 2 (victim onset ~27k chars into its generation; BOS leaks + non-Latin salad). So the live race is not only the `max()`-sizing aliasing — the **cross-layer reuse** of each template family under aux-stream overlap is implicated.
- **Pool disabled: fully clean** (`eager_scratch_pool = None` at the construction site) — 2/2 clean rounds under the same load, and it's what we now run in production.
- **The reproducer above is validated against the affected build**: 1 corrupt round in 2 (round-2 onset within the victim's first tokens).

Recommendation: gate the pool behind an env flag defaulting off (e.g. `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_EAGER_SCRATCH_POOL`) until per-layer buffers or stream-ordering events make the reuse safe — sizing alone doesn't. Happy to send the gate patch against this branch.


- tobymao · comment · 2026-08-03T21:37:25Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5172010656)

**Tested your fix commit (d42b8d9) directly under the same harness — the race persists.**

- **Your per-family-offset commit**: corrupt in round 1 (victim onset ~23k chars into its generation, same BOS/salad signature). Consistent with our follow-up above: sizing removes the cross-family aliasing but not the failure.
- **Double-buffering on top of your commit** (two aux storage sets, every accessor alternates phase — should defeat any adjacent-use race): corrupt 1 round of 3 (onset ~28k chars, 4,232 leaked specials).
- Observed pattern across variants: original pool 7/7 rounds corrupt → sizing/alternation variants ~1 in 2–3 → pool disabled 0 corrupt. Mitigations narrow the window; only removal closes it.

A hypothesis for why alternation still fails: in mixed decode+prefill batches the indexer path can acquire the same family more than once per layer, so phase parity shifts and consecutive layers can collide again — and mixed batches are exactly the corruption condition. More generally: the pre-pool code was race-free for free because per-call transients go through the caching allocator, whose cross-stream reuse is event-guarded; the pool reuses memory without that machinery. Getting it safe probably needs producer-waits-on-consumer events placed with knowledge of the actual stream/call graph — which is yours, not ours.

Until then we'd recommend defaulting the pool off (flag-gated); that config is 0-for-N corrupt under our harness and is what we run in production.

pool handing out raw reused memory drops that guarantee no matter how the bytes are

had been fine, and that's the more useful question.

same family more than once per layer in a mixed batch, alternation desynchronises and
adjacent layers collide again — and mixed batches are the corruption condition.

stream/call graph, and agreed that's ours to write. Not something to land at the end of a
long night against a defect people are hitting in production, so: off by default now,
events later, and the flag stays until it's genuinely safe rather than narrowed.

One data point from our side that may save you a detour. We ran the pool question against
a *different* symptom — long-context recall under concurrency on the V2 model runner — over
14 serves, and the pool is not implicated there:

| | good | bad |
|---|---|---|
| pool on | 2 | 6 |
| pool off | 3 | 3 |

Fisher ≈ 0.3. So whatever else the pool does, it isn't behind that one, and if you see
recall oddities separate from the output corruption they're likely a different bug.


- jasl · comment · 2026-08-03T22:07:53Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5172268998)

@fuzzifikation Your root cause is correct, and this branch is not affected by it — you
should be able to drop the workaround entirely.

**Your analysis is right for stock 0.26.0.** `_decode_dsv4_dispatchable` requires
`page_block_size == _DECODE_DSV4_PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE` (64), so at `--block-size 256` the
DSv4 decode dispatch can never succeed, it falls through to the prefill orchestrator,
and that asserts `num_tokens > 64`. Nothing to do with your `num_speculative_tokens`.

Worth knowing there are **two independent gates in that same predicate** that produce
the identical error, and this thread has now hit both:

```python
return (num_tokens <= _DECODE_MAX_TOKENS
        and d_qk == 512
        and page_block_size == _DECODE_DSV4_PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE      # yours
        and (num_heads, topk) in _DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH)          # vllm-project/vllm#50720
```

The other one is `dspark_markov_rank=256` landing outside the instantiated `topk` set,
which is what vllm-project/vllm#50720 tracks and what flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3989
fixes. Same message, different gate — so if you patch one and still see it, check the
other before assuming the fix didn't take.

**Why this branch doesn't hit yours.** We run `--block-size 256` too, and our DSv4
decode goes through the SM120 packed sparse-MLA path without trouble. The reason is that
the DSv4 packed KV cache is laid out in **64-token pages internally**
(`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/cache_utils.py`, "K Cache block layout
(block_size=64 tokens)"), independent of vLLM's logical `--block-size`. FlashInfer derives
`page_block_size` from the *tensor geometry* (`_packed_kv_page_block_size`), not from the
engine config, so the 64-page layout satisfies the gate whatever `--block-size` you pass.
Confirmed empirically rather than by reading: our serve logs
`FlashInfer SM120 packed sparse-MLA decode via the low-level runner` at `block_size: 256`
and serves normally — if the gate were failing we would be getting your exact assertion.

So no need to change `--block-size`, and no need to wait on a FlashInfer dispatch change
for this particular failure.

**And yes, please do test.** That would be genuinely valuable to us rather than a
courtesy: our CI is 2× GB10 (SM121a), so every SM120 discrete-GPU result on this PR is
currently someone else's measurement that we cannot reproduce. We have an RTX PRO 6000
box of our own but it is out of service at the moment. Both the DSpark run and the
non-spec baseline you offered would be useful; the reference configuration is in the PR
description, and it is worth pulling the current head — several fixes landed in the last
day, including one illegal-memory-access in the DSpark draft sampler that only triggers
with non-greedy sampling.

## Validated on both architectures

| gate | SM121 (2× GB10) | SM120 (2× RTX PRO 6000) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| serve, DSpark nst=5, `--block-size 256` | ✅ | ✅ |
| jasl/vllm#19 instruction-following | PASS | PASS |
| arthur recall c=1 / c=12 | 2/2 · 22,23,22 | 2/2 · 22,23 |

**This is the first head we validated on SM120 ourselves.** Until now every SM120 result on this
thread was someone else's measurement we could not reproduce; we rebuilt a 2× RTX PRO 6000 box as
a first-party target specifically because that was an unhealthy position to argue from.

Two things that immediately paid for:

- **@fuzzifikation's `Check failed: num_tokens > 64` does not reproduce here.** Same hardware
  class, same `--block-size 256`: the serve comes up, the assertion never appears, and the SM120
  packed decode path is confirmed engaged. The DSv4 packed KV cache uses 64-token pages
  independent of the logical block size. I had asserted that from reading the code; it is now
  measured.
- **@alexbi29's tuned FP8 configs are demonstrably active** on the device they target — zero
  `Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config` warnings. When merging jasl/vllm#37 I wrote that we
  vouched for correctness but not performance because GB10 is not in the alias table. That gap is
  closed.

## Prefill: V1 vs V2 runner, and why V1 stays the default

Prefill was never measured for the runner comparison. Now done properly — 10 blocks, both arms
inside each node pair, exact permutation test, Holm-corrected, **decision rule committed before
any data was collected**:

| | V2 / V1 | exact p |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ctx_pp @ d8192 / 16384 / 32768 | **+1.18% / +1.11% / +1.61%** | 0.0020 / 0.0137 / 0.0020 |
| pp2048 @ d8192 / 16384 / 32768 | **+4.18% / +4.18% / +4.33%** | all 0.0020 |

All six survive Holm; both pairs agree in direction. Decode is **not** resolved in either
direction and is reported for the record only.

**V1 remains the default anyway.** Across 14 independent serves on one build and configuration,
roughly two thirds of V2 serves land in a state that loses most long-context needles (arthur c=12
down to 3/24) while the rest match V1 at 22–24. The mode is fixed at startup, stable within a
serve, and nothing we have found predicts it — worse operationally than a consistent deficit,
because a deployment can run clean for days and restart into the bad mode. Cause **not
identified**; the eager scratch pool is cleanly exonerated for it (pool on 2/8 good vs pool off
3/6 good). If you opt into V2 with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, know this.

## Two corrections to earlier comments in this thread

**1. On @tobymao's scratch-pool report** — I proposed `sum()` sizing with per-family offsets as
the fix. They tested that exact commit and it was still corrupt. Their diagnosis is the one worth
keeping: the pre-pool code was race-free *for free* because per-call transients go through the
caching allocator, whose cross-stream reuse is event-guarded. My change addressed *which bytes
overlap* when the real invariant is *when reuse is safe* — which is also why their double-buffered
variant failed. No static partitioning fixes it. Hence: off by default until events are placed
against the real stream graph.

**2. On our own measurements** — the n=8 sampling that established V2's recall deficit and drove
the revert took eight gate runs from **one serve**. It measured within-serve variance while the
quantity that varies is across-serve: n raised on the wrong axis. Anything in this thread derived
from that number should be read with the 14-serve figures above instead.

Related to the second point, for anyone benchmarking this branch: a coarse range comparison over
the same 10 blocks that produced the prefill table returns "no measurable difference" on all six
cells. The blocked paired design is what makes a ~1% effect visible at all. The `±` printed in a
benchy row is within-invocation spread and runs 5–30× smaller than build-to-build.

Not fixed and stated as such: V2's recall cause, and the eager scratch pool's cross-layer reuse
(gated off rather than repaired).

### Stochastic long-context output corruption on `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260804`, 2× GB10 — not DSpark, not prefix caching, not #50686

Reporting a corruption that survives every mitigation discussed in this thread, including disabling speculative decoding entirely. I've tried to eliminate as much as I can from outside the code before posting; the remaining candidates are all in the sparse-MLA / fp8_ds_mla long-context path, which I can't isolate from here.

**Setup.** 2× DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP=2 across nodes over RoCE, `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, built from tag `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260804`. Both nodes verified running `vllm 20260805.dev0+g0f59188db.d20260804`, and both confirmed to have the eager-scratch-pool gate and the #50686 encoder fix present in the installed package.

```
--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4 --block-size 256
--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --load-format instanttensor
--max-model-len 500000 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 4
--enable-chunked-prefill --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-auto-tool-choice
--enable-flashinfer-autotune --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4
--tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4
--tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2
--override-generation-config '{"top_p":0.95, "temperature":0.6}'
--default-chat-template-kwargs.reasoning_effort max
--default-chat-template-kwargs.thinking true
env: VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_EAGER_SCRATCH_POOL=0  VLLM_DSPARK_FORWARD_CUDAGRAPH=1
     VLLM_DSPARK_FORWARD_CUDAGRAPH_ALLOW_TP=0  VLLM_DSPARK_REPLICATE_MARKOV_W1=1
     VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE=1  VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1  VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1
     VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1  VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_{DECODE,PREFILL}=1
     VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1  VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0
     (no VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER, no --async-scheduling)
```

**Symptom.** At long context the output degrades stochastically. In milder cases it is semantically broken prose with **no special tokens at all**; in worse cases the model emits `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` (often hundreds of times), `<｜DSML｜` markup as plain text, or reserved slots such as `<｜place▁holder▁no▁764｜>`. Identical requests sometimes succeed, so this is not deterministic.

**Repro.** One non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions`, 33,175 prompt tokens, 2 tools, `reasoning_effort: max`, `thinking: true`. Originally an agentic reviewer thread (122 messages alternating assistant-with-`tool_calls` and `tool` results), but **a plain single-turn prompt of similar length corrupts too**, so the multi-turn/tool shape is not required.

#### With DSpark (`nst=5`, `probabilistic`), same request ×4

| run | completion tokens | leaked `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` | tool_calls | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 255 | 0 | 1 | correct |
| 2 | 365 | 354 | 0 | completion is *only* BOS |
| 3 | 8 | 1 | 0 | `I've reviewed all<BOS>cd e0e4<BOS>def it = is.` |
| 4 | 18 | 2 | 0 | `Let me step back<BOS>#include be` |

#### Without speculative decoding (`--speculative-config` removed), same request ×4

| run | completion tokens | leaked | tool_calls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1500 | 104 BOS + 10 `<｜DSML｜` | 0 |
| 2 | 148 | 104 BOS | 0 |
| 3 | 1242 | 104 BOS | 1 (`submit_report`) |
| 4 | 119 | 10 BOS + 2 `<｜place▁holder▁no▁N｜>` | 0 |

**The corruption is not caused by DSpark — but DSpark changes its severity completely.** With speculation on, corrupt generations collapse after 8–365 tokens and never produce a tool call. With it off, the model produces 1242–1500 token answers and one run completed the task correctly despite 104 BOS in its reasoning channel. Speculation appears to turn a survivable defect into a fatal one, which is consistent with the acceptance numbers below.

Two details that may narrow it: the BOS run length was **exactly 104** in three independent generations (once in `content`, twice in `reasoning_content`), which looks like a structural boundary rather than ordinary degeneration; and corruption is not uniform within a response — run 3 above returned a valid parsed tool call while its reasoning channel was destroyed.

#### Leak counts understate it — degradation starts earlier, with zero special tokens

Counting special tokens alone is misleading. These runs all reported **0 leaked tokens** and are still broken (verbatim first ~110 chars of `reasoning_content`):

| prompt tokens | output |
| --- | --- |
| 22,294 | `Let me now take stock. Careful — that is, I have been given a message that I realize that's on the report da` |
| 23,893 | `All thirty‑eight files inspected against the same self‑reference repeated. Every hunk of the view enforcement, neither assemblied reads ho` |
| 27,715 | `Let me analyze what I've read are all report — every one of the places comply the reviewer inspects the mean` |
| 30,445 | `The files are all identical — that phrase everywhere, and where the line number that summary non tensors of` |

Coherent outputs at 3,145 / 8,059 / 15,703 / 25,506 in the same session, so it is context-correlated but **not a clean threshold** — the earliest corruption I recorded was at **15,703** prompt tokens (1,440 leaked BOS in one run, while three further runs at the same size were clean). A recent 3-run set at 33,175 gave: one coherent, one that parroted the instruction back verbatim, one word salad.

An extreme sample (33k, with DSpark), showing reserved-vocabulary slots and multi-script salad:

```
Let tracksuchy `. generously rec Magn phosphory Theo�יוון<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>采 sehat অত国家和地区ETHignty开口说道一转остьmass Mouse是非<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>synス Gamma styles体重oxylic还是会 절itles稠्म-focused<｜place▁holder▁no▁764｜>...
```

Sampling reserved/unused vocab slots alongside this kind of multi-script mixing reads to me like a corrupted logit distribution rather than a chat-template problem.

#### Acceptance metrics (DSpark set)

Cumulative over the four runs, so contaminated by the degenerate ones — but the shape is clear:

| metric | this box | your nst=5 reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| avg draft acceptance | **7.34%** (2278/31020) | 22.9–23.8% |
| position 0 | **0.178** (1104/6204) | 0.41–0.68 |
| mean acceptance length | **1.37** | 2.15–2.23 |
| draft tokens per draft | 5.00 | 5 (nst floor honoured) |

Close to @kelnei's collapse figures (0.181 / 1.31 / 4.4%), but at **nst=5**, where the validator's equality rule is satisfied.

#### What I've ruled out

- **DSpark** — reproduces 4/4 with `--speculative-config` removed.
- **Prefix caching** — reproduces with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`; in fact the earliest corruption (15,703) was observed with caching *off*.
- **Eager scratch pool** — `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_EAGER_SCRATCH_POOL=0` throughout.
- **Draft-forward cudagraph TP hatch** — `VLLM_DSPARK_FORWARD_CUDAGRAPH_ALLOW_TP=0` throughout.
- **FlashInfer sampler** — not enabled.
- **`--async-scheduling`** — not passed.
- **#50686 / chat template** — fix present in the installed package, and a plain single-turn prompt with no tools and no assistant-turn history corrupts as well.
- **The RoCE fabric** — both links ACTIVE and in use by NCCL; byte counters mirror *exactly* across nodes (878,124,571,144 xmit on one = rcv on the other, and likewise for the second link, over ~1.7 TB each way); zero `port_rcv_errors`, discards, and zero RoCE retransmit/ordering counters (`packet_seq_err`, `out_of_sequence`, `local_ack_timeout_err`, `rnr_nak_retry_err`).

#### What I could not test

- **TP=1 control** — the 0731 checkpoint is 156 GB and does not fit one 128 GB GB10; EngineCore is killed by signal during weight load.
- **bf16 KV control** — blocked by design:
  `AssertionError: DeepseekV4 fp8_ds_mla layout only supports fp8 kv-cache, got auto`

#### One config oddity

`--block-size 256` is passed and visible in the process command line, but `vllm:cache_config_info` reports `block_size="4"` with `user_specified_block_size="True"` and `sliding_window="128"` (`num_gpu_blocks=17903`, `kv_cache_size_tokens=1394221`). Possibly unrelated, but I don't know how to read it.

---

Everything above came out of one capture script (provenance, engine config, metrics, raw repro with leak counts and verbatim output). Happy to run it against any patch, env var, or configuration you want tested on this hardware — including instrumented builds.

### The one env var I would drop first: `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1`

DeepGEMM's SM120 support lives in the [`nv_dev`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/tree/nv_dev) branch and has to be built manually. Unless you did that, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1` will not give you DeepGEMM kernels — but `_E8M0=1` still changes how block scales are prepared. That combination puts E8M0 scales on the **Triton** block-scaled MM path, which is the only subclass that opts into a change merged *into this very tag*: PR #38's `prefers_fp32_block_scale`, which caches an fp32 copy of the block scale at load time and deliberately leaves the E8M0 original in place because other consumers (DSv4's fused `o_proj`, the DSpark kernels) read `layer.weight_scale{,_inv}` directly.

Because our gates set no DeepGEMM env, the scales are never `float8_e8m0fnu`, the guard `scale.dtype != e8m0` returns early, and that code path **never executes in any test we run**. We have zero coverage of it, and your configuration is the one that activates it. That makes it the highest-value single flag to remove.

Second on the list is `--enable-flashinfer-autotune`: the tactic it selects is not logged, and we are separately chasing a per-serve nondeterminism we suspect it for.

### One observation on your own numbers

Corruption at 15,703 but clean at 25,506, and 1-of-3 coherent at 33,175, is weakly length-correlated at best. That reads less like a long-context path and more like something that varies **per token** — MoE expert routing is the obvious candidate, and it fits a bad block scale on a subset of experts: same request, different routing, different outcome. Worth keeping in mind before assuming the sparse-MLA path.

### Your "config oddity" may be a real second bug

`num_gpu_blocks=17903` with `kv_cache_size_tokens=1394221` gives 77.9 tokens/block, which matches neither the reported `block_size=4` nor the 256 you passed. Those three numbers are mutually inconsistent whatever the true block size is, so that is worth its own issue regardless of how the corruption resolves.

Happy to run any patch or configuration on our 4× GB10 side to compare against yours.

#### 1. Clean now — at 85k context, with the original KV layout, ceiling and memory target

Two consecutive review rounds through our agent harness, on the same tag:

| | run A | run B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| max context reached | 87,568 | **84,810** |
| input / output tokens | 330,356 / 5,802 | **978,865 / 21,449** |
| status | completed | completed |
| leaked special tokens (whole event stream) | **0** | **0** |
| output quality | coherent | coherent |

Run B is the important one: it runs **`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `--max-model-len 500000`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`** — i.e. the exact settings from the corrupting config — and it is clean at 84.8k tokens, which is 2.5× the context where corruption used to be routine. The output stays coherent and on-task at that depth.

**So we were both wrong about the likely candidates.** KV layout (`fp8_ds_mla`), the 500k context ceiling, and the 0.85 memory target are all exonerated. Your instinct that this is per-token rather than long-context looks better supported than my sparse-MLA theory.

#### 2. Your gate config does not run on 2× GB10 — TileLang JIT inside `execute_model`, then OOM

Two attempts, both dead within minutes: `Worker proc VllmWorker-0 died unexpectedly (exit code: None)` — signal death, no Python exception, no CUDA error. The worker was killed inside `tilelang/contrib/nvcc.py:189 compile_cuda → proc.communicate()`, i.e. **compiling kernels during a forward pass**: 41 TileLang compiles in the first attempt, 20 in the second, all `mhc_*`, all during serving rather than warmup. `Running: 1 reqs` throughout — concurrency was not involved.

The cause is memory, and it is a TP-shape effect rather than a config error:

```
Free memory on device (110.19/121.63 GiB) at startup
weights + non-torch  80.71 GiB
peak activation       1.95 GiB
CUDA graphs           1.83 GiB
KV cache             20.70 GiB
                    -----------
                    105.19 GiB   → ~5 GiB left for nvcc/TileLang
```

At TP=2 each node carries ~80.7 GiB of weights; at your TP=4 it is ~40 GiB. Same `gpu_memory_utilization: 0.85`, very different absolute headroom. `journalctl -k` confirms it: **95 `NVRM ... Out of memory [NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY] from _memdescAllocInternal`** events in the 30 minutes around the crash. (Note for anyone else reproducing: on these boxes `dmesg_restrict=1`, so `dmesg` shows nothing without root — we initially and wrongly concluded there was no OOM. `journalctl -k` is readable.)

What fixed it was **`--load-format instanttensor`**; `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` alone was not enough. Worth considering whether the D512 split-prefill warmup covers the `mhc_*` kernel shapes — the compiles we saw were clearly not pre-compiled.

#### 3. What is left — the narrowed suspect list

Everything below is present in the corrupting config and absent from the clean one. Dropping settings that merely restate this build's defaults, the real remaining differences are:

| difference | note |
| --- | --- |
| `VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE=1` | non-default; our leading suspect, and the same Triton block-scaled path your E8M0 mechanism describes |
| `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` pinned | clean config lets it auto-select |
| `--enable-flashinfer-autotune` | your second suspect |
| `--no-enable-prefix-caching` | clean config has caching **on** |
| `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0` | reduces the effective memory margin |
| `--max-num-seqs 4` → `64`, DSpark now **on** | |

Note: `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM`, `VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM` and `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0` all default to `1` in this build, so they are still active in the clean config above and are **not** among the differences — dropping them from our recipe changed nothing.

We can bisect these one at a time on our side — each test is one restart plus a review round to ~85k context. Order we would use unless you prefer otherwise: `VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE=1`, then `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0` (explicitly, since the default is on), then the pinned attention backend, then `--enable-flashinfer-autotune`.

- jasl · comment · 2026-08-05T09:14:07Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5189910484)

@wagzee Following up on section 2 of your report (TileLang JIT inside `execute_model`, then OOM) — root-caused and fixed.

**Root cause.** The DSv4 mHC TileLang warmup that should compile these kernels at startup gates on `hc_pre`/`hc_post` layer attributes that only the AMD/XPU layer classes expose. The NVIDIA layer never has them, so on every CUDA build the warmup silently no-ops, and the mHC kernels JIT-compile inside the first forward pass that hits each new shape bucket — an nvcc subprocess spawned mid-inference. A cold TileLang cache (i.e. every fresh install) hits this on its first real traffic; a warm `~/.tilelang` never does, which is why long-serving boxes (ours) never reproduced it and your fresh 2-node did.

**Why it presents as a TP-shape effect.** The nvcc spike needs memory headroom in the GB10's unified pool. At TP=2 each node carries ~80.7 GiB of weights, leaving the ~5 GiB you measured — the spike kills the worker exactly as you observed (signal death, no Python exception, NVRM OOM in `journalctl`). At TP=4 the same spike lands in ~45 GiB of headroom and passes unnoticed. Your `--load-format instanttensor` result is consistent with this: it does not remove the JIT, it leaves enough headroom to survive it — a workaround, not a fix.

**Quantified on a cold cache** (2-node TP=2, 12-shape probe load): 18 mid-serving TileLang compiles, all of them the two mHC prenorm kernels recompiling per `n_splits` bucket (the compile key is `(n_splits, tile_n)`; `num_tokens` is a dynamic dim, so one cubin serves a whole bucket of batch shapes — agentic traffic with diverse shapes walks the whole staircase, which is why your workload hit it repeatedly).

**Fix** — commit `4eedf48765` on the PR branch: the warmup now gates on config alone (any CUDA DSv4 serve) and drives one dummy forward per distinct compile key, skipping keys cudagraph capture already owns. Acceptance on a cold cache, identical probe load, cross-node-verified identical trees: **18 → 0** mid-serving compiles, at +81 s of startup (11 dummy runs, ~11% of total boot). First boot per install now pays the TileLang compile at startup instead of inside your requests, which is the intended trade.

After this lands, `--load-format instanttensor` should no longer be needed for this failure mode (keeping it is harmless).

Ran your acceptance condition on the hardware that reported it. Result: the fix
works, and `--load-format instanttensor` is indeed no longer needed.

Also answering your `deep_gemm` question, and one finding about cache
persistence that makes the blast radius larger than "first boot per install".

#### 1. `import deep_gemm._C` — fails on our nodes too, for a different reason

```
$ docker run --rm --entrypoint python3 <image> -c "import deep_gemm"

```

The package is **not installed at all** in our image, so `._C` cannot import
either. Verified on both nodes, and re-verified on the rebuilt image. So our MoE
is not running DeepGEMM kernels — the difference you were worried about does not
exist. Worth noting the asymmetry: yours has the package with a torch-ABI-broken
`._C`, ours has no package. Same net effect, different mechanism.

#### 2. Validation of `4eedf48765`

Build: `20260805.dev1+g4eedf4876.d20260805`, verified identical on both nodes.
Config: our working recipe **minus `--load-format instanttensor`**, i.e. the same
shape that died twice on `0f59188db1`. `fp8_ds_mla`, `--max-model-len 500000`,
`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, DSpark nst=5, prefix caching on, TP=2.

| | `0f59188db1` (before) | `4eedf48765` (after) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TileLang compiles at startup | 0 | **27 + 27** (both nodes) |
| **compiles during serving** | **41, then 20** | **0 + 0** |
| NVRM `NO_MEMORY` after serve-ready | many | **0** |
| outcome | worker killed at ~5 min, twice | **~96 min, 0 restarts** |
| `--load-format instanttensor` | required to survive | **not needed** |

Workload was a real multi-turn tool-calling agent pipeline, not a synthetic
probe: **46 request sequences, all completed**, mixing short tool-result turns
with long generation turns, up to 1.46M cumulative input tokens in a single
sequence. Peak prompt throughput 4,835 tok/s, KV usage to 47%, prefix-cache hit
rate 89.6%. One sequence walked prompt sizes upward in ~4,500-token steps from
17,929 to 95,909 — the `(n_splits, tile_n)` staircase you described — and
produced **zero** new compiles.

One nuance worth recording: the nvcc memory spike did not disappear, it **moved**.
`journalctl -k` shows 34 `NVRM ... NO_MEMORY` events during the startup warmup
(before serve-ready), and **none** after. At TP=2 the spike still exceeds available
headroom, but at startup the process survives it; mid-forward it killed a worker.
That is also why `instanttensor` is no longer needed — it was buying headroom for a
collision that no longer happens during requests.

#### 3. The cache never persists in a containerized deployment — this hits every restart

You attributed our reproduction to a fresh install versus your warm `~/.tilelang`.
On our setup it is stronger than that:

- no `~/.tilelang` baked into the image
- `~/.tilelang` on both hosts is empty (4.0K)
- it is **not mounted** into the container — the cache lives inside the container
  filesystem and dies with it

So every `sparkrun run` starts cold by construction, and the pre-fix bug hit **every
restart**, not just the first boot per install. Empirically confirmed: 27 kernels
compiled at startup on this boot, which a warm cache would have skipped.

That makes the fix considerably more valuable for anyone running vLLM in
containers without a mounted TileLang cache — which we suspect is most people
using the Docker path. It may be worth either mentioning a cache mount in the
published config, or noting that the startup cost is per-container rather than
per-install.

#### 4. `block_size` filed separately

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51163 — it reproduces on this build
too, with different numbers: `--block-size 256` passed,
`block_size="4"` reported, `num_gpu_blocks=20377`, `kv_cache_size_tokens=1179770`
→ 57.9 tokens/block (previously 77.9). Two builds, two configs, same contradiction.

- jasl · comment · 2026-08-05T15:34:18Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5193853778)

@allenh1 Thanks — and the bisect boundary you gave is the answer. `1a2e0390` (07-27) sits immediately before the DSv4 eager scratch pool landed, and that pool ran **unconditionally, with no env switch**, from 07-31 11:45 (`df71917cf1`, upstream #49236) until 08-04 04:11.

Symptoms in that window, independently reported by @tobymao with a clean bisect (TP=4, DSpark, long context): leaked BOS tokens mid-sentence, multilingual token salad in English text, terminal single-token repetition — under concurrent mixed prefill+decode, with speculative decoding on *or* off. That matches your description, and your "revert to 1a2e0390" lands exactly on the other side of the pool's introduction.

Two defects, both confirmed in our tree rather than taken on report:

1. **Cross-template aliasing.** The aux scratch was sized with `max()` across the FP4-indexer, global-topk and compressor families while `_views()` carved all three from offset 0, so they aliased the same bytes. The justification was temporal disjointness, which the attention eager break invalidates by running the indexer and compressor on parallel aux streams. Fixed 08-04 (`sum()` sizing, explicit per-family base offsets).

2. **Cross-layer reuse.** Each template is shared by all 43 layers keyed only by `num_tokens`, so layer N's consumer can read while layer N+1 writes. tobymao still saw 1 corrupt round in 2 with fix 1 applied. Making it safe needs per-layer buffers or stream-ordering events; instead the pool became opt-in (`VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_EAGER_SCRATCH_POOL=1`) and **defaults off**, which is what the branch has shipped since 08-04.

So current tip should be clean for you without carrying patches for this — and your own rebase carrying both pool commits is consistent with your outputs being correct again.

Separately, I went through your branch commit by commit against ours. Two things worth flagging:

**Your `e384f93761` (DSpark shared-expert pad guard) is right about the defect but the fix doesn't fully close it.** DSpark builds `DeepseekV4MoE` with the default `use_sequence_parallel=False` — in your tree too — so aligning the loader's guard to `_use_sequence_parallel(vllm_config)` still diverges under `mega_moe + EP + tp>1 + dp==1`, where that helper returns True and padding is skipped for a layer that expects it padded. The invariant is "match what this MoE was constructed with", not "match the target model", so I tied both sites to one constant instead. Worth noting for anyone reading either branch: it is only reachable at `dp>1` with a listed all2all backend, so at dp=1 both the old and new guards pad identically — neither version explains your garble.

**Your `96ae58781d` hunk 2 (SWA vs indexer short-extend tiering) reproduces in our tree and I have not fixed it yet.** Our indexer passes `treat_short_extends_as_decodes=not has_prefilling_rows and not self.use_pcp` while the SWA builder takes the default `True`, so a short extend in a mixed batch is tiered prefill by one and decode by the other, and they share `topk_indices_buffer` through a boundary index. Aligning only `sparse_swa.py` would desynchronize it from the C128A builder in `sparse_mla.py`, whose comment mandates it match SWA's split and whose decode rows use global rather than local coordinates — so this needs all the consumers moved together, plus a mixed-batch regression gate, which I would rather land with a reproduction than blind.

On upstreaming: agreed, and thank you for framing your rebase that way. If you are up for it, the cleanest split is probably the datacenter-guard removals and other model-agnostic pieces going up first, with the SM12x-specific activations following behind them.

One request, since we just got burned by this ourselves: could you confirm the exact commit your garbled build was at, and that every node in your cluster was serving the same one? We found our own four nodes sitting at three different SHAs yesterday — each rank imports vLLM from its own filesystem and nothing in the launch path checks. Our start script now fingerprints every node's tree and refuses to launch on a mismatch.

Status: we merged upstream/main this evening and the full gate campaign is running now (ETA 2-3 h). It has a **TP=4 + DSpark coherence arm added specifically because of your report** — every TP=4 run we did today used llama-benchy `--skip-coherence`, which measures throughput and is structurally blind to garbled output, so our own gates could not have caught what you hit. Unit suite is already green (1317 passed; the one failure needs two GPUs in a single node, which a GB10 does not have). I will post the results either way.

So this looks like a *second*, spec-decode-specific path that survives the scratch-pool fix. Built from tag `20260804`; both nodes on `vllm 20260805.dev0+g0f59188db`, `flashinfer 0.6.15.post1` (python+cubin), `torch 2.13.0`. Eager scratch pool confirmed **off** by default (`envs.VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_EAGER_SCRATCH_POOL=False`).

**Serve config (the corrupting one).**
```
--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --max-model-len 262144
--max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.89
--tensor-parallel-size 2 --distributed-executor-backend ray
--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4
--tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice
--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}'
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'
```

**Repro.** 20 concurrent requests (max_workers=20 into `--max-num-seqs 4`), mixing prefill-heavy (single-sentence summary over a ~70K-token log) and decode-heavy (~700-word essays). Scan each response's `content` and `reasoning_content` for `<｜…｜>`.

**Result — single variable is MTP:**

| config | leak in `content` (user-visible) | leak in `reasoning` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MTP on, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=1` | **9/20** | 14/20 |
| MTP on, sampler **off** | **9/20** | 11/20 |
| **MTP off** (no `--speculative-config`) | **0/20** | **0/20** |

Idle / single-stream is clean regardless (needle-in-haystack 5/5 exact @ ~71K, tool-calling 8/8, instruction+math 7/7). It requires concurrency to trigger.

**Signature.** A spurious `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` appears mid-stream, after which the continuation degrades — often language-mixed:
```
<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜># Summary
<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>厦门 mainte…

<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>package m…

- jasl · comment · 2026-08-05T16:32:25Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5194509947)

@brianmiller Quick heads-up before you spend a run on it: **`-0731` does not ship MTP weights**, so `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` against it will not be the controlled comparison you want.

From the `-0731` weight index (`model.safetensors.index.json`):

```
top-level prefixes : embed, layers(0..42), norm, head, mtp(4705 tensors)
mtp sub-modules    : mtp.0 (1568), mtp.1 (1565), mtp.2 (1572)
mtp.2.markov_head.markov_w1 / markov_w2
eh_proj / enorm / hnorm : 0 / 0 / 0
config             : dspark_block_size = 5, dspark_target_layer_ids, dspark_markov_rank
```

The `mtp.` prefix on `-0731` is a **storage location holding a three-block DSpark drafter with a Markov head**, not a DeepSeek MTP module — none of the MTP-hallmark tensors (`enorm`/`hnorm`) exist. Compare `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4`, which is derived from the base checkpoint you are on: one `mtp` block (1575 tensors), `enorm` 1, `hnorm` 1, no markov head, no `dspark_block_size`. That one has real MTP; `-0731` does not.

Worth noting that our loader remaps `mtp.{i}.*` by prefix, so `method=mtp` on `-0731` is liable to half-load DSpark blocks rather than fail cleanly. If you do run it, treat any result as uninterpretable rather than as evidence about your BOS leak — and if it boots at all, that is a validation gap on our side that we should close (a checkpoint without MTP tensors should refuse `method=mtp` at startup, not limp).

So the clean matrix for your repro is:
- your base checkpoint + MTP=2 — the failing case you already have
- `-0731` + **DSpark** (`{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}`) — what we and @allenh1 run
- `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4` + MTP=2 — your architecture, current weights, if you want to separate "old MTP tensors" from "MTP code path"

We have that last one cached and are setting up your 20-way concurrent mixed prefill+decode repro against it now, since it is the configuration that can actually reproduce your report on our hardware. Will post what we see either way.

One gap your report exposed on our side regardless of outcome: our coherence gate scores replacement characters, script mixing and degenerate repetition — it does **not** look for leaked special tokens, so a mid-stream `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` followed by fluent English scores as coherent. We are adding that check; thank you for the precise signature.


- tobymao · comment · 2026-08-05T16:51:41Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5194708694)

### Same BOS-leak signature on 4× GB10 / TP=4 — but **spec-decode-off does NOT fix it here**

@brianmiller our symptom is byte-for-byte yours (spurious `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` mid-stream, language-mixed continuation, concurrency-only, clean single-stream). Our config differs in two ways that matter: **4× GB10 TP=4** over RoCE, and **DSpark** (`{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}`) rather than MTP, on `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260802c` (`72f5a301`).

**We cannot reproduce your MTP-off result.** Removing `--speculative-config` entirely — verified off by the absence of `vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total` on `/metrics`, not just by config — still corrupts: **round 4 of 12**, `leaked_specials=8070`, onset ~47k chars. So on this config the draft/verify path is not the trigger. Either there are two distinct faults, or the common cause sits upstream of spec-decode.

**Three corrections to our own earlier reports in this thread, all of which we got wrong:**

1. **The 128 MB pre-attention flush never executed.** `VLLM_DSV4_ZERO_WORKSPACE`/`VLLM_DSV4_FLUSH_MB` gate code in `_get_flashinfer_dsv4_workspace()`, which is dead on this build — `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE`/`..._PREFILL` both default `True` and route through `flashinfer_sm120_decode.py`, which takes scratch from the workspace manager instead. Our "9/9 clean" measured an inert knob, and the 128 MB-vs-1 MB result that we offered as evidence for an L2/stale-line story is **no evidence** — neither arm ran.
2. **The image is not the cause.** The pre-upgrade `20260731` build corrupts identically on the same kernel/driver (2/2 rounds, incl. 16,000 tokens of U+2060 word-joiner). Rolling back the image is not a mitigation.
3. **There is no context threshold.** We reported one; it was underpowered sampling. 62,030 prompt tokens corrupts (4 clean reps then a corrupt 5th) while 68,497 ran 5/5 clean.

**The measurement that invalidates most short eliminations, including several of ours:** the true rate is **~10% per battery round**, not the 25–50% we assumed. Two clean rounds miss corruption 81% of the time; five miss it 59%. Any "tested, still corrupt" entry resting on 2–3 rounds carries almost no information.

**Eliminated here on genuine corrupt rounds, each with a liveness heartbeat proving the probe executed** (several earlier probes were silently inert): sparse index validity (slots always inside the requesting token's own block table), `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache` determinism, compressor store determinism at **both** `head_dim=128` and `512`, KV-cache stability between writes, query rope+quant determinism, MoE (differs only at ~1 ULP bf16 — reduction-order noise, not a miscompute), TP all-reduce convergence (all 4 ranks bit-identical), residual-stream finiteness (no NaN/Inf/overflow through corruption), RMSNorm, **both sampler backends** (FlashInfer `forward_cuda` and native — `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` still corrupts), and the **eager scratch pool** (gated off explicitly; corrupt round 1 — note the pool is unconditional in `72f5a301`, `b1ef3033f4` is not in it). Swapping the entire attention implementation (sm120 → FlashMLA/Triton) also changed nothing.

**On the eager scratch pool (@jasl's cross-layer-reuse diagnosis).** It fits our data better than anything we tested — a consumer reading layer N's template while layer N+1 writes is byte-stable at every instant, so it is invisible to every determinism/sentinel check by construction, needs concurrency, and sits upstream of everything above. Two caveats from our side, offered as data rather than argument: (a) we ran with the pool explicitly disabled (patched `eager_scratch_pool = None` in `nvidia/model.py`, confirmed by a log line, since `b1ef3033f4`'s switch is not in `72f5a301`) and **still corrupted in round 1** — our patch may simply not have disabled every consumer, but we could not clear it that way; (b) our pin `72f5a301` (20260802c) and the `-0731` tag both sit inside the 07-31 → 08-04 unconditional-pool window, which is consistent with both corrupting identically.

**The methodological caveat we'd flag for anyone bisecting this:** every check above tests **determinism**, not **correctness**. A deterministically-wrong forward pass passes all of them. The instrument we have not built is a per-layer reference diff across two temperature-0 runs on identical input, to find the first layer that diverges — that's where we'd go next.

Repro harness (single file, no deps): the `dsv4_corruption_repro.py` posted earlier still reproduces. One caveat that cost us a false verdict: if you feed it a repo snapshot, **exclude the harness itself** — its source contains the literal special-token vectors the detector greps for, so a model asked to write tests quotes them back and a clean run scores CORRUPT.

- jasl · comment · 2026-08-05T20:29:48Z · [source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834#issuecomment-5196985793)

@tobymao That rebuild is the useful kind of negative result — thank you for running it, and for retracting the retraction. Agreed: the pool is not your cause.

**There is a variable that separates your config from @allenh1's, and it is your own patch.**

@allenh1 reports 4× GB10 / TP=4 / DSpark clean after his patches; you report the same topology, same drafter, corrupt on `0f59188db`. The difference is not build date — it is that his tree carries the short-extend tiering fix and `0f59188db` does not:

```
allenh1/vllm@96ae58781d  touches sparse_swa.py — SWA and indexer tier short extends alike
0f59188db1               grep -c treat_short_extends_as_decodes  sparse_swa.py -> 0
ds4-sm120-preview-dev    after merging your #40                            -> 1
```

His version aligns SWA to the indexer; yours covers all three builders including C128A. So on the two configs where anyone has actually reproduced this — yours and his — presence of that fix tracks the outcome exactly.

That makes the arm worth running the one you have not: **your own PR under your repro**. It is merged as `b2bdfc7d31` on `ds4-sm120-preview-dev`. Since you offered — that is the arm I would ask for, because you have the only 4× GB10 + DSpark reproduction anyone has, and we would be guessing at 2 nodes.

Two things I verified before merging that bear on how you read a result:

**The alignment direction is forced, not a preference.** The indexer lays the buffer out as `[decode rows | prefill rows]` using its own split — its decode path writes from row 0 (`sparse_attn_indexer.py:674`) while its prefill path writes by absolute token range (`:525`). The C4A consumer then reads decode rows as *local* coordinates against prefill's global (`flashinfer_sparse.py:347`). So a boundary disagreement is not only row misattribution, it is a coordinate-space misread on top — consumers must adopt the producer's split, and aligning the other way would have added a second fault.

**A second divergence axis is still open and is DSpark-specific**, which is why I would not expect this patch alone to be the whole story for you: the indexer's `decode_threshold` is `num_speculative_tokens + 1` while sparse-SWA and C128A use `1 + (2 if parallel_drafting else 1) * num_speculative_tokens`. At your `num_speculative_tokens=5` that is **6 against 11**, so any row whose query length lands in (6, 11] is tiered prefill by the producer and decode by both consumers — the same misattribution, no short extend required, and it vanishes without parallel drafting. There is a test pinning that arithmetic on the merged branch; it is deliberately not a fix, because those thresholds may encode real kernel limits (paged-MQA `next_n` vs flashmla's spec-as-decode range) and forcing them equal could trade one fault for another. If your run still corrupts with the merged patch, that axis is where I would look next, and it would be worth trying `parallel_drafting` off as a diagnostic since it collapses 1+2k to 1+k.

I also strengthened the gate on your PR before merging (`Co-authored-by:` you): the original compared one helper against itself at a fixed `threshold=1`, so it reported `3 passed` against a tree where none of the three builders were touched. It now inspects the call sites and fails on unfixed sources. Not a knock on the mechanism — but it is the same underpowered-elimination trap you flagged in the thread, in test form, and hardcoding `threshold=1` for all three is exactly what hid the axis above.

On your per-layer instrument: worth noting two temperature-0 runs under *identical* conditions is still a determinism test, and a deterministically-wrong pass agrees with itself. The asymmetry you have already established is more useful as an oracle — single-stream is clean, concurrent corrupts — so diffing a request's per-layer activations **run alone versus run inside a concurrent batch** tests correctness rather than reproducibility. It needs a noise floor from clean co-batched rounds first, since batching legitimately perturbs reduction order at the ~1 ULP level you measured.

The check that costs nothing and is structurally impossible in valid output:

```

I would treat repeated `<ds_safety>` as a secondary signal rather than a primary one.
